AT&T and Corning Team Up to Engineer the Connected World with Fiber 
AT&T and Corning Team Up to Engineer the Connected World with Fiber 
Dallas, TX and Corning, NY | Corning Incorporated | September 29, 2026 
The more than $3 billion agreement solidifies AT&T’s commitment to bring the best and fastest connection to more Americans as internet use and AI continue to drive demand 
Key Takeaways: 
AT&T and Corning entered into a multi-year agreement to supply the fiber and cable AT&T needs to bring fast, reliable internet to more Americans as demand grows.
Fiber is the gold standard for home internet. AT&T Fiber can deliver speeds 3x faster than satellite 1 services and the capacity to handle how people stream, work, game, video chat, create and use AI today, with room for whatever comes next.
AT&T’s powerful combination of fiber and wireless makes connectivity simple for customers at home, at work and on the go. Satellite will complement those networks by helping extend connectivity in roughly 2% of remote areas where fiber and wireless may not be available.
This agreement supports the American economy by building on AT&T’s investments in critical connectivity infrastructure and its fully unionized frontline workforce, along with Corning’s extensive U.S. advanced manufacturing operations and American-made products. 
What it is: AT&T (NYSE: T) and Corning Incorporated (NYSE: GLW) entered into a multi-year agreement valued at more than $3 billion. Corning will supply the fiber and cable AT&T needs to expand its network and bring fast, reliable internet to more Americans as AI drives growing data demand. 
Why it Matters: Americans are using more data than ever. The average AT&T Fiber household now uses more than 1 terabyte each month, 5x more than in 2016. And that number is expected to keep climbing. As streaming, gaming, video calls, cloud services and AI become a bigger part of everyday life, monthly use is expected to reach 2 to 2.5 terabytes by 2030.
Why Fiber: Fiber is the only technology that can meet the growing demand for data. It can quickly and reliably carry everything from video calls and movie streaming to business applications, AI tools, live camera footage, and near real-time information. That gives families, businesses and communities the speed and capacity they need today, with room for whatever comes next. 
AT&T Connects You Always and All Ways: With America’s largest wireless 2 and fiber networks, AT&T is uniquely positioned to keep people connected across all 50 states and around the world. Fiber provides the high-capacity foundation connecting homes, businesses and communities, while wireless keeps people connected as they move through their day. Satellite complements those networks by extending connectivity to remote, hard-to-reach areas. Together, these technologies help create the seamless connectivity experience customers increasingly expect. 
Deal to Connect America: This deal with Corning helps AT&T deliver on its commitment to bring fast, reliable internet to 60 million Americans by the end of 2030. This means more access to the connectivity they need today, tomorrow, and for generations to come. Corning’s solutions help AT&T accelerate network deployment and improve installation efficiency at scale. 
“Fiber remains the gold standard for superior internet connectivity, and AT&T is the nation’s leader in fiber,” said John Stankey, Chairman and CEO of AT&T. “Fiber’s speed, reliability and capacity remain unmatched for any home or business. We deeply value our long and successful relationship with Corning and look forward to continuing our work together as we expand the nation’s largest fiber network and make the long-term investments needed to keep America connected
Investing in American Infrastructure: The collaboration builds on both companies’ U.S. investments. For the 150th anniversary of the first phone call, AT&T committed more than $250 billion over five years to strengthen U.S. connectivity infrastructure. 
As it celebrates its 175th anniversary, Corning continues to expand its U.S. fiber and cable manufacturing, including at North Carolina facilities that have created hundreds of jobs. 
“Corning and AT&T have worked side by side for generations to connect people across this country, and this agreement is the next chapter in that partnership,” said Wendell Weeks, Chairman, CEO, and President of Corning. “By pairing our large, U.S.-based advanced manufacturing with AT&T's network leadership, we can keep co-innovating to build the dense fiber networks that will drive the future of connectivity—while sustaining thousands of highly skilled American jobs and strengthening domestic supply chains.”
The agreement unites these investments: Corning’s U.S. workforce produces the fiber, while AT&T technicians—the industry’s largest union-represented workforce—build and maintain networks connecting homes, businesses and communities nationwide. These jobs provide American families with competitive pay, benefits, wellness programs and long-term financial security.
Together, the companies strengthen the domestic supply chain and support skilled U.S. manufacturing and network jobs.
AT&T reiterates the financial outlook and capital allocation plan provided in its second-quarter 2026 earnings release , which reflects the financial impact of this agreement and AT&T’s commitment to expand and strengthen U.S. connectivity infrastructure.
AT&T and Corning are helping more Americans connect when it matters most—at home, at work and on the go.
About AT&T
We help more than 100 million U.S. families, friends and neighbors, plus nearly 2.5 million businesses, connect to greater possibility. From the first phone call 150 years ago to our 5G wireless and multi-gig internet offerings today, we @ATT innovate to improve lives. For more information about AT&T Inc. ( NYSE:T ), please visit us at about.att.com . Investors can learn more at investors.att.com .
About Corning Incorporated 
Corning ( www.corning.com ) is one of the world’s leading innovators in materials science, with a 175-year track record of life-changing inventions. Corning applies its unparalleled expertise in glass science, ceramic science, and optical physics, along with its deep manufacturing and engineering capabilities to develop category-defining products that transform industries and enhance people’s lives. Corning succeeds through sustained investment in RD&E, a unique combination of material and process innovation, and deep, trust-based relationships with customers who are global leaders in their industries. Corning’s capabilities are versatile and synergistic, which allows the company to evolve to meet changing market needs, while also helping its customers capture new opportunities in dynamic industries. Today, Corning’s markets include optical communications, mobile consumer electronics, display, automotive, solar, semiconductors, and life sciences.

title: Infineon extends collaboration with SolarEdge to enable
query: https://www.infineon.com/en.sitemap.row-sitemap.xml
content_text:
Infineon extends collaboration with SolarEdge to enable solid-state protection for 800 VDC AI data centers
Business & Financial Press
Sep 09, 2026 
Companies extend collaboration into solid-state circuit breaker (SSCB) technology in line with leading industry framework for 800 Volts direct current (VDC) architecture 
SSCB technology is designed to interrupt DC faults orders of magnitude faster than electromechanical breakers, addressing one of the key challenges in deploying high-voltage DC power architectures 
The collaboration advances a DC-native power architecture from medium-voltage grid connection through distribution to the rack, to support higher density, greater reliability and reduced environmental impact for AI data centers 
Munich, Germany and Milpitas, California – 9 September, 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) and SolarEdge Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: SEDG), a global leader in smart energy, today announced an extension of their collaboration to advance solid-state circuit breaker (SSCB) technology for high-voltage DC distribution in AI and hyperscale data centers. The collaboration addresses a key challenge in the adoption of 800 VDC architecture: Safe operation of increasingly power-dense infrastructure requires a very fast fault-isolation to achieve selectivity while maintaining high efficiency.
Extending the collaboration to solid-state protection addresses a critical gap in the distribution layer between the solid-state transformer (SST) and the compute rack, advancing a comprehensive grid-to-rack solution. SolarEdge is leading the design of the SSCB solution, with Infineon providing its silicon carbide (SiC) JFET technology at the core of the protection devices.
As rapidly increasing AI compute density drives the industry toward higher-voltage DC distribution, solid-state circuit breakers address one of the most fundamental challenges in enabling safe and reliable operation. Unlike conventional alternating current (AC) systems, DC protection presents a different engineering challenge. Without a natural current zero, mechanical interruption faces challenges with arcing. It is comparatively slow, and as such requires a different approach to circuit protection than conventional AC systems. Solid-state circuit breakers are designed to interrupt faults within a few microseconds, with no mechanical contacts to separate, while Infineon's CoolSiC™ JFET devices deliver efficient operation and superior robustness. Together, these capabilities help protect high-value compute equipment and enable more compact, higher-density DC distribution designs.
The collaboration builds directly on SolarEdge's SST platform with Infineon SiC components, first announced in November 2025. The SST is designed to enable direct medium-voltage (13.8-34.5 kV) to 800-1500 VDC conversion at over 99 percent efficiency, collapsing multiple conversion stages into a single solution while reducing physical footprint. 
"High-density AI infrastructure at 800 VDC demands uncompromising efficiency and protection", said Shuki Nir, Chief Executive Officer of SolarEdge. "Solid-state protection will enable operators to achieve both, delivering ultra-fast and dependable fault isolation without sacrificing conversion performance. Infineon's silicon carbide technology is what makes it practical at scale."
"Today’s data infrastructures have become more vulnerable to electrical faults, thereby driving the demand for smarter, faster and more robust power distribution systems," said Andreas Weisl, Executive Vice President and Chief Sales Officer of Industrial & Infrastructure at Infineon. "By combining our advanced silicon carbide JFET technology with SolarEdge’s expertise in final power distribution, we are addressing these demands to ensure fast, safe and reliable operations in AI data centers."
Building on more than 15 years of leadership in DC-coupled power electronics, SolarEdge is developing an 800 VDC powertrain for AI factories, a DC-native chain that carries power from the medium-voltage grid connection through conversion, distribution and protection to the compute rack. Infineon's broad portfolio of silicon, silicon carbide and gallium nitride solutions provides that foundation, supporting the decarbonization of AI infrastructure through lower losses, reduced environmental impact, and improved total cost of ownership.
About SolarEdge

title: Infineon enters into agreement to sell NOR Flash and F
query: https://www.infineon.com/en.sitemap.row-sitemap.xml
content_text:
Infineon enters into agreement to sell NOR Flash and F-RAM business to Winbond and sharpens focus on core growth areas 
Business & Financial Press
Sep 16, 2026 
Transaction valued at $1.12 billion supports Infineon's strategic focus and profitable growth 
Transaction reflects the strong market position and value created by the NOR Flash and F-RAM business 
Infineon to retain portfolio of specialty memory solutions including SRAM, HYPERRAM™, nvSRAM and SONOS based radiation-hardened memory solutions 
Munich, Germany – 16 September 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement under which Winbond Electronics Corporation, a Taiwan-based global supplier of semiconductor memory solutions, will acquire Infineon’s NOR Flash and F-RAM business in an all-cash transaction valued at $1.12 billion on a cash and debt free basis. The business comprises a portfolio of NOR Flash memory as well as F-RAM products serving customers across automotive, industrial and infrastructure markets. Subject to obtaining the required regulatory approvals, the parties currently target closing the transaction in the second half of 2027.
“The transaction represents a highly compelling strategic outcome for all stakeholders,” said Peter Schiefer, President of Infineon’s Automotive Division. “It allows Infineon to further focus its portfolio and capital allocation on its core growth drivers. At the same time, it enables our NOR Flash and F-RAM business to unlock its full potential.”
Winbond is a leading provider with a focus on memory solutions which makes the company a good fit to unlock future growth possibilities for Infineon’s NOR Flash and F-RAM business. The combination of Winbond’s existing memory portfolio and Infineon’s NOR Flash and F-RAM business will provide customers with a broad and complementary portfolio of NOR Flash and F-RAM products. Winbond will operate the acquired business as a standalone entity with headquarters in Silicon Valley in the United States.
Infineon will continue to offer a portfolio of specialty memory solutions, including SRAM, HYPERRAM™, nvSRAM and SONOS based radiation-hardened memory solutions. These technologies remain an important part of Infineon's portfolio across automotive, industrial, infrastructure, aerospace and defense applications, including a strong product offering of high-reliability memory solutions for space missions.

Infineon Wins Integrated Communication Award 2026 for Integrated Communication Management 
Business & Financial Press
Sep 23, 2026 
Munich, Germany – 23 September 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG has been honored with the Integrated Communication Award 2026 in the category “Integrated Communication Management.” The award was presented on 22 September during the 19th German Brand Summit at the F.A.Z. Tower in Frankfurt am Main. Through this recognition, the F.A.Z. Institute and an expert jury acknowledge companies that consistently organize their communications strategically, from alignment with overarching business objectives and clear governance structures to technology-enabled processes and a collaborative communication culture.
“Strategic and integrated communication makes a decisive contribution to business success. We are pleased to receive this recognition,” said Florian Martens, Executive Vice President & Chief Communications Officer at Infineon. “In an increasingly complex communications landscape, we can only create impact by breaking down silos and addressing topics holistically. This award recognizes the progress our team has achieved together over the past several years. My sincere thanks go to all colleagues who have helped shape this journey.”
Infineon’s communications function operates within an integrated organization that brings together all communication disciplines, ranging from public affairs and corporate communications to marketing communications, regional communications, and communication services. Content is planned and managed across functions and channels, topic ownership is bundled, and communication activities are aligned with strategic objectives. Clear performance indicators are used to measure success. In this way, communications makes a significant and measurable contribution to Infineon’s corporate strategy and business performance.
The jury particularly recognized the holistic approach with which Infineon manages communications across the company: “What impressed us was the consistent way communication has been transformed into an integrated management system. Planning, processes, topic management, and measurement are systematically interconnected. Particularly noteworthy are the clear governance framework and the transparent management architecture, which create a traceable link between communication activities and business objectives.”
The Integrated Communication Award, presented by the F.A.Z. Institute, recognizes outstanding approaches to integrated communications. In the category “Integrated Communication Management,” Allianz, Bayer, GEA, and Merck were also nominated alongside Infineon. The jury comprises communications experts from both industry and academia and is chaired by Prof. Dr. Ansgar Zerfass of Leipzig University.

title: Infineon and Eaton leverage silicon carbide technology
query: https://www.infineon.com/en.sitemap.row-sitemap.xml
content_text:
Infineon and Eaton leverage silicon carbide technology to advance solid-state transformers for 800 VDC AI data center power architectures
Business & Financial Press
Sep 29, 2026 
Infineon and Eaton are partnering to drive solid-state transformer (SST) technology 
The collaboration addresses demand for more efficient power conversion solutions in AI data centers 
Infineon’s silicon carbide power devices help enhance efficiency, power density and system reliability of Eaton’s SST platform 
Munich, Germany – 29 September, 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) will deliver silicon carbide (SiC) power devices to Eaton, an intelligent power management company, for use in its medium-voltage solid-state transformer (MVSST) 2.0 platform designed for deployment across APAC. The collaboration helps increase the efficiency and reliability of the power conversion required to connect AI data centers to the electricity grid. It targets 800 Volts direct current (VDC) data center power distribution architectures.
The rapid expansion of AI data centers and rising power requirements are driving demand for more efficient ways to connect high-density computing infrastructure to the grid. At the same time, advances in medium-voltage DC distribution technologies are accelerating the need for next-generation power conversion solutions that can improve efficiency, power density, scalability and reliability.
"As energy demand from AI data centers and industrial applications continues to grow, the demand for efficient, reliable and sustainable power conversion is increasing," said Andreas Weisl, Executive Vice President and Chief Sales Officer of Industrial & Infrastructure at Infineon. "By joining forces with Eaton, we aim to advance solid-state transformer technology and contribute to the development of a more scalable, efficient and sustainable infrastructure for powering the AI data centers of the future."
"Against the backdrop of rapidly increasing requirements for power efficiency, system reliability and scalability in AI data centers, our goal is to advance the development and adoption of SST technology. Thus, we aim to create greater value for data center and power grid operators as well as the renewable energy sector," said David Zheng, Vice President of R&D for Power Quality in APAC at Eaton. "Infineon’s advanced SiC technology is helping us accelerate the deployment of these next-generation power architectures." 
Designed for high-density computing infrastructures and emerging 800 VDC AI data center power distribution architectures, Eaton’s MVSST 2.0 platform reduces conversion stages compared with conventional architectures, improving efficiency, power density and deployment flexibility. As one of the first medium-voltage solid-state transformer platforms to achieve IEC certification, it combines advanced silicon carbide technology with Eaton's expertise in power distribution and conversion to support next-generation energy infrastructure. 
Looking ahead, Eaton and Infineon are exploring next-generation SST platforms based on 2.3 kV and 3.3 kV SiC power modules to support higher system voltages, greater efficiency and enhanced reliability for future AI data centers, grid modernization and renewable energy applications.

Annual report 2025
The fiscal year 2025 was marked by various challenges for Jenoptik, particularly from the semiconductor equipment and automotive markets. Nevertheless, we have continued to focus on our relevant growth potentials in our core markets of semiconductors, medical technology, metrology and smart mobility, and we look to the future with optimism thanks to our strong growth platforms. 
Overview over the fiscal year 2025
Jenoptik performed well overall in a challenging market environment in 2025.
Despite a 6 percent decline in revenue , we were able to maintain our profitability at a good level, with an EBITDA margin of 18.4 percent, thanks to cost reduction measures implemented early on.
We succeeded in further improving key balance sheet and financial ratios. The Group increased its equity ratio to around 60 percent, and free cash flow before interest and taxes rose by approximately 50 million euros.
The Executive Board and Supervisory Board will propose a dividend  payout of 0.40 euros per share to the Annual General Meeting.
The Group’s organizational structure has been realigned more closely with our growth areas of semiconductors, medical technology, metrology, and smart mobility.
With the opening of the new fab  for innovative micro-optics in Dresden, Germany, an important foundation was laid to realize further growth potential in this area.
Our approach to sustainability : As an “enabler,” we use our expertise and innovative products to make an important contribution to overcome social and climate challenges, enable customers worldwide to contribute more efficiently and sustainably to conserving resources and protecting the climate.
Outlook : We expect to return to a growth path in fiscal year 2026.

title: Finerenone showed consistent effects in reduction of UPCR, UACR and kidney function decline versus placebo in diverse patient populations with chronic kidney disease without diabetes

Finerenone showed consistent effects in reduction of UPCR, UACR and kidney function decline versus placebo in diverse patient populations with chronic kidney disease without diabetes
Not intended for U.S. and UK Media – Late-Breaking data presented at ASN Kidney Week 2026
Summary
New sub-analyses from the global FIND-CKD Phase III study show that finerenone provides kidney-protective benefits compared with placebo in subgroups of patients with chronic kidney disease without diabetes, reducing proteinuria and slowing kidney function decline / In patients with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), finerenone reduced albuminuria and proteinuria at month 12 by 40% and 41% respectively, and slowed the rate of eGFR decline over 32 months versus placebo / In patients with immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN), finerenone reduced proteinuria by 51% versus placebo, attenuated eGFR decline and also reduced established plasma and urine biomarkers of kidney injury / Finerenone is a selective, non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (nsMRA) that in five pivotal Phase III studies has demonstrated cardiovascular and/or kidney benefits across multiple patient populations with chronic kidney disease and/or heart failure
Berlin, October 22, 2026 – Bayer today announced results from two subgroup analyses from the Phase III FIND-CKD study, showing that finerenone provides consistent kidney-protective effects in diverse etiologies of chronic kidney disease (CKD) without diabetes, including focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) and IgA nephropathy (IgAN). 
“Patients living with FSGS and IgAN face a high risk of disease progression and kidney failure, underscoring the significant unmet need for new treatment options. Despite differences in the biological mechanisms underlying glomerular diseases, consistent, clinically meaningful reductions in proteinuria and a slower kidney function decline were observed with finerenone in both the IgAN and the FSGS subgroups. These findings further support the kidney-protective benefits of finerenone in CKD without diabetes,” said Dr. Christian Rommel, Global Head of Research and Development at Bayer’s Pharmaceuticals Division. “These findings provide important insights to slowing disease progression and improving long-term patient outcomes in CKD without diabetes.” 
Results in patients with Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis (FSGS): 
The FSGS subgroup in the FIND-CKD study included 215 patients, 50% of whom had primary and 50% secondary FSGS. Overall, finerenone preserved kidney function, lowered proteinuria (UPCR), and was well tolerated in the subgroup of patients with FSGS. Finerenone showed a statistically significant improvement in total estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) slope (mL/min/1.73 m 2 /year) over 32 months compared with placebo (between-group difference: 1.3 mL/min/1.73 m 2 /year [95% CI, 0.5-2.2; p 
Results in patients with immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN): 
In FIND-CKD, 416 out of overall 1584 patients had immunoglobulin A nephropathy. The effect of finerenone on total eGFR slope (mL/min/1.73 m 2 /year) over 32 months versus placebo was 0.63 (95% CI, 0.19-1.46] in participants with IgAN. From baseline to Month 12, finerenone reduced UPCR vs placebo by 51% (95% CI, 42–59). Finerenone was associated with a nearly 7-fold increase in the odds of achieving a UPCR of 
In both subgroup analyses, finerenone was well tolerated, with a safety profile consistent with that of the overall trial population, and the incidence of hyperkalemia leading to permanent discontinuation was low. 
Among the non-diabetic CKD patients included in FIND-CKD, approximately 60% had an underlying glomerular disease, around half of them had immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) or focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS). The results of the FSGS and IgAN subanalyses were presented today as late-breaking posters at the American Society of Nephrology’s (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 in Denver, Colorado. 
Approximately 850 million people worldwide have CKD. An estimated 50-70% of these patients have CKD without diabetes. Additionally, more than 3.5 million people with kidney failure are treated with dialysis, which is associated with a 5-year survival rate of about 40% after treatment initiation. CKD without diabetes can have a range of etiologies, of which the most common include kidney disease linked to hypertension and glomerulonephritis (including immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) or focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS)). Despite standard of care, patients with CKD without diabetes remain at risk of kidney failure and cardiovascular events. 
About Kerendia ™ / Firialta ™ (finerenone) 
Kerendia™ and Firialta™ are globally protected trademarks for finerenone. Finerenone is the first drug targeting the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) pathway that in five pivotal Phase III studies has demonstrated cardiovascular and/or kidney benefits across a broad range of patient populations, including patients with HF with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≥40%, patients with CKD associated with type 2 diabetes, patients with CKD associated with type 1 diabetes, and patients with CKD without diabetes. Finerenone is a selective, non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (nsMRA) that has been shown to block harmful effects of MR overactivation. MR overactivation contributes to CKD progression and cardiovascular damage which can be driven by metabolic, hemodynamic, or inflammatory and fibrotic factors. 
Since 2021, finerenone has been marketed as Kerendia™ or, in selected countries, as Firialta™, and has been approved for the treatment of adult patients with CKD associated with type 2 diabetes (T2D) in more than 100 countries worldwide, including in China, Europe, Japan, and the U.S. Finerenone is also approved for the treatment of heart failure with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≥ 40% in the U.S., the EU, Japan, and China among other Health Authorities, with additional applications under regulatory review. In the U.S., finerenone has recently been approved for the treatment of adult patients with CKD associated with type 1 diabetes. Applications for marketing authorization of finerenone in CKD without diabetes have been filed in China, Japan and the U.S., with further submissions underway. Finerenone is currently not approved for the treatment of CKD without diabetes. 
The clinical study program with finerenone, FINEOVATE, currently comprises twelve Phase III studies with dedicated programs in CKD and HF respectively. The THUNDERBALL CKD program consists of the completed Phase III studies FIDELIO-DKD, FIGARO-DKD, FIND-CKD, and FINE-ONE, and the Phase II study CONFIDENCE; as well as the ongoing Phase III studies in pediatric patient populations FIONA, and FIONA-OLE. The MOONRAKER program includes the completed pivotal Phase III study FINEARTS-HF, the ongoing investigator-sponsored, collaborative studies REDEFINE-HF, CONFIRMATION-HF, and FINALITY-HF, as well as the ongoing Phase III studies in pediatric patient populations, FIORE and FIORELLO. 
About FIND-CKD 
FIND-CKD is the largest Phase III study to date focused on CKD without diabetes. The study investigated finerenone in a broad patient population spanning different etiologies of CKD without diabetes, adding to the positive data and breadth of evidence of finerenone in CKD. FIND-CKD investigated the efficacy and safety of finerenone compared to placebo in addition to standard of care in more than 1,500 patients with CKD without diabetes, including kidney disease linked to hypertension and glomerular diseases. Patients were randomized to receive either finerenone 10mg or 20mg or placebo on top of maximum tolerated labeled doses of a renin-angiotensin system (RAS)-blocking therapy such as an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor or an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB). 
In FIND-CKD, finerenone demonstrated significant cardiorenal benefits versus placebo, in addition to standard of care. Over 32 months, patients treated with finerenone experienced a statistically significant 0.7 ml/minute/1.73 m 2 /year slower annual decline in eGFR than those receiving placebo. Finerenone also significantly reduced the risk of the key secondary composite cardiovascular-kidney outcome by 23% compared with placebo. Additional secondary endpoints, including composites of sustained ≥57% eGFR decline or kidney failure, and of hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular death, showed results consistent with the overall positive profile of finerenone. 
Finerenone was well-tolerated in the FIND-CKD study, which is consistent with the well-established safety profile of finerenone.

title: AskBio Announces 5 Presentations at the European Society of Gene and Cell Therapy (ESGCT) 33rd Annual Congress

content_text:
AskBio Announces 5 Presentations at the European Society of Gene and Cell Therapy (ESGCT) 33rd Annual Congress
Summary
Five poster presentations will highlight exciting progress in AskBio’s adeno-associated virus (AAV) manufacturing technologies 
Durham, N.C., – October 22, 2026 – AskBio Inc. (AskBio), a gene therapy company wholly owned and independently operated as a subsidiary of Bayer AG, and its subsidiary Viralgen Vector Core S.L.U. (Viralgen) will deliver five presentations offering insights into advancements in manufacturing technologies of adeno-associated virus (AAV) therapies for a range of diseases, at the European Society of Gene and Cell Therapy (ESGCT) 33 rd Annual Congress taking place October 27–30, 2026, in Hamburg, Germany. 
“ESGCT is one of the defining scientific meetings for the global cell and gene therapy community, and at AskBio we are proud to continue contributing to the science that is shaping the future of these potentially transformative medicines,” said Gustavo Pesquin, Chief Executive Officer, AskBio. “Our presence this year highlights advances across our AAV manufacturing platform and our work to make production increasingly reproducible, measurable and robust. Collectively, these presentations reflect our continued investment in the technologies, analytical capabilities and process understanding needed to consistently and reliably manufacture gene therapies at scale with a goal to ultimately bring them to the patients who may benefit.” 
AskBio’s presentations include (all times CET): 
Posters 
Development of a stable producer cell line for successful AAV production (Poster #P0767). Poster Session I, Wednesday, October 28, 1:30–3:30 p.m., Elena Lazarova, Scientist II, Cell Line Development, AskBio. 
In-line capacitance probes enable enhanced and consistent high-quality rAAV manufacturing (Poster #P0803). Poster Session I, Wednesday, October 28, 1:30–3:30 p.m., Andoni Gonzalez, R&D Associate Scientist, Viralgen. 
Optimization of recombinant adeno-associated virus vector production: Integrating synthetic molecules to enhance vector yield and quality for clinical gene therapy applications (Poster #P0801). Poster Session I, Wednesday, October 28, 1:30–3:30 p.m., Jose Luis Abad Minguez, R&D Senior Scientist, Viralgen. 
Repeatability and intermediate precision of a genome integrity assay for rAAV by long-read sequencing (Poster #P0253). Poster Session I, Wednesday, October 28, 1:30–3:30 p.m., Oihana Aldasoro, R&D Associate Scientist, Viralgen. 
Investigations of AAV stability under stress conditions using small-scale models (Poster #P0802). Poster Session II, Thursday, October 29, 2:00–4:00 p.m., Ferran Vila Julia, MSAT Scientist, Viralgen. 
AskBio continues to develop an ambitious portfolio of investigational AAV-based gene therapies with the potential to treat some of the world’s most debilitating diseases, including congestive heart failure, limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, multiple system atrophy, Parkinson’s disease, and Pompe disease. By targeting diseases in several therapeutic areas, AskBio aims to deliver innovative treatments that may possibly benefit more than 35 million patients worldwide. 1–5 
About AskBio 
AskBio Inc., a wholly owned and independently operated subsidiary of Bayer AG, is a fully integrated gene therapy company dedicated to steering gene therapy into a new era where it can transform the lives of a wider range of people living with rare and more common diseases. The company maintains a portfolio of clinical programs across a range of disease indications related to a single gene or multiple factors across cardiovascular, central nervous system, and neuromuscular conditions, with a clinical-stage pipeline that includes investigational therapeutics for heart failure, limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, multiple system atrophy, Parkinson’s disease, and Pompe disease. AskBio’s end-to-end gene therapy platform includes our Pro10™ technology and Aava™ manufacturing platform, which make gene therapies more accessible by making research and commercial grade manufacturing more affordable. With global headquarters in Durham, North Carolina, the company has generated hundreds of proprietary capsids and promoters, several of which have entered pre-clinical and clinical testing. An early innovator in the gene therapy field with over 900 employees in five countries, the company holds more than 600 patents and patent applications in areas such as AAV production and chimeric capsids. Learn more at www.askbio.com or follow us on LinkedIn . 
About Viralgen 
Viralgen Vector Core S.L.U. is a leading Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization (CDMO) specializing exclusively in adeno-associated virus (AAV)–based cell and gene therapies. Founded in 2017 as a subsidiary of AskBio Inc. within the Bayer AG group, Viralgen delivers end-to-end support from early development to large-scale commercial manufacturing. Leveraging their proprietary Pro10™ suspension cell line and Aava™ manufacturing platform, Viralgen achieves industry-leading, high-yield, scalable manufacturing across all AAV serotypes. Located in San Sebastián, Spain, its state-of-the-art facility includes three cGMP suites with 2,000-liter capacities each, certified by the AEMPS/EMA, and integrates services including plasmid production, process optimization, fill-finish, and in-house QC testing. With over 1,500 AAV batches produced, Viralgen provides reliable, efficient solutions to bringing life-changing gene therapies to patients with greater speed and consistency. Learn more at https://viralgen.com and follow us on LinkedIn . 
About Bayer 
Bayer is a global enterprise with core competencies in the life science fields of health care and nutrition. In line with its mission, “Health for all, Hunger for none,” the company’s products and services are designed to support efforts to master major challenges presented by a growing and aging global population and create value through innovation and growth. The Bayer brand stands for trust, reliability and quality throughout the world. In fiscal 2025, the Group employed around 88,000 people and had sales of 45.6 billion euros. R&D expenses amounted to 5.8 billion euros. For more information, go to www.bayer.com .

Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany Collaborates with NVIDIA, Microsoft and Dawn Health to Develop Novel Support Model for People Living with Rare Tumors 
Collaboration between with NVIDIA, Microsoft and Dawn Health to explore how AI-facilitated technology can help build an innovative model for PSPs. 
Subscribe
Share 
Icons revealed to the left 
21 Oct 2026 
| 
Darmstadt, Germany 
Collaboration to explore how AI-facilitated technology can help make patient support programs more individualized, responsive and continuously available to people living with rare tumors 
Collaboration brings together clinical and pharmaceutical expertise, digital health product development, and enterprise AI services 
Company aims to bring the model to patients with desmoid tumors and neurofibromatosis type 1 with plexiform neurofibromas (NF1-PN) 
Not intended for UK-based media 
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, a leading science and technology company, today announced a collaboration with NVIDIA Corporation (Santa Clara, California, USA), Microsoft Corporation (Redmond, Washington, USA) and Dawn Health A/S (Copenhagen, Denmark) to build an innovative model for Patient Support Programs (PSPs). The four-way collaboration brings together pharmaceutical and clinical expertise, enterprise technology, AI services and digital health product design, with the shared goal of making specialist-level support more individualized, responsive and continuously available to patients, no matter how complex their treatment journey is.
“Across their treatment journeys, patients with rare tumors often describe challenges that extend well beyond clinical care, like navigating multiple specialists, complex regimens and repeatedly reconstructing their treatment story for each new stakeholder. Our integrated support ecosystem starts with the need. The goal is to truly transform how healthcare is experienced, not add another tool on top of it,” said Miguel Fernández Alcalde, Head of Global Commercial Strategy for Healthcare business sector of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany. “This solution is designed to make more continuous and personalized support available across small and geographically dispersed rare tumor populations, including patients who may have limited access to specialist care.”
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany is collaborating on the design of a pioneering integrated support ecosystem tailored to individual needs of people living with rare tumors, their disease state and circumstances. In practice, the outcome is a AI-facilitated companion, available to patients 24/7. Every interaction is grounded in clinically reviewed content, with defined escalation pathways, and full traceability and audit capabilities. Designed to complement, not replace, the care patients receive from their healthcare team, the companion extends the reach and responsiveness of support, while a nurse or healthcare provider remains available when needed. The collaboration builds on and expands a previously announced partnership between the company and Dawn Health to support rare tumor patients.
The new model to be piloted in key markets in Europe, has an initial focus on rare tumors, specifically desmoid tumors and neurofibromatosis type 1 with plexiform neurofibromas (NF1-PN). These disease areas are known to have complex treatment pathways, and high unmet needs of patients, which makes the case for more consistent, higher-quality support particularly urgent.
The multi-way collaboration is grounded on a shared belief that bringing digital interactions, human services and structured data closer together could, over time, help build a more complete view of how a patient's needs evolve throughout their journey.
Three other relevant players in the technology space have key roles in developing this novel patient solution. NVIDIA contributes AI technology & services including NVIDIA Nemotron , NVIDIA Nemotron Reranking open model, NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails, NeMo Relay, NeMo Gym, NeMo Evaluator, NeMo Data Designer, to help power the program's performance and safety capabilities; Microsoft provides cloud services (Microsoft Foundry, Azure AI Search, the AI Red Teaming Agent as well as Azure Kubernetes Service, Azure SQL and Azure Monitor to run the Dawn Platform); and Dawn Health leads product development, regulatory experience, and the design of patient-facing applications based on the Dawn Platform offering.
Traditional PSPs have long been a cornerstone of the support pharmaceutical companies offer patients, providing structured, validated guidance throughout the treatment journey. As treatment and care pathways grow more complex, patient demand for support is rising, while the reach of these programs often cannot keep pace. Patients in small or dispersed populations, such as those with rare tumors, continue to have limited access to specialist care.

title: EU and UK Risk Falling Further Behind Global Agricultural Competitors, Weakening Strategic Autonomy
query: https://www.bayer.com/media/en-us/
content_text:
EU and UK Risk Falling Further Behind Global Agricultural Competitors, Weakening Strategic Autonomy
Summary
Europe’s crop output has grown more slowly than in major agricultural markets including the US, Brazil, China, Canada and India, a new study finds / Geopolitical and climate pressures are increasing risks for farmers while global peers gain faster access to new technologies, widening Europe’s resilience gap / Consumers support science-based innovation and want farmers to have access to technologies that help strengthen food security, resilience and affordability
Leverkusen, October 15, 2026 – The EU and the UK risk falling further behind major agricultural competitors like the US, Brazil, China, Canada and India unless farmers gain faster access to innovation that can help address growing climate and productivity pressures. A more proportionate regulatory framework and more openness to new technologies could help reverse this trend. These are the main takeaways of a new report commissioned by Bayer, combining economic analysis by Oxford Economics, representative polling of more than 8,000 consumers and in-depth farmer interviews across eight European markets. 
The findings identify crop agriculture as a strategically important sector that underpins food security and contributes 246 billion euros to EU GDP and 5.7 billion euros to UK GDP, with every 1 billion euros of crop agriculture output supporting almost 3 billion euros of downstream production in other sectors. However, crop output growth in Europe has significantly lagged global peers between 2011 and 2023, averaging just 0.1 percent a year. In the UK, growth was even lower, at 0.0 percent. This compares with 1 percent in the US, a global average of 2 percent, and between 2 and 3 percent in China, Canada and India. Brazil was among the fastest-growing markets, with annual growth averaging 3.3 percent over the period. The longer-term comparison is equally stark: average EU production was only 2 percent higher than in the previous decade, compared with increases of 16 percent in the US, 44 percent in Canada and 51 percent in Brazil. 
These competitive pressures are being compounded by sharply rising input costs and the growing impact of climate change. Climate-related risks already cause estimated average annual losses of 17.4 billion euros—equivalent to 6.4 percent of EU crop production—with significant variation across regions. By 2050, these losses are projected to rise to between 24.8 billion euros and 28.9 billion euros. 
The research identifies a growing risk arising from the rapid pace at which pressures on farmers are intensifying, combined with the time it takes for innovations to reach the field. European farmers compete against producers from other regions who have access to a wider variety of seed technologies, crop protection solutions and digital technologies or gain access to such innovations faster. According to Oxford Economics, better access to modern technologies can support farmers in addressing the significant climate and geopolitical challenges, strengthening the agricultural sector’s competitiveness and resilience. 
“The EU and the UK are confronted with a widening resilience gap. To counter that, agriculture must be understood as a critical strategic sector for Europe’s autonomy and competitiveness,” said Frank Terhorst, Head of Strategy & Sustainability for Bayer’s Crop Science Division. “It is critical to embrace innovation as an opportunity rather than a risk to be managed. Europe has the capabilities to lead, but we need to ensure that enough solutions are available to farmers and that innovation can reach the field faster.” 
Research highlights regulatory barriers to agricultural innovation 
The report argues that European farmers need access to a broader range of solutions, including innovative seed technologies, modern crop protection products, precision agriculture, automation and artificial intelligence. Just recently, Bayer announced an upcoming phase of major innovation launches with new seed and trait solutions, including genome editing, and the AI-enabled discovery of new modes of action for crop protection. However, the availability of these agricultural solutions depends largely on regulatory frameworks. 
The research findings highlight a growing concern among farmers that their toolbox is becoming increasingly constrained: While more than 1,000 active ingredients were authorised in the EU in the early 2000s, only around 420 remain approved today. Farmers have lost access to 92 active ingredients in the last seven years, while only one new synthetic active ingredient reached the market over the same period. The UK has approved four entirely new active ingredients since 2022 that remain unapproved or pending in the EU while maintaining approval of 15 crop protection active ingredients whose EU licences have expired or been banned since Brexit. However, the dynamic alignment with the EU regulatory framework currently under discussion could lead to a withdrawal of these approvals, potentially impacting crop yields and farm incomes if transitions are not managed carefully. 
As a consequence, the research points to the need for a more predictable and proportionate regulatory environment that supports innovation while maintaining high standards of safety and stewardship. It highlights lengthy approval processes, increasing administrative burdens and slower adoption pathways as factors limiting access to new technologies across Europe. 
“An approval approach based on real-world risks and benefits instead of theoretical hazards can help ensure farmers gain access to proven innovations while maintaining Europe's high safety standards. Recent UK approvals demonstrate how proportionate pathways can support quicker access to innovation,” added Frank Terhorst. “The report’s findings underscore the urgent need for agricultural innovation. We invest heavily in such new solutions, and we want European farmers to benefit from them like their global peers do.” 
Consumers recognise the importance of agriculture and support science-based innovation 
The consumer polling reveals public awareness of the strategic importance of agriculture. Across Europe, 84 percent of consumers agree that food security is a matter of national security. Consumers see farmer resilience, food affordability and food security as interconnected elements of the same challenge. 
Europeans are also broadly supportive of science and technology. 84 percent say farmers should have access to the latest technology and innovation, so that innovation moves faster, farmers get better harvests and food prices come down. They perceive regulatory barriers, too: 77 percent say cutting bureaucracy and red tape would help make sure Europe can produce enough food. 63 percent say they are more likely to vote for a party that backed farmers using new science and technology. 
“Europeans are more open to innovation and technology than many would assume. People see the connection between resilient farming, food security and affordable food,” summarised Matthias Berninger, Head of Public Affairs, Science, Sustainability & HSE at Bayer. “The findings are a call to action for political, business and civil-society leaders to champion science and new technologies. Europe has spent too much time admiring problems rather than seizing opportunities. While regulation must ensure safety and build trust, it should also enable progress in areas such as AI and agriculture. Europe must move from a culture of risk avoidance to one of innovation.” According to Berninger, Europe has exactly what it takes: “This summer’s decision on New Genomic Techniques demonstrated that Europe can choose innovation over hesitation. We must not lose that momentum. We have great farmers, scientific expertise, good soils and industrial capabilities. We now need to translate these strengths into greater resilience and competitiveness.” 
About the report: 
The research was commissioned by Bayer and combines economic analysis conducted by Oxford Economics, representative polling of more than 8,000 consumers and in-depth interviews with around 90 farmers across eight European markets (Benelux, France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Romania, Spain, United Kingdom). It examines the role innovation can play in strengthening the productivity, competitiveness and resilience of European agriculture, as well as the conditions affecting access to and adoption of new technologies.

Bayer is a global enterprise with core competencies in the life science fields of health care and nutrition. In line with its mission, “Health for all, Hunger for none,” the company’s products and services are designed to support efforts to master major challenges presented by a growing and aging global population and create value through innovation and growth. The Bayer brand stands for trust, reliability and quality throughout the world. In fiscal 2025, the Group employed around 88,000 people and had sales of 45.6 billion euros. 10/01/2026 Martina Gartner Reinforces Schmalz's Executive Management Team
Effective October 1, 2026, Martina Gartner will join the Managing Director team at Schmalz. With her many years of experience in corporate management, controlling, and organizational development, she will help shape the strategic growth of this globally active industrial company in the commercial sector.
Martina Gartner, Schmalz's new Managing Director.
“I look forward to actively shaping the future of Schmalz together with the employees and driving the group’s continued development,” says Martina Gartner, who joined Schmalz’s management team today and is reinforcing the role of Managing Director. “Schmalz stands for innovative strength, long-term thinking, and a unique corporate culture. It is precisely these values and the trusting nature of our collaboration that inspire me.”
I'm inspired by the company culture and the trusting way we work together. ∼ Martina Gartner 
Together with Dr. Kurt Schmalz, Dr. Johannes Schmalz, and Andreas Beutel, Martina Gartner will now steer Schmalz’s course as a member of the executive board. “With Martina Gartner, we are gaining an experienced colleague for our executive management team,” said Dr. Kurt Schmalz, Managing Shareholder. “As our global corporate group becomes increasingly international, the commercial side of the business is growing more complex. By creating a fourth position for a Managing Director, we are responding to this development.”
The Schmalz managing directors (from left): Dr. Kurt Schmalz, Dr. Johannes Schmalz, Martina Gartner, and Andreas Beutel.

title: maxon acquires strategic minority stake in Synapticon
query: https://www.maxongroup.com/en/news-and-events/news
content_text:
maxon acquires strategic minority stake in Synapticon
Download 
Contact us 
Share current page 
The Swiss maxon Group is expanding its expertise in the field of motion control through a strategic partnership with the German company Synapticon. The goal of the collaboration is the joint development of high-performance drive solutions with integrated functional safety, based on optimally combined components from both companies. 
As part of this partnership, the maxon Group has acquired a minority stake in Synapticon. The company, based in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, is a leading provider of intelligent motion control solutions with integrated, certified safety functions. Together, the partners are building a comprehensive portfolio of mechatronic drive systems, which already includes market-ready solutions.
Synapticon follows a "software-first" approach and develops pioneering software and hardware for drive control in robotics and mechanical engineering. The company offers one of the world’s leading portfolios of highly compact, powerful, and intelligent motion control technologies. Its products are used in robotic arms, autonomous transport systems, and complex industrial machinery, among others.
Customers are already benefiting from intelligent, highly integrated solutions based on technologies from maxon and Synapticon. The close collaboration enables efficient further development of existing products and targeted alignment with new applications.
Considering increasing functional safety requirements in many high-tech industries, this investment represents an important strategic step for maxon. The partnership strengthens maxon's position as a provider of future-proof drive systems in dynamically growing markets such as robotics, medical technology, intralogistics, and industrial automation.
Nikolai Ensslen, CEO of Synapticon, states: “This partnership with maxon is of great strategic importance for Synapticon. Together, we will push the boundaries of motion control even further. The market opportunities arising from this collaboration are tremendous.”
Dr. Stefan Müller, CTO of the maxon Group, adds: “Our collaboration with Synapticon opens new possibilities for expanding our expertise in highly integrated drive systems. It enables us to offer even more powerful and safer solutions to our customers.”
The companies have agreed not to disclose the financial terms of the investment.
Contact information 
If you have any questions, please contact the maxon Newsroom:
For inquiries by phone, please call +41 41 662 43 81, or send an e-mail to media@maxongroup.com.
Pictorial material 
Current images can be found by clicking on the download button of this media release.
About maxon: The Swiss specialist for quality drives 
maxon is a leading provider of high-precision electric motors and drive systems, developing solutions tailored to the needs of customers in medical technology, industrial automation, aerospace, mobility, and robotics. Founded in 1961, the Swiss company is family-owned by the Braun family and headquartered in Sachseln, in the canton of Obwalden. maxon Group employs around 3,000 people worldwide across ten production sites and is represented in more than 40 countries.
About Synapticon 
Synapticon is a leading full-stack provider of intelligent drive and safety technologies for robotics and mechanical engineering. Headquartered in Schönaich near Stuttgart and with locations in Silicon Valley and Shenzhen, the company develops and produces highly integrated solutions for motion control and functional safety. The product portfolio includes the award-winning and safety-certified SOMANET Circulo and Integro servo drive families, power-dense actuators for robotics and mechanical engineering from the ACTILINK series, the OBLAC and MOTORCORTEX software solutions and the POSITRON Safety AI platform for the most demanding applications in the field of functional safety. With its software-first approach, deeply integrated electronics and innovative control technology, Synapticon reduces engineering complexity while increasing performance, precision and efficiency. Leading developers of industrial, collaborative, mobile and humanoid robots and complex machines worldwide rely on Synapticon as a trusted partner for the realisation of their most ambitious products.

maxon at the SPS 2025: New drive solutions for robotics, automation and mobility
Download 
Contact us 
Share current page 
At the SPS trade fair from November 25 to 27, 2025, maxon will present a wide range of new products. From highly integrated robotic actuators to powerful servo drives and controllers: a diverse technology portfolio awaits visitors at the maxon booth in Hall 3, Stand 468.
One focus at the maxon booth will be the further developed robotics solutions, in particular the High Efficiency Joints (HEJ). These compact, highly integrated quasi-direct drive (QDD) actuators combine motor, gearhead, sensors, and electronics in a single, robust housing. Following the successful launch of the HEJ 90 (140 Nm), the HEJ 70 with 62 Nm torque now follows - ideal for smaller robots. The HEJ 50 variant is also currently in production and will be available from early 2026. The powerful HEJ "Hercules" with over 250 Nm is under development.
With this scalable platform, maxon consistently pursues the goal of shortening development times and reducing the overall costs for modern robotics.
Additions to the maxon portfolio
At SPS, maxon will present several additions to its product portfolio: 
IDX 70 - Compact high-performance servo drive with safety certification 
The new IDX 70 combines high power density with a compact footprint, making it ideal for mobile robotics, cobots, and driverless transport systems (AGVs). The IDX 70 offers an excellent torque-to-weight ratio and is suitable for demanding industrial environments thanks to its robust design. The certified Safe Torque Off function (STO) and Safe Brake Control (SBC) ensure compliance with the highest safety standards.
EC frameless DT 50 - Flexible, dynamic, efficient 
The new EC frameless DT 50 is a brushless motor without a flange and now also available with integrated Hall sensors. The design allows for optimal installation versatility, whether in articulated joints, machine tools, or exoskeletons. With high torque density and outstanding efficiency, it enables precise, dynamic motion with minimal heat generation. Additional sizes — 38 mm, 65 mm, and 85 mm — will be available next year.
Strain wave gearheads - precision in the smallest space 
With the new Strain wave gearheads, maxon expands its portfolio, especially for applications with high demands on precision in torque transmission. The backlash-free design ensures exact motion control in minimal installation space – ideal for robotic arms, surgical instruments, or optical applications. In combination with maxon drives, this results in a perfectly matched drive system from a single source - currently available in diameters of 55mm and 62mm. Additional sizes and variants are planned and will be presented at SPS. 
EPOS4 Module/Compact 60/20 STO - Compact controllers with integrated safety 
The new positioning controllers, with certified STO function up to SIL 3 / PL e category 3, combine advanced control performance and safety in a compact form. They enable precise motion control in modular machines, collaborative robots, or autonomous vehicles. Thanks to versatile interfaces, they can be seamlessly integrated into existing automation systems.
MiniMACS6 AMP 4IF1 Profinet - multi-axis controller for networked systems 
The MiniMACS6 AMP 4-IF1 Profinet adds a Profinet communication interface to the successful MACS family. This positions the controller as a key link between motion control and industrial networking. In production environments and robotic systems, it ensures precise real-time coordination of multiple axes and processes.
BIKEDRIVE AIR S e-bike drive: efficiency meets driving experience 
In addition to industrial applications, maxon will also be showcasing its latest innovation in the field of lightweight electromobility: the BIKEDRIVE AIR S –the lightest full-power e-bike drive in its class. With a drive weight of just 2 kg, 90 Nm torque, and whisper-quiet operation, the system sets new standards for a sporty yet natural riding experience.

Meet us in Hall 3, Stand 468, and talk to our experts about the latest drive solutions.

maxon at Hannover Messe 2026: Robotics drives, latest portfolio additions, and functional safety
Download 
Contact us 
Share current page 
At Hannover Messe 2026, maxon will present itself with an updated trade fair appearance. From April 20 to 24, the maxon Germany team will showcase the latest highlights from our product portfolio.
At Hannover Messe, maxon traditionally introduces its latest portfolio additions. Here is what visitors can expect at our booth:
Robotics solutions: maxon’s High Efficiency Joints (HEJ) bring motion to robotics. They enable humanoid robots to operate in unstructured environments and are also suitable for industrial applications. At Hannover Messe, we will present the proven High Efficiency Joint 90, as well as the new, smaller HEJ 70.
Drives: In our highlight showcases, we present a wide range of maxon drives combined with gearheads and sensors. Among them is the EC frameless DT 50 M: easy to integrate into customer applications thanks to its separate stator and rotor design, offering high efficiency and dynamic torque. Another example is the ECX PRIME 16L - the long version of our brushless motor with ironless winding. These are just two of many new additions.
EC frameless DT50M 
1 / 6 
Gearheads: Since launching our new GSW strain wave gear series, we have continuously developed it further. Our gearheads transmit high torques precisely and efficiently and can be combined with a wide range of maxon drives. In Hannover, we will, for example, present the GSW 20 in combination with an ECX PRIME drive.
Industrial drives: Our IDX series meets industrial standards and is a proven plug-and-play solution - for industrial applications or autonomous vehicles in intralogistics. At Hannover Messe, we will present the IDX 70 Safe Control, featuring integrated functional safety up to SIL3 / PL e, Cat. 3.
Precision, performance and integrated safety
Electronics: Functional safety is also becoming increasingly important in this field, which is why maxon continues to develop its control solutions accordingly. One example is the EPOS4 Compact 60/20 STO (Safe Torque Off). Visitors can also see the smallest controllers in the maxon portfolio: ESCON2 Nano 24/2 and ESCON2 Micro 60/5. We will also present the MiniMACS6, our freely programmable multi-axis controller, now also available with a PROFINET interface. In addition, we will demonstrate our predictive maintenance solution, maxon MIND, and explain why the motor is the best sensor in a customer application.
Parvalux: The UK-based company Parvalux, part of maxon, specializes in small and medium-sized geared motors. Parvalux solutions drive windshield wipers in high-speed trains or move patients in hospitals. At Hannover Messe, we will show how maxon and Parvalux products can be ideally combined, for example, the maxon IDX industrial drive with the Parvalux GB 28 right-angle gearbox.
At our booth, we will also present various live demos showcasing our drive solutions in action. The maxon Germany team will be available for any questions.
You can find us at Hannover Messe in Hall 13, Booth C51. 
For further information, please contact the maxon Newsroom . 
Learn more about our solutions .

The completely revised maxon catalog 2026/2027 has been released
Download 
Contact us

The completely revised maxon catalog 2026/2027 has been released 
maxon has fundamentally revised its catalog. The new structure is designed to make access to products and applications easier while providing a clearer overview of the company, its markets, and its technological capabilities. 
The maxon Catalog 2026/2027 has been completely reconceived. As part of a targeted portfolio streamlining, redundancies were minimized and complexity reduced. The revised structure of the product categories now features clearly organized introductory pages that enable a quick entry into each portfolio segment. This is complemented by a new “Welcome” section that positions maxon as a company and clearly communicates at a glance what maxon stands for.
A particular focus has been placed on the Market Solutions, which now have their own dedicated section. Each maxon business unit (Medical, Aerospace, Industrial Automation, and Mobility) is presented on a double-page spread, with the respective expertise in the relevant submarkets clearly highlighted.
In addition, the areas of Robotics, Space, and Electronics are presented separately within the Market Solutions. This demonstrates maxon’s broad market competence and enables targeted browsing while maintaining a clear overview of the core markets. The section “Technology – short and to the point” has also been completely revised.
The stars of the new catalog, of course, remain the products. The portfolio has been expanded with several highlights, including the brushless ECX PRIME 4-pole motors for high speeds and torque, the powerful ECX FLAT flat motors with fan, new diameters of the EC frameless high‑torque motors, and the backlash-free GSW planetary gearheads. The new products are complemented by the versatile ESCON2 servo controllers and the EPOS4 positioning controllers.
The new catalog is available as an e-paper .
Images 
An image of the current catalog is available via the download button of this release.
Further Information 
For inquiries, the maxon Newsroom is available:
media@maxongroup.com 
Phone: +41 41 662 43 81
About maxon: The Swiss Specialist for Quality Drive Systems 
maxon is a leading provider of precision electric motors and drive systems, developing solutions tailored to customer needs in the fields of medical technology, industrial automation, aerospace, mobility, and robotics. Founded in 1961, the Swiss company is owned by the Braun family and is headquartered in Sachseln (Canton of Obwalden). The maxon Group employs around 3,000 people worldwide at ten production sites and is represented in more than 40 countries.

Investment in LOMBY Inc., through Nabtesco Technology Ventures
Sep 30, 2026 
Business 
Investment and Alliance 
Nabtesco Corporation (Head Office: Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo; President & CEO: Kazumasa Kimura) is pleased to announce that Nabtesco Technology Ventures L.P. (Managing Partner: Hiroshi Nerima), the corporate venture capital fund established by Nabtesco, has invested in LOMBY Inc. (LOMBY), a Tokyo-based robotics company developing, manufacturing and operating autonomous mobility robots.
LOMBY is a startup company that develops outdoor autonomous mobility solutions combining robotics and AI. Its flagship product, the LM-A autonomous delivery robot, is an autonomous mobility robot that travels on sidewalks and similar areas under a remote-monitoring framework, having completed the required notification as a "remote-controlled compact vehicle" under the Road Traffic Act, thereby contributing to labor savings and greater efficiency in delivery operations. Commercial operation has already commenced in certain areas, and in the future the company also envisions expanding beyond the delivery field into services that support the mobility of people.
In the logistics industry, addressing labor shortages and improving delivery efficiency have become critical challenges, and expectations for autonomous delivery technology are rising. To date, Nabtesco has supplied wireless charging systems manufactured by WiBotic Inc. of the United States, which the Company distributes, for LOMBY's delivery robots. This investment builds on that existing business relationship and is intended to support LOMBY's business expansion.
Through this investment, Nabtesco will further build its knowledge of the autonomous delivery robot market and related infrastructure, while exploring the creation of new business opportunities and synergies through collaboration with LOMBY.
Going forward, Nabtesco will continue to deepen its collaboration with promising startup companies through open innovation activities, pursuing new business opportunities and working to enhance its corporate value.

content_text:
EV Group Highlights Hybrid Bonding, Layer Transfer and Lithography Technologies for Heterogeneous Integration and Device Scaling at SEMICON West 2026
Chiplet integration on a wafer enabled by collective die-to-wafer hybrid bonding. Source: EV Group.
ST. FLORIAN, Austria, September 29, 2026 —EV Group (EVG), a leading provider of innovative process solutions and expertise serving leading-edge and future semiconductor designs and chip integration schemes, today announced that its experts will be available to discuss EVG’s latest solutions for heterogeneous integration and device scaling at SEMICON West, the premier microelectronics exhibition in North America, to be held on October 13-15 in San Francisco, Calif. EVG’s process solutions address key manufacturing challenges associated with increasingly complex device architectures and integration approaches, including high-bandwidth memory (HBM), complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs), co-packaged optics (CPO), 3D/chiplet integration and other advanced packaging applications. 
“As semiconductor device architectures become more complex and increasingly integrated, manufacturers are facing new challenges that cannot be addressed through isolated solutions,” stated Hermann Waltl, executive sales and customer support director at EV Group. “EVG provides the breadth of process expertise and manufacturing capabilities needed to address these challenges across advanced packaging, heterogeneous integration, and next-generation device scaling. By applying our solutions and know-how across these different areas, we help customers turn these emerging integration opportunities into manufacturable processes for future semiconductor devices.”
Supporting High-Yield Hybrid Bonding for Advanced Memory and 3D Integration 
Wafer-to-wafer (W2W) hybrid bonding is critical for enabling high-yield, scalable manufacturing of next-generation 3D NAND and DRAM, which demand sub-micron alignment accuracy and excellent bond strength. Die-to-wafer (D2W) hybrid bonding is an important enabler of chiplet integration, HBM stacks, and 3D system-on-chip (SoC) integration processes. 
EVG provides a complete hybrid bonding process flow for W2W bonding, including the GEMINI ® FB automated production wafer bonding system for high-volume hybrid and fusion wafer bonding.  imec and EVG recently demonstrated a highly yielding W2W hybrid bonding process at 200-nm copper interconnect pitch, achieving sub-40-nm post-bond overlay accuracy across 100 percent of dies on a 
300-mm wafer, using a GEMINI FB system. EVG also provides comprehensive support for D2W hybrid bonding, including surface preparation, cleaning, and collective die transfer with the EVG ® 320 D2W, and high-resolution die-to-wafer overlay measurements at the highest throughput with the EVG ® 40 D2W. 
Comprehensive Process Expertise for CPO Manufacturing 
EVG’s process portfolio addresses numerous critical manufacturing requirements across the CPO ecosystem. The GEMINI FB enables high-density, low-parasitic integration of photonic integrated circuits (PICs) and electronic integrated circuits (EICs), while the EVG320 D2W supports heterogeneous integration of III-V semiconductor materials for laser fabrication and emerging modulation materials. EVG’s ComBond ® automated high-vacuum wafer bonding system ensures low-loss, optically transparent interfaces and integration of heat spreader materials such as diamond and silicon carbide (SiC), while the EVG ® 850 TB/DB supports wafer thinning for laser diode fabrication and ultra-thin ASIC die stacking. The HERCULES ® NIL fully integrated SmartNIL ® UV-NIL system provides a scalable manufacturing approach for optical coupling and beam-shaping elements used in chip-to-chip and chip-to-fiber optical interconnects.
Digital Lithography for Advanced Packaging Applications 
EVG’s LITHOSCALE ® XT system with MLE™ (maskless exposure) technology combines high-resolution, stitch-free patterning with high throughput for advanced packaging and MEMS applications, including fan-out wafer-level packaging (FOWLP) for AI and HPC devices, fine-pitch wafer probe cards, advanced imaging sensors, and die traceability for security and automotive applications. Its real-time wafer-level distortion and die-shift compensation provides improved die-placement accuracy and patterning yield for bowed or warped wafers, such as those used in FOWLP, without impacting throughput.
Enabling Thin-Die Stacks with IR LayerRelease™ 
EVG’s IR LayerRelease technology is a fully front-end-compatible layer transfer technology that uses an infrared laser in combination with specially formulated inorganic release layers to enable laser-initiated release of ultra-thin films and layers from silicon carriers with nanometer precision and high throughput. The technology enables the use of silicon wafer carriers instead of glass carriers in advanced packaging processes such as FOWLP and interposer-based 3D integration. At the same time, its compatibility with high-temperature processes enables novel process flows for 3D-IC and 3D sequential integration, including hybrid and fusion bonding of ultra-thin layers on silicon carriers for next-generation transistor designs.
Hear from EVG’s Process Experts 
At the Advanced Packaging & Heterogeneous Integration Summit during SEMICON West, Vineeth Reddy Bijjam, director of technology and IP, will present “Accelerating 3D Heterogeneous Integration with Advanced Bonding, Lithography and Metrology” during the Metrology & Inspection: The Gatekeepers of Yield in Advanced Packaging session on Tue., October 13, 2:30-2:50 pm in Room 156, South Hall, Upper Mezzanine, Moscone Center.
To speak with an EVG expert and learn more about the company’s industry-leading solutions for heterogeneous integration and device scaling, visit EVG’s booth 2039 (South Hall) during exhibition hours.
About EV Group (EVG) 
EV Group (EVG) provides innovative process solutions and expertise that serve leading-edge and future semiconductor designs and chip integration schemes. The company’s vision of being the first in exploring new techniques and supporting next-generation applications of micro- and nanofabrication technologies enables customers to successfully commercialize new product ideas. EVG’s high-volume-manufacturing-ready products, which include wafer bonding, lithography, thin-wafer processing and metrology equipment, enable advances in semiconductor front-end scaling, 3D integration and advanced packaging, as well as in other electronics and photonics applications. More information about EVG is available at  www.EVGroup.com .

Hydro to receive EUR 28 million compensation following wind farm sale
Hydro agreed in 2025 to a future settlement related to the long-term power purchase agreement (PPA) with the Swedish wind farm Cloud Snurran AB. An agreement to sell the wind park has now been entered into and Hydro expects to receive its settlement compensation following the sale.
The settlement agreement regarding the voluntary termination of the long-term power purchase agreement was entered into in July 2025. According to the agreement, Hydro’s ultimate compensation depends on the realized value from a future sale and an agreed value sharing mechanism.
Following completion of the transaction, Hydro expects to receive compensation of approximately EUR 28 million. The final amount remains subject to customary closing adjustments. Completion is expected mid-October 2026.
