content_text:
Nvidia Teams Up With Supply Chain on Glass Substrates, Next-Gen GPUs Set to Pack More HBM
Add preferred source 4 
Nvidia is working with supply chain partners to accelerate the commercialization of glass substrate technology, aiming to integrate more HBM into next-generation GPU packaging. German equipment maker SCHMID disclosed it is collaborating with core companies in the supply chains of Intel, Nvidia, and AMD to develop glass core substrate equipment, though TGV metallization still faces technical hurdles and end-customer qualification remains incomplete. Jensen Huang has discussed related cooperation with SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won and is pushing TSMC to accelerate technology development. Notably, major players are pursuing different routes: TSMC's CoPoS replaces silicon interposers with square panels, while Intel and Samsung Electro-Mechanics target the core layer of organic substrates. Japanese materials suppliers such as NEG and AGC have already unveiled large glass substrate samples measuring 515×510 mm. Glass substrates offer superior flatness, lower thermal expansion coefficients, and excellent dielectric properties, potentially boosting packaging density and data transmission capability, but large-scale commercialization still requires time.
Key Elements 
Nvidia SCHMID Jensen Huang SK Group TSMC Intel AMD Roland Rettenmayer Chey Tae-won 
Nvidia is joining forces with supply chain partners to accelerate the industrialization of glass substrate technology, targeting the increasingly prominent physical bottlenecks in AI chip packaging. If this technology route achieves a breakthrough, next-generation GPUs could integrate significantly larger amounts of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) within a single package, substantially boosting data throughput.
German equipment maker SCHMID disclosed at its recent first-half earnings briefing that the company is collaborating with core companies in the supply chains of Intel, Nvidia, and AMD to advance the development of glass core substrate equipment. SCHMID Chief Sales Officer Roland Rettenmayer acknowledged at the briefing that through-glass via (TGV) metallization still faces technical obstacles, and end-customer qualification has yet to be completed.
This statement has thrust glass substrate technology from the laboratory into the industry spotlight. As a potentially transformative material for AI chip packaging, glass substrates are expected to address the inherent limitations of traditional plastic substrates in heat resistance and warpage control, while offering a new pathway to overcome the size and cost constraints of silicon interposers.
Glass Substrates Target Packaging Bottlenecks
As AI chip performance and power consumption continue to climb, packaging is becoming a critical chokepoint constraining further gains in computing power. Traditional plastic substrates tend to deform under high temperatures and lack sufficient heat resistance, whereas glass substrates—with higher flatness and strength and a lower coefficient of thermal expansion—exhibit significantly less deformation under high-temperature operating conditions. This property is particularly important for high-performance AI chips that generate enormous amounts of heat.
Moreover, glass substrates offer excellent dielectric properties and lower signal loss, enabling higher accuracy in ultra-high-speed signal transmission. These physical characteristics position them as a potential solution for next-generation high-performance chip packaging.
Even more noteworthy is the potential of glass substrates in packaging size expansion. Current mainstream AI chips generally adopt a silicon interposer approach, integrating GPU and HBM side by side within the same package. However, silicon interposers face clear constraints in size scaling and manufacturing cost. Glass substrates could partially or even fully replace silicon interposers, accommodating more chips and HBM within a single package, thereby increasing packaging density and shortening data transmission paths.
Size constraints are not merely theoretical. According to a June 30 report by semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis, the four-compute-die version of Rubin Ultra announced by Nvidia at GTC 2026 has been cancelled because TSMC's existing CoWoS-L packaging cannot control substrate warpage at the four-die scale; the production version reverts to a dual-die design, with compute capability and memory bandwidth roughly half of the originally announced specifications. Per the report's calculations, the interposer area required for the four-die configuration would be approximately 7.5 to 8 times the reticle area limit (about 858 square millimeters), and organic substrates and silicon dies expand and contract at different rates under temperature cycling—warpage beyond a certain threshold causes dies to lose electrical contact with the substrate. Nvidia has not publicly confirmed this design change.
For AI chips, this translates into larger HBM integration scale and higher data throughput. HBM boosts bandwidth by vertically stacking multiple layers of DRAM and is the core memory component of current AI accelerators. As large model scale and compute demand continue to grow, how much HBM a single package can accommodate is increasingly becoming a critical factor limiting AI chip performance.
Three Routes, Three Different Targets
Glass substrates are often discussed as a single technology, but the major players are actually targeting different replacement objects, and their progress differs by years. TSMC aims to replace the silicon interposer, while Intel and Samsung Electro-Mechanics are targeting the core layer of organic substrates—the two approaches involve different validation targets and technical specifications.
Company Technology Route Replacement Target Latest Progress 
TSMC CoPoS: square panel + multi-layer redistribution layer Silicon interposer (current CoWoS) Pilot line built; targeting volume production in 2028–2029 
Intel Glass core substrate ABF organic substrate core layer Unveiled industry's first sample in September 2023; targeting mass production in the latter half of the 2020s 
Samsung Electro-Mechanics Glass core substrate Organic substrate core layer Joint venture GlaSSEM with Sumitomo Chemical's wholly owned Korean subsidiary; targeting supply system readiness in the second half of FY2027 
SKC (Absolics) Glass core substrate Organic substrate core layer Small-volume production at Georgia, USA plant 
Nvidia's Multi-Pronged Approach
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has already engaged with multiple parties on this technology route. In meetings with SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won, the two discussed next-generation semiconductor cooperation including glass substrates, and Huang has actively pushed TSMC to accelerate the pace of related technology development. These moves indicate that Nvidia is seriously evaluating the feasibility of introducing glass substrates into next-generation GPUs.
From a supply chain perspective, Nvidia is not acting alone. SCHMID is simultaneously working with core companies in the supply chains of Intel and AMD, indicating that glass substrate technology has been incorporated into the next-generation product technology evaluation scope of multiple leading chipmakers. This multi-track parallel landscape reflects both the industry consensus on existing packaging bottlenecks and the possibility that once the technology matures, the industrialization of glass substrates could proceed faster than market expectations.
The SCHMID Group is currently developing equipment and solutions required for glass substrate production, while simultaneously expanding its business in AI server motherboards and next-generation packaging equipment. Against the backdrop of sharply rising demand for high-performance computing infrastructure in the AI era, the strategic intent of this business layout is unmistakable.
Progress in the Japanese and Taiwanese Supply Chains
The shift in packaging from circular wafers to square panels benefits more than just chipmakers. SCHMID noted at its earnings briefing that three panel sizes—310×310 mm, 510×515 mm, and 600×600 mm—are gradually becoming standardized across the supply chain, with TSMC, Intel, Samsung, and their respective supply chains all adopting these specifications; the panel-level packaging market could expand three to four times by 2030.
TSMC has been advancing glass substrate validation together with Japanese substrate leader Ibiden and Taiwanese panel maker Innolux—panel makers inherently have advantages in large-format glass processing, and after production line modifications, they can handle substrate areas several times larger than wafers. Intel does not produce panels, circuit boards, or substrates in-house, instead sourcing them indirectly through substrate maker partners in Japan and Taiwan; its progress on glass core substrates therefore depends equally on these manufacturers' production line investments. This Japanese substrate maker announced in February that it will invest approximately ¥500 billion (approximately $3.2 billion) during fiscal years 2026–2028 to expand high-performance IC packaging substrate capacity, primarily targeting AI and high-performance servers.
Japanese materials suppliers are actually further ahead in this segment. Nippon Electric Glass (NEG) has developed a glass-ceramic core substrate called GC Core, and can already provide large samples measuring 515×510 mm with TGV processing; it also exhibited at SEMICON Taiwan in Taipei in early September. The company has mastered two via processes: CO₂ laser direct drilling, which involves fewer steps and higher speed and can leverage existing laser processing equipment used for circuit boards; and a modified etching method that can achieve smaller via diameters and finer pitches. AGC's alkali-free glass packaging substrate has already been commercialized, with both 500 mm square panels and 300 mm diameter wafers available.
In terms of market size, research firm Counterpoint estimates that the combined market for fan-out panel-level packaging (FOPLP) and glass substrate packaging will grow from approximately $650 million in 2024 to more than $8.1 billion by 2030. This scope covers only advanced packaging; it is not the same as the commonly cited global glass substrate market size (which is dominated by glass for display panels).
TGV Metallization Remains the Mass Production Hurdle
Despite the promising outlook, glass substrates still face substantial obstacles before large-scale commercialization. SCHMID explicitly identified TGV metallization as one of the most critical technical bottlenecks at present.
Glass itself is non-conductive, so forming stable, reliable, high-density interconnect vias within the substrate is the key to achieving mass production. The maturity of this process directly determines whether glass substrates can move from the sample stage to volume supply.
At the same time, end-customer qualification has not been completed, meaning the technology remains in the industrialization phase. For Nvidia and its supply chain, whether glass substrates can ultimately enter large-scale GPU production still depends on further maturation across multiple dimensions, including manufacturing process stability, long-term reliability, and customer qualification.
The industrialization timeline is becoming concrete:
From a timeline perspective, semiconductor packaging material transitions typically require lengthy validation cycles. The journey of glass substrates from technology validation to production adoption may still need to cross multiple thresholds, including equipment maturity, yield ramp-up, and cost optimization. But the sustained investment by Nvidia and its partners in this direction has already sketched a clear technology path for the packaging evolution of next-generation AI chips.

content_text:
More than 10 Applied Materials tools were built in Singapore. Now its advanced packaging lab is expanding 
Dashveenjit Kaur 
September 25, 2026
Share this story:
Tags:
A*STAR 
advanced packaging 
AI infrastructure 
Applied Materials 
GlobalFoundries 
KLA 
R&D 
semiconductors 
silicon photonics 
singapore 
Categories::
Asia Pacific Focus 
Government Initiatives & Policy 
Singapore 
Applied Materials will expand its advanced packaging joint lab with A*STAR in one of its largest Singapore R&D investments to date. 
Singapore also announced collaborations in silicon photonics, process control, and MEMS, and a national brand for the sector. 
Applied Materials will expand its advanced packaging joint laboratory with Singapore’s Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR), in what Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) Dr Tan See Leng called one of the company’s largest R&D investments in Singapore to date. 
Announcing Phase 4 of the partnership at the Innovate Together forum on Friday, Tan said the expansion would significantly increase the lab’s infrastructure, equipment and headcount, supporting deeper research into advanced packaging for AI and advanced computing. 
“Advanced packaging is one area where public-private partnerships have produced encouraging results, including spillovers to the wider ecosystem,” Tan said. 
The collaboration dates back to 2011 and has run through three phases. Applied Materials has launched more than 10 semiconductor manufacturing tools developed in Singapore through the partnership, most of which have become global bestsellers, according to Tan: the ministry named Ventura, InVia 2 and Kinex among them. Over the past five years, the partnership has also enabled work between A*STAR and about 50 companies, including nine local SMEs, on R&D projects worth S$46 million in industry funding. 
Two more advanced packaging collaborations 
A*STAR will set up a joint lab with KLA, the US company whose inspection and measurement tools chipmakers use to find defects during production. The lab will develop process control solutions that catch those defects earlier, according to the ministry, with the aim of improving device reliability and manufacturing yield, and will sit with A*STAR’s Institute of Microelectronics. KLA is partway through a US$200 million expansion of its own Singapore operations, due to reach 420,000 square feet this year. 
A*STAR will also work with STATS ChipPAC on co-packaged optics, combining A*STAR’s technologies with the assembly and test firm’s manufacturing capabilities to build a pathway towards high-volume production. Co-packaged optics moves the optical components into the chip package itself, which the ministry said would enable faster and more energy-efficient data movement inside AI data centres. 
GlobalFoundries returns to A*STAR a year after acquiring its 2017 spin-off 
In silicon photonics, A*STAR and GlobalFoundries will collaborate on next-generation technologies built on 300-millimetre wafers, aimed at high-performance computing and, potentially, quantum applications. 
For context, the two have a longer history than the announcement suggests. A*STAR spun off Advanced Micro Foundry (AMF) in 2017, and Tan said AMF’s manufacturing assets, intellectual property and talent were what attracted GlobalFoundries to acquire the company in 2025. The agreement announced on Friday brings the foundry back to the agency that created the business it bought. 
See also: How Singapore and Malaysia are betting on advanced packaging from opposite ends of the value chain 
Separately, the National Centre for Advanced Integrated Photonics, hosted at Nanyang Technological University, will work with Battery Age Minerals on germanium-based optical interconnect technology. The Australian company holds access to raw germanium, and A*STAR said the collaboration creates a potential pathway from upstream resources into higher-value semiconductor applications. 
In sensing, Tacta Systems will develop MEMS technologies for robotics using A*STAR’s Lab-in-Fab platform, which lets companies validate technologies in a production-relevant environment before scaling. Tacta has also opened its Singapore operations. 
Talent remains the constraint 
Tan named talent as the second of two priorities for the sector, alongside industry partnerships. 
The Singapore Institute of Technology will pilot a “2+2” model from September 2027, under which students spend their first two years on campus and almost two years in workplace immersion. At the postgraduate level, 14 semiconductor companies have taken part in the Industrial Postgraduate Programme over the past five years, producing close to 100 graduates. 
The announcements were made under SG Semiconductor, a national identity for the sector developed jointly by A*STAR and the Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) and launched at the same event. A*STAR said the brand is intended to raise global visibility of Singapore’s capabilities and make the ecosystem easier for companies and talent to navigate, and that the effort will focus on public sector R&D as its first course of action. 
“As semiconductor technologies become more complex, companies are increasingly seeking trusted locations where innovation, manufacturing and talent come together,” said Jermaine Loy, managing director of EDB. 
Singapore accounts for about one in ten chips produced globally and one in five pieces of semiconductor manufacturing equipment, according to the ministry. “We must not take this position for granted,” Tan said. The sector’s seven priority technology areas span advanced packaging, silicon photonics, power electronics, radio frequency gallium nitride, piezoMEMS, flat optics and integrated circuit design, supported by the S$800 million RIE Flagship in Semiconductors announced earlier this year, which runs from 2026 to 2030.

Jenoptik wins deal for 140+ intersection safety cameras in Canada
By Tom Stone September 25, 2026 3 Mins Read 
Share 
LinkedIn 
Twitter 
Facebook 
Email 
Jenoptik will supply more than 140 intersection safety camera systems combining red light and speed on green detection for ICBC 
Jenoptik has been awarded a contract by the Insurance Corporation of British Columbia (ICBC) to supply more than 140 intersection safety camera systems as part of ICBC’s Intersection Safety Camera Program, which aims to improve safety at signalised intersections across the Canadian province.
Under the agreement, Jenoptik Canada will deliver, implement and install the systems, which combine red light violation detection with speed on green detection. The cameras will be supported by the company’s FlowTris back-office platform, which will handle the capture, processing and management of enforcement data generated by the programme.
Enforcement data from the cameras will be captured, processed and managed through Jenoptik’s FlowTris back-office platform 
Red light and speed on green detection
Combining the two functions allows each installation to monitor vehicles entering an intersection against a red signal and vehicles exceeding the speed limit as they pass through on green. The FlowTris platform is intended to provide a secure workflow for administering the programme, from the point of capture through to processing and data management.
Intersection safety camera programmes are designed to encourage compliance with traffic laws at signalised intersections. By reducing high-risk driving behaviour, they aim to improve safety for motorists, pedestrians and cyclists.
“We are proud to partner with ICBC in supporting its Intersection Safety Camera Program and its commitment to improving road safety across British Columbia,” says Candice Holder-Mattadeen, head of sales at Jenoptik Canada. “With more than 20 years of experience delivering road safety solutions in Canada, we look forward to working with ICBC to implement a modern, reliable intersection safety camera program that helps improve safety for all road users.”
Coast-to-coast footprint and new Vancouver office
With the British Columbia contract, Jenoptik says it now has installations from coast to coast in Canada. The company is also opening a new office in Vancouver, which it says will bring more jobs to the local community.
About Jenoptik Smart Mobility Solutions
Jenoptik is a photonics technology group whose core markets include semiconductor technology, medical technology, metrology and smart mobility. The group employs approximately 4,300 people worldwide and generated revenue of €1,046m in fiscal year 2025.
Its Smart Mobility Solutions strategic business unit provides roadside equipment and software for road safety and security, supporting customers with integration, installation, maintenance and financing models through to full-service operation. The company reports tens of thousands of systems deployed worldwide and 40 years of experience in automatic number plate recognition (ANPR).

content_text:
Vestas wins first order for new V182-7.2 MW turbine for project in Sweden
Friday, 25 September 2026 
Robin Whitlock 
Vestas has secured a firm order with SR Energy in Sweden for the newly launched V182-7.2 MW turbine, marking the first order globally for the turbine only a day after its official launch to the market. V182 wind turbine. Courtesy of Vestas. 
The order confirms the market-readiness of Vestas’ latest turbine and demonstrates a strong market interest in the latest evolution of the EnVentus platform, designed to increase energy production and strengthen business case certainty for customers.
The order is for the 29 MW Staverhult project and includes supply, delivery, and commissioning of four V182-7.2 MW turbines as well as a 35-year Active Output Management 5000 (AOM 5000) service agreement designed to ensure optimised performance throughout the lifetime of the project.
“We are delighted to take the next step and begin construction of the Staverhult wind farm” said Peter Zachrisson, CEO, SR Energy. “By investing in Vestas’ latest generation of efficient wind turbine technology, we can make the most of the excellent wind conditions and deliver more renewable electricity where it is needed most. Staverhult is exactly the kind of project we want to develop - a long-term investment that strengthens electricity supply in southern Sweden and contributes to a more robust and competitive energy system.”
By utilising the proven EnVentus platform and upgrading only what creates meaningful customer value, the V182-7.2 MW is now ready for customers’ project planning and Vestas is able to ramp up serial production from end of 2027.
“This milestone underlines that our new turbine is ready for the market and it demonstrates that when the right technology is matched with the right business case, projects can move forward even in challenging market conditions” added Jens Kück, Senior Vice President for Sales in Vestas Northern and Central Europe. “By combining enhanced energy production and the certainty of a proven platform, the V182-7.2 MW helps improve project economics and unlock investment opportunities, supporting the next phase of wind energy growth in Sweden.”
Turbine delivery is expected to begin in the second quarter of 2028, with commissioning scheduled for the third quarter of 2028. Once commissioned, the project will help meet Sweden's growing demand for affordable, secure, and sustainable energy.

content_text:
Zhejiang Petrochemical and Sumitomo Chemical Shutdowns Tighten Asian MMA Supply
Nicholas Sparks 25-Sep-2026 
The Asian Methyl Methacrylate (MMA) market is experiencing tighter supply conditions following multiple maintenance-related disruptions and reduced operating rates across key production facilities in China, Singapore, and South Korea. In China, maintenance at Zhejiang Petrochemical and Zibo Qixiang Tengda temporarily reduced domestic MMA availability, while Sumitomo Chemical Asia’s Jurong Island facility operated at a significantly lower rate, limiting supply from Singapore. The prolonged reduction in Singapore further tightened regional availability before the facility returned to operations on September 25. Meanwhile, reduced operating rates at LG Chem’s Yeosu Acrylic Acid facility temporarily constrained feedstock availability and added pressure to the MMA production chain. Although several affected facilities have restarted, the cumulative impact of overlapping disruptions has kept regional supply relatively constrained. Improving plant availability is expected to gradually ease procurement pressure, although the supply recovery may remain gradual as producers restore stable operating rates and inventories.
The Asian Methyl Methacrylate (MMA) market is facing tighter supply conditions as multiple production facilities across China and Singapore experienced maintenance-related disruptions and reduced operating rates during August and September 2026. The overlapping constraints reduced regional production flexibility and placed greater emphasis on available inventories and alternative supply sources. Although some facilities have since returned to production, the cumulative impact of these disruptions continued to influence MMA availability across the region. 
In China, Zhejiang Petrochemical Company’s Zhoushan facility was taken offline for maintenance on August 20 and returned to production on September 15, temporarily removing around 7,500 tonnes per month of MMA capacity from the market. Earlier, Zibo Qixiang Tengda Chemical Co., Ltd. in Shandong Province had entered maintenance on August 1 before restarting on August 20. The successive disruptions reduced domestic supply during August and contributed to the tightening trend that extended into September. 
The supply pressure was more prolonged in Singapore, where Sumitomo Chemical Asia Pte Ltd’s Jurong Island facility operated at a significantly reduced rate after the disruption began on August 1, with the plant returning to operations on September 25. Its total capacity stands at 18,583 tonnes per month, compared with only 3,097 tonnes per month of active capacity during the reduced-rate period. The prolonged loss of production availability restricted regional supply flexibility of MMA and increased the importance of material from other Asian producers. 
Feedstock availability also added another layer of pressure to the MMA supply chain. In South Korea, LG Chem’s Yeosu Acrylic Acid facility faced a reduced operating rate following the maintenance activity initiated on September 1, with operations restored on September 15. The plant has a total capacity of 59,583 tonnes per month and an active capacity of 29,792 tonnes per month. The temporary reduction in Acrylic Acid availability provided additional cost support to MMA producers at a time when the downstream market was already dealing with tighter MMA supply. 
These combined disruptions have kept the Asian MMA market relatively firm despite the restart of several facilities. MMA Ex-Qingdao was assessed at USD 1,745/MT for the week ending September 18, 2026, up 10% from the previous week. The continued increase since early August reflects the effect of reduced regional availability, while higher Acrylic Acid costs have reinforced the upward pressure. 
Supply conditions are expected to gradually improve as affected facilities resume stable production and rebuild availability. The September 25 restart at Sumitomo Chemical should provide additional material to the Asian market, while previously restarted Chinese units can further support supply normalization. However, the recovery is likely to take time as producers restore operating rates and inventories. Consequently, MMA prices may remain supported in the near term, although improving availability could gradually moderate the recent upward momentum. Acrylic Acid costs will remain an important factor in determining the extent of any price correction.

Communities In Schools of the Dallas Region Celebrates 15 Years of Golfing for a Greater Purpose
PressAdvantage
Dallas, Texas – September 24, 2026 – PRESSADVANTAGE – 
Communities In Schools of the Dallas Region (CIS Dallas) will celebrate 15 years of golfing for a greater purpose at its 15th Annual Kids Classic Golf Tournament , taking place Monday, December 7, 2026, at Cowboys Golf Club in Grapevine. Chaired by Karl Schmalz, the milestone tournament will feature a 9:30 a.m. shotgun start and, for the first time in the event’s history, bring supporters together at one of North Texas’ most distinctive golf destinations.
For 15 years, the Kids Classic Golf Tournament has helped CIS Dallas raise critical funds to support students throughout the Dallas region and across North Texas. Event participation helps provide the resources, encouragement and opportunities students need to overcome barriers, remain engaged in their education and build a path toward long-term success.
“This tournament has always been about much more than golf. It is about bringing people together around the belief that every student deserves the opportunity to succeed,” said Karl Schmalz, CIS Dallas Board Member and Kids Classic Golf Tournament Chair. “As we celebrate 15 years and move to Cowboys Golf Club, we are excited to offer an incredible experience while continuing to raise critical support for students across North Texas.”
Founded locally in 1985, Communities In Schools of the Dallas Region is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to surrounding students with a community of support and empowering them to stay in school and achieve in life. CIS Dallas places trained professionals directly on school campuses, where they work alongside educators, administrators, families and community partners to provide coordinated, individualized support to K–12 students.
Through services focused on academics, attendance, behavior and mental health, social services, college and career readiness and basic needs, CIS Dallas addresses challenges that can interfere with a student’s ability to learn. These challenges may include housing instability, food or clothing insecurity, mental health needs, academic difficulties, inconsistent support systems and other circumstances that extend far beyond the classroom.
CIS Dallas currently serves students across 54 schools in 11 North Texas school districts. During the 2025–2026 school year, nearly 6,000 students received individualized case management services from CIS Dallas. Among students served, 99% were promoted to the next grade level, 96% of eligible high school seniors graduated and 100% remained in school.
“Every day, our team sees what students can accomplish when they have someone in their corner who understands their needs and connects them with the right support,” said Dr. Summer Rose, CEO of Communities In Schools of the Dallas Region. “The Kids Classic helps make that work possible. Every golfer, sponsor and partner is investing directly in students and helping ensure that challenges outside the classroom do not prevent them from reaching their full potential.”
This year’s 15th anniversary will offer a new experience for longtime supporters and first-time participants. Cowboys Golf Club recently underwent a multimillion-dollar renovation and features a redesigned course, a state-of-the-art driving range with Toptracer technology and the unique atmosphere of the world’s only NFL-themed golf club. The new setting gives CIS Dallas an opportunity to celebrate the tournament’s history while elevating the experience for the golfers, sponsors and community partners who make its impact possible.
CIS Dallas is also partnering with Mixed Media Creations (MMC) as the dedicated creative partner for this year’s tournament. The Dallas-Fort Worth full-service marketing and design studio will bring its expertise in branding, design, storytelling, and marketing to the event, helping elevate the tournament experience, strengthen sponsor visibility, and communicate the impact supporters are helping create for students. MMC works with businesses, nonprofits, and community organizations through a collaborative approach that combines creative strategy with purposeful design.
The mission of Communities In Schools of the Dallas Region (CIS) is to surround students with a community of support, empowering them to stay in school and achieve in life. CIS was founded in 1985 to improve the high school dropout rate in the Dallas area by providing academic, attendance, basic needs, and other support to students in local public schools. Today, in partnership with 11 school districts, CIS serves 54 Elementary, Middle, and High School campuses to serve 5,000 students who have been labeled “at-risk.”

What's Driving Demand for Ouster's Rev8 OS1 Max Digital Lidar?
3 min read 
Ouster, Inc. OUST, a provider of sensing and perception technologies for Physical AI, is seeing strong customer adoption of its Rev8 OS1 Max native-color digital lidar. Payload integrators and drone manufacturers in the aerial mapping market are selecting the sensor for applications including utility corridor inspections, infrastructure monitoring and defense. 
Ouster’s Rev8 OS1 Max addresses key challenges in aerial mapping by combining broad coverage with high-resolution data. Powered by the L4 Max chip, the sensor features 256 channels of 3D range data and native 48-bit color, allowing operators to maintain detail when flying at higher altitudes. It can detect narrow objects such as power lines, wires and branches with greater clarity, while its spot size is up to 50% smaller than the previous Rev7 generation. With a range of up to 200 meters at 10% reflectivity, the sensor supports mapping at typical altitudes of 80 to 120 meters. 
The Rev8 OS1 Max delivers ±0.25 cm 1σ precision and ±1.25 cm accuracy, representing a twofold improvement over Rev7. Its 256 vertical channels and up to 4K horizontal resolution help maintain point density at higher flight speeds, enabling more efficient corridor surveys. As a native-color lidar, it captures RGB and 3D data through the same sensor, reducing parallax and calibration requirements. 
The sensor also offers IP68 and IP69K protection, 100 G shock resistance and operation from -40°C to +85°C. Ouster’s U.S.-developed sensors comply with FY2025 NDAA supply-chain requirements and include BABA-certified options. Beyond aerial mapping, Flyability is evaluating the Rev8 OS0 for color 3D mapping in hazardous, GPS-denied environments. OUST currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). The company collaborated with more than 50 embodied AI companies worldwide for its JT128 lidar and ranked No. 1 in China’s humanoid and quadruped robot lidar market, according to GGII. Hesai also captured a 44% share of China’s long-range ADAS lidar market in June 2026. Meanwhile, Hesai’s Picasso 6D SPAD-SoC reached the SOP-ready stage, with Picasso-equipped ETX lidar undergoing customer validation and advancing toward RFI and RFQ discussions with global automakers and robotaxi operators. 
Aeva Technologies, Inc. AEVA is positioned to benefit as lidar expands into higher-level ADAS and autonomy applications. In June, Bendix selected Aeva’s 4D lidar and perception software for its next-generation Level 2+ commercial-vehicle ADAS system. Bendix’s current solution is available on most North American Class 8 platforms, representing a roughly 300,000-unit annual truck market and extending Aeva’s opportunity into high-volume Level 2+ applications.

Aircraft Bye Aerospace completes first flight of all-electric eFlyer 2 trainer 
By Ian Molyneaux Edited By Emma Yates-Badley 
September 24, 2026, 17:30 GMT+03:00 
2 minute read
f 
x 
in 
Bye Aerospace 
Bye Aerospace successfully completed the first flight of its all-electric eFlyer 2 aircraft, designed specifically for the flight training market.
On September 24, 2026, Bye Aerospace said its eFlyer 2 took off from Centennial Airport (APA) near Denver, Colorado, flown by Chief Test Pilot Elliot Seguin.
During the test flight, Bye Aerospace conducted an initial evaluation of the aircraft’s handling qualities, aerodynamic characteristics, and system performance, while collecting data to support the next phase of flight testing.
“First flights are always significant moments for any new aircraft program. This team has worked hard and they will remember this achievement for a long time,” Seguin said. “The eFlyer 2 handled well during the flight and validated the work the engineering team has put into designing and testing the aircraft over the past several years.”
According to Bye Aerospace, the eFlyer 2 has a safety-focused design incorporating an advanced electric propulsion system and a lightweight composite airframe.
The company said that the aircraft can reduce operating costs by up to 80% while eliminating in-flight emissions.
The flight signifies the launch of the aircraft’s flight test program as it progresses towards Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) certification and eventually customer deliveries.
“The first flight of eFlyer 2 exceeded all of our expectations in terms of aerodynamics, handling, propulsion and overall performance—and there were no maintenance discrepancies during the flight,” Rod Zastrow, CEO of Bye Aerospace, said. “This program is an important step in demonstrating that electric aircraft can deliver disruptive operational cost advantages while maintaining the performance, safety, and handling qualities required for real world training environments.”
He added that the flight represents a “milestone” for the future of electric aviation by helping “reduce the oftentimes prohibitive costs of flight training”.
The company said that the eFlyer 2 enables customers such as flight schools to “break free from high and uncertain fossil fuel prices, and crippling engine overhaul backlogs”.
Bye Aerospace’s partners and customers
Bye Aerospace’s partners include Safran Electrical and Power, magniX, Siemens, Toray, Composite Approach, Garmin, Sensenich Propeller, Electro.Aero, Flying S, M4 Engineering, ACME Aero, and Risse Racing.
Earlier this month, the FAA awarded Bye with a Special Airworthiness Certificate for eFlyer 2.
Bye Aerospace’s orderbook for the two-seat eFlyer 2 and four-seat eFlyer 4 stands at over 1,000 aircraft.
Buyers include Spartan College of Aeronautics & Technology, Skyborne Academy, Flex Air Flight School, and KLM Academy (NL).

Rio Tinto to expand metals trading beyond own output
Cecilia Jamasmie | September 24, 2026 | 4:46 am 
Markets   Suppliers & Equipment   Top Companies   Asia   Australia   Europe   Aluminum   Copper   Iron Ore   Lithium   
Rio Tinto produces alumina as a core intermediate step in its vertically integrated aluminum business. ( Image courtesy of Rio Tinto. ) 
Rio Tinto (ASX, LON: RIO) plans to expand its metals trading business into third-party material and derivatives as chief executive Simon Trott seeks to squeeze more value from the world’s second-largest miner.
The initiative, Bloomberg reported , would mark a shift for Rio Tinto, which has historically focused on marketing its own production and operates a much smaller trading business than Glencore (LON: GLEN).
Glencore’s extensive trading network was one attraction during unsuccessful takeover talks between the companies over the past two years.
Rio Tinto does not intend to replicate standalone commodity trading houses, but is considering a significant expansion of its existing commercial business under chief commercial officer Bold Baatar, according to Bloomberg .
The push could give Rio greater flexibility to profit from regional supply imbalances and spare capacity across its global operations while broadening a commercial business that remains modest compared with major commodity traders.
Trading opportunities 
Rio Tinto is considering more third-party trading in markets where its existing assets could provide an advantage. That includes alumina, where the company has surpluses in some regions and shortages in others.
In North America, its Kennecott operations have spare copper smelting capacity, creating opportunities to handle additional material. Rio Tinto could also trade copper cathode and related products such as sulphuric acid.
The commercial team currently has about 20 traders and could add several more as the company expands the operation.
The strategy fits with Trott’s broader overhaul of Rio Tinto since he became CEO last year . He has laid out plans to simplify the company, sell assets, cut costs and improve returns.
Rio Tinto is also in talks with Dutch multinational Vitol Group over a potential freight and logistics joint venture, another move that could reshape how the miner handles its global supply chain.

Particles for Humanity and Hexagon Nutrition validate heat-stable vitamin A in India
24 Sep 2026 | By Benjamin Ferrer 
Key takeaways
Particles for Humanity has validated its heat- and humidity-resistant vitamin A ingredient (Vit A+), with Hexagon Nutrition transferring its commercial manufacturing to India.
Each commercial batch produces enough Vit A+ to fortify 600 million servings of food staples like bouillon, flour, and sugar.
In stability tests, the fortified ingredient retained three times more vitamin A after 12 months in high heat and humidity compared to commercial alternatives.
(Image credit: Particles for Humanity). 
Particles for Humanity has completed the commercial-scale process validation for its PFH-VAP ingredient, which is vitamin A palmitate (VAP) coated in a material that protects it from heat and humidity during processing, transport, and cooking. The stabilized nutrient will be marketed as Vit A+ for large-scale food fortification. 
The process validation demonstrates that it can be produced consistently at commercial scale while maintaining the key product attributes established during development.
Hexagon Nutrition completed this validation campaign in India and has finalized the transfer of Vit A+ manufacturing from Lesaffre Ingredients Services’ French facility to a site in India.
“Completing this manufacturing transfer is a major milestone in the development of PFH-VAP and brings us one step closer to making this technology broadly available through food fortification programs,” says Sherri Oberg, co-founder and CEO of Particles for Humanity.
“This achievement reflects years of collaboration among scientists, engineers, and manufacturing partners committed to reducing the burden of vitamin A deficiency. We are excited to see PFH-VAP positioned for the next phase of commercialization.”
Following this manufacturing transfer and validation, Particles for Humanity and Hexagon Nutrition aim to expand the use of Vit A+ in fortification programs for vulnerable populations, including food staples such as bouillon, flour, and sugar.
Stability throughout food prep 
Particles for Humanity developed Vit A+ to improve the stability of vitamin A during storage and cooking under conditions common in low- and middle-income countries where deficiencies of the nutrient remain high.
According to the supplier, each commercial-scale batch will produce enough Vit A+ to fortify 600 million servings of food. The company anticipates this will enable more cost-effective production, helping expand access in regions requiring food fortification.
Following the 2025 announcement of their partnership, Particles for Humanity and Hexagon Nutrition worked together to transfer manufacturing knowledge and prepare Vit A+ for commercial supply.
Vikram Kelkar, managing director of Hexagon Nutrition, says improving nutrition through innovation is central to the company’s mission.
“The completion of process validation demonstrates that Vit A+ can be manufactured reliably at commercial scale and reflects the strong collaboration between our organizations. We look forward to working with partners across the food fortification ecosystem to expand access to stable vitamin A.”
Advancing fortification programs 
In one previous demonstrative study of Vit A’s stability, researchers incorporated the ingredient into bouillon cubes , a staple food consumed widely across West Africa. After 12 months of high-temperature, high-humidity storage, the fortified bouillon retained three times more vitamin A than that containing a commercial alternative.
Other suppliers have also made strides to raise the bar on vitamin A performance. For instance, dsm-firmenich developed a dry form of vitamin A designed to enrich baby formula nutrition without the stability issues associated with the essential nutrient. The nutrient is particularly essential for the development of healthy vision in infants.
“Golden rice” is another example of successful vitamin A fortification efforts. The genetically modified variety of the staple crop contains genes from daffodils and bacteria, developed at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology. These fortify the rice plant with enzymes that allow it to produce beta-carotene, which the human body converts into vitamin A.

Qualcomm to acquire robotics software firm PickNik
Qualcomm's Dragonwing robotics platform is set to gain closer integration with PickNik's open-source MoveIt manipulation framework · Verdict · mrinalpal/Shutterstock.com. 
BV Swagath 
September 24, 2026 3 min read 
QCOM 
+1.78% 
Qualcomm Technologies has agreed to acquire Colorado-based robotics software company PickNik, which develops and maintains MoveIt, an open-source robotics manipulation framework. 
The acquisition is designed to reinforce Qualcomm's commitment to an open robotics ecosystem. It aims to give developers the tools and frameworks needed to move more efficiently from early-stage research and prototyping through to deployment and production at scale. 
Closing of the transaction remains subject to customary conditions. 
MoveIt is set to remain open-source and will also gain closer integration with Qualcomm's Dragonwing robotics platforms. This is expected to create a more direct route for developers between AI models such as vision-language-action and vision-language systems and the planning, manipulation and real-time control functions needed to run a robot. 
Qualcomm executive vice president and automotive, industrial and embedded IoT, and robotics group general manager Nakul Duggal said: "Robotics is one of the most exciting frontiers of physical AI, and software is the connective tissue that turns great hardware into great robots. 
"PickNik has earned tremendous trust within the global robotics community through its stewardship of MoveIt and its commitment to open-source innovation." 
MoveIt is built on the Robot Operating System (ROS) and is used by developers, students, researchers and commercial robotics organisations. Its applications span industrial automation, service robotics, mobile manipulation and the emerging field of physical AI. 
Qualcomm has said it intends to keep MoveIt open-source under its existing licence, with roadmaps continuing to be shaped by the community. The company also plans to maintain support for the framework across hardware from other suppliers, preserving MoveIt's ability to work independently of any single robot, compute platform or sensor set. 
Both Qualcomm and PickNik are founding members of the Open Source Robotics Alliance. Qualcomm has also said it will continue to back Space ROS, a version of the ROS framework hardened for demanding applications such as space missions. 
PickNik founder and chief product officer Dave Coleman said: "Since our founding, PickNik's mission has been to provide industries with a powerful, open platform that accelerates innovation and development of advanced robotics, well beyond traditional factories. 
"Joining Qualcomm Technologies will allow us to accelerate that mission, expand investment in MoveIt as a leading AI training platform for robotics, and deliver even more value to developers while preserving the openness, community collaboration, and cross-platform support that have always been central to our approach." 
Story Continues 
PickNik CEO Dave Grant said MoveIt was "entering an exciting new chapter with the resources and support to help expand its impact", adding that the company looked forward to "building on MoveIt's momentum" as part of Qualcomm. 
As part of the deal, MoveIt, PickNik's commercial MoveIt Pro platform and future PickNik technologies are due to be more closely integrated with Dragonwing. 
Qualcomm said this should let developers draw on Dragonwing's AI, heterogeneous computing, connectivity and real-time robotics functions when building robots. It added that the aim is to give developers dedicated support for MoveIt's motion planning, manipulation, perception and kinematics tools, helping speed the move from prototype to production. 
Separately, MoveIt is also being extended to Arduino hardware, beginning with the Arduino VENTUNO Q boards. Qualcomm said the goal is to widen access to advanced robotics, edge AI and heterogeneous computing for a broader developer base. 
The semiconductor major added that the integration is intended to shorten the path from prototype to production-ready robots for what it described as millions of developers. 
Prior to this, Qualcomm announced the acquisition of AI-native software platform Modular in June this year. The all-stock transaction was completed in the following month.

content_text:
Cognex to acquire RealSense for $500M in factory edge AI deal 
Muhammad Zulhusni 
24th September 2026
Share this story:
Tags:
ai 
edge ai 
IoT 
machine learning 
Manufacturing 
robotics 
sensor 
Categories::
AI & Intelligence 
Computer Vision & Sensors 
Features 
M&A, Investment & Startups 
Manufacturing & Industry 
On-Device Machine Learning 
Robotics & Automation 
Cognex has agreed to acquire RealSense for about $500 million in cash, adding 3D depth-sensing and robotic perception technology to its industrial machine-vision portfolio. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.
Cognex plans to fund the acquisition using cash and investments already on its balance sheet.
RealSense was established within Intel in 2014 and became an independent company in 2025. The business is expected to generate between $80 million and $90 million in revenue this year, according to Cognex.
Before the transaction closes, RealSense will separate its facial authentication product line into an independent company. Cognex will acquire the remaining depth-camera and robotic-perception business.
From fixed inspection to robotic perception
Cognex said its existing machine-vision systems are used in controlled industrial applications to identify and inspect products, take precise measurements, and guide fixed-arm robots. RealSense extends those capabilities into applications where robots use depth information to recognise their surroundings, judge distance, avoid obstacles, and navigate changing environments.
“We enable machines to identify, inspect, measure and guide while RealSense enables them to perceive and navigate their surroundings,” Cognex CEO Matt Moschner said.
The Association for Advancing Automation describes adaptive robotics as combining machine vision, sensors, AI, and real-time computing so robots can respond to changing conditions without extensive reprogramming. Conventional industrial robots typically operate in structured environments where movements are programmed and parts arrive at expected positions.
Cognex said its outlook for the robotic-perception market is based largely on vision-guided fixed-arm robots and autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), where adoption is more established. The company considers quadrupeds and humanoid robots longer-term opportunities rather than necessary to its core growth expectations for the acquisition.
RealSense’s industrial technology includes cameras that generate depth information to help machines determine the position and distance of objects in their surroundings. Its systems support applications including robot guidance, part recognition, measurement, tracking, and safety monitoring.
The company’s D555 depth camera connects to industrial Ethernet networks using Power over Ethernet (PoE), allowing power and data to travel through the same connection. The camera also includes onboard vision processing rather than operating solely as an image sensor connected to a separate computing system.
Its RealSense Vision SoC V5 combines stereo disparity processing and motion estimation with a vision digital signal processor and image signal processor. The D555 also supports native on-camera people detection.
RealSense says image processing and inference can take place on cameras based on its V5 architecture. The D555 can also publish data directly into ROS 2 networks over Ethernet, allowing depth information to feed into robotics software without first passing through a USB-connected host.
The D585 also uses a V5 system-on-chip with a depth engine, image signal processor, vision DSP, and quad-core Arm processor. It offers depth output of up to 90 frames per second, while RealSense lists on-camera person detection as a beta feature at launch.
This allows depth calculation and some vision workloads to be handled on the camera before information is passed into the wider robot software and control system.
Existing RealSense deployments provide examples of how that architecture is being used on production floors. French robotics company Inbolt mounts RealSense D435 depth cameras on industrial robots as part of a system that continuously determines the location of components while a robot is operating.
According to a RealSense case study, the Inbolt system can adjust when bins move or conveyors remain in motion instead of relying only on a previously determined component position. RealSense reports perception-to-motion latency below 80 milliseconds, with the technology deployed across more than 70 factories.
According to RealSense, the system continuously re-localises components while the robot is operating, allowing its motion to be updated when the position of a part changes. This differs from applications where a robot executes a predefined movement based on a fixed or previously measured position.
“RealSense is one of the few 3D cameras that delivers both the point cloud quality we require,” Inbolt COO Albane Dersy said in the case study.
According to a RealSense case study, Italian industrial automation company GEFIT has integrated RealSense depth cameras into its vision platform. The system uses depth data to provide robots with information about objects and people in their workspace for applications including bin picking, human detection, and movement in shared areas.
Bringing more vision processing to the factory edge
Cognex already processes machine-vision workloads on embedded hardware at the edge. Its In-Sight 3900, introduced in May this year, combines image capture, AI processing, and inspection software in a system that can operate without an external PC.
The system uses a dedicated AI processor for local inspection workloads and supports Ethernet connections to PLCs and robots. Cognex said its processing architecture enables deterministic, real-time inspection on production lines.
RealSense’s V5-based cameras perform a different set of workloads on-device, including depth processing and other vision functions used by robotic systems. Cognex described RealSense’s wider technology platform as spanning imaging, custom silicon, 3D vision algorithms, embedded software, and developer tools.
According to Cognex, RealSense has shipped more than one million units. Its software development kit has recorded more than 1.2 million downloads and has approximately 20,000 active developers across four major platforms.
The SDK provides tools for integrating RealSense depth data into robotics and computer-vision applications, including support for ROS and ROS 2.
Cognex estimates the robotic-perception market at about $600 million and expects it to grow by more than 25% annually to approximately $1.6 billion by 2030. The estimates come from Cognex and are not presented as independent market forecasts.
The company expects RealSense to generate between $80 million and $90 million in revenue in 2026. Cognex said the business has approximately 160 employees and more than 70 patents and patent applications.
Cognex has also discussed combining the two companies’ software and processing technologies after the acquisition closes. During its acquisition call, management said newer RealSense devices have enough onboard processing capacity to run vision functions directly on the device.
Moschner said possible integrations include running Cognex-trained AI models and vision tools on RealSense hardware, as well as applying RealSense’s 3D depth-sensing technology to Cognex’s existing machine-vision applications. Cognex has not announced these integrations as commercial products.

Industrial fire breaks out at recycling center in Solvay
September 24, 2026 
An industrial fire broke out at the Weitsman Recycling Center located at 333 Bridge St. in the village of Solvay at around 1 p.m. Wednesday afternoon.
The Solvay Fire Department responded to reports of a scrap pile on fire. When crews arrived on scene, they discovered that one of the large piles of scrap material in the back of the scrap yard had ignited.
Arriving alongside Solvay firefighters was the Taunton Fire Department. While Solvay took charge of the scene, Taunton prepared its aerial master stream, a water hose fixed to the top of an extending ladder, due to the height of the fire.
Once both crews were able to establish a consistent supply of water, the fire was put out using the aerial master stream in under twenty minutes. At this time, the cause of the fire is unknown. No injuries have been reported.

Judges Scientific PLC (JSCIF) (H1 2026) Earnings Call Highlights: Revenue Slumps 21% but Order ...
GuruFocus News 
September 24, 2026 9 min read 
JDG.L 
JSCIF 
This article first appeared on GuruFocus . 
Revenue: Down 21% year over year; like-for-like revenue down 13% excluding the prior-year Geotek coring expedition. 
Adjusted Operating Profit: Down approximately two-thirds, reflecting high operational leverage on lower revenue. 
Adjusted Basic EPS: GBP0.39, down 72% year over year. 
Order Intake: Down 12% in H1; improved to roughly 1% down year to date by late September. 
Cash from Operations: GBP4.3 million, with 90% cash conversion. 
Adjusted Net Debt: Increased by GBP3 million. 
Interim Dividend: Increased 10% to 36 pence per share; dividend cover of 1.1. 
Effective Tax Rate: Expected at 18% for the year, aided by the UK Patent Box scheme. 
Cost Reduction: Approximately GBP2 million of costs removed from underperforming businesses, mainly people costs. 
Return on Total Invested Capital (ROTIC): Declined to around 13%. 
Business Growth: Eight businesses grew in H1; 13 businesses declined. 
Acquisitions: No acquisitions completed in H1 2026. 
Banking Facilities: Two-year extension announced, now maturing July 1, 2030. 
Pension Scheme: Defined benefit pension scheme fully bought out in August 2026; group no longer has responsibility.

Is JSCIF fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. 
JSCIF GF Value chart Release Date: September 23, 2026 
For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript . 
Positive Points 
Order intake momentum has returned, with like-for-like order intake down only 1% year-to-date compared to a 12% decline in H1, and the last four months of orders annualized are at or above budget levels. 
Eight businesses achieved growth in H1, driven by internal initiatives, new product development, and positive market dynamics in industrial sectors such as semiconductor and battery development. 
Cost reduction actions removed nearly GBP2 million from underperforming businesses, primarily through headcount reductions, while protecting innovation and R&D capacity. 
Cash conversion remained strong at 90%, in line with historical expectations, despite significantly lower profitability. 
The interim dividend was increased by 10% to 36 pence per share, reflecting confidence in the group's future and its progressive dividend policy. 
The group extended its banking facilities by two years to July 2030, maintaining a strong balance sheet and covenant headroom. 
Progress was made at underperforming businesses like Fire Testing Technology and Armfield, with new product launches and order intake growth. 
The defined benefit pension scheme was fully bought out, removing a long-standing liability from the balance sheet. 
The effective tax rate is expected to be 18%, benefiting from the UK Patent Box scheme due to continued investment in innovation. 
The acquisition pipeline remains healthy, with a strong deal pool and disciplined approach, despite no acquisitions completed in H1. 
Story Continues 
Negative Points 
H1 revenue declined by 21% year-over-year, or 13% on a like-for-like basis, due to challenging market conditions. 
Adjusted earnings per share plummeted 72% to GBP0.39, reflecting high operational leverage and significant revenue decline. 
Adjusted operating profits dropped by two-thirds, as the high-margin business model amplifies the impact of lower revenue. 
Continued uncertainties in US research funding and delays in China's tax exemption processes negatively impacted orders and revenue. 
Offshore wind investments remained postponed, with no expected improvement in the near term, affecting companies like GDS Instruments. 
The next Geotek coring expedition is now not expected before 2028, delaying a significant revenue opportunity. 
Return on total invested capital (ROTIC) declined to around 13%, well below historical levels, due to weaker performance. 
Adjusted net debt increased by GBP3 million, and gearing rose as a consequence of the weaker H1 performance. 
Dividend cover for the interim dividend is only 1.1, which is not sustainable in isolation and is driven by the low H1 result. 
Execution risks remain for H2, with a significant Q4 weighting in revenue and potential delays in high-value instrument shipments. 
Q & A Highlights 
Q : Once the balance sheet has deleveraged further, has the board considered adding opportunistic share buybacks alongside the 10% dividend progression, particularly during quieter M&A periods? A : CFO Bradley Ormsby stated that share buybacks have been considered and are seen as a viable use of capital allocation, but not necessarily at the moment. He noted that using increased debt for buybacks is not an excellent use of capital currently, and the group needs to deleverage with improved performance first. CEO Tim Prestidge added that while buybacks have been increasingly raised by investors, the board concluded it was not the most effective way of returning cash to investors, though special dividends have been used in the past and may be considered again. 
Q : You reaffirm the current full year market expectations. Could you please explain the key assumptions behind this guidance, particularly regarding second half revenue, operating margins and Q3 order intake? A : CFO Bradley Ormsby explained that Q3 order intake has been in line with expectations, providing a higher volume to deliver in Q4. To meet market expectations, the group needs to deliver 160 pence in H2, which it has done before. The lower cost base in H2 compared to last year, benefits from the Patent Box scheme reducing the effective tax rate, and operating leverage on higher volumes with good visibility are key assumptions. He noted it is very much Q4 weighted and not without risk, but the orders are largely in hand. 
Q : You noted a GBP2 million reduction in the cost base of underperforming businesses during H1. How much of this represents permanent structural overhead reduction versus temporary variable cost containment? And did any of these measures require cutting back on active R&D or engineering capacity? A : CEO Tim Prestidge stated that the majority of the cost reduction related to headcount costs at underperforming businesses, with some structural reductions made where previous investments had not delivered expected growth. Group Commercial Director Ian Wilcock added that at FTT and Armfield, cost reductions were done in a way that protected core innovation, allowing new product launches while still reducing the overall cost envelope. 
Q : What share of your North American revenue is directly tied to federally funded labs versus commercial customers? Are those labs telling you 2027 budgets are recovering, or should we model North America at the current lower base? A : CFO Bradley Ormsby explained that the group cannot measure this precisely, but historically around half of revenue comes from the academic world and around a sixth from indirectly financed entities like the NIH. In the US, somewhere between half and two-thirds of revenue is affected by federal funding. Last year, around 25% of total revenue was generated in the US, with about two-thirds of that exposed to federal funding uncertainties. He could not give a clearer number due to the complexity of funding sources. 
Q : Of the revenue lost in China this half, how much do you think comes back versus is gone for good? A : CFO Bradley Ormsby said the vast majority is about delay rather than lost business. He cited a significant distributor order expected in H1 that has been pushed to Q4 due to the 13% tax exemption process. He does not believe much has been lost, but delivery of existing orders and routine orders have been pushed to the right, with some possibly coming in 2027. Progress is happening as existing orders are now being asked to be delivered. 
Q : Where is the order intake inflection coming from? Is it universities or industrial activity? A : CEO Tim Prestidge said it is a real mix, with pretty big-ticket items across multiple businesses and sectors, including scientific instrumentation, batteries, and semicon. He emphasized this is not a general rising tide or recovery in the scientific instrumentation market, but rather specific high-value opportunities that have been in the pipeline coming through. Some high-value scientific instrumentation is still being ordered from the US where research groups are finding ways to secure funding. 
Q : You've explained why North America is down, but Europe is down even more. So why is that, and when do you expect Europe to recover? A : CEO Tim Prestidge explained that Europe was down 20% in H1 versus North America down 7%. The decline in Europe was relatively broad, including at OEMs that supply into the US, and there was a significant impact from a one-off non-recurring industrial order last year that did not repeat. North America benefited from region-specific non-academic recovery in order intake at some businesses, which offset the federal funding challenges. 
Q : Aside from recent disruption, what impact, if any, will the new Chinese procurement processes have on the group in the medium term? A : CEO Tim Prestidge stated the new processes are replacing previous ones and are not expected to have a long-term impact. The impact has been delays, not lost orders, with shipments postponed and orders delayed until processes resolved. Group Commercial Director Ian Wilcock agreed, noting bidding processes have been frozen by many customers, but there is no indication orders will drop off, and a decent recovery is anticipated next year in the Chinese market. 
Q : The delay in a new coring expedition seems longer than usual. If that is correct, what is the reason for this? A : CEO Tim Prestidge explained that the customer has had funding approved but elected to reverse the order of projects, so the coring expedition will follow another expedition. Geotek continues to follow other opportunities in a vibrant field, but no coring expedition is currently expected in 2027. CFO Bradley Ormsby added these projects are incredibly expensive, usually tens of millions, and timing is out of the group's control, though Geotek is the only company that can do the pressure coring for gas hydrates. 
Q : Are current markets and uncertainties leading to lower valuation multiples for potential acquisition targets in the scientific instruments niche? A : CEO Tim Prestidge said no, that is not the experience. The group looks to acquire successful businesses to keep forever, which is a high bar. Owners of successful businesses coming off a tough year may have a number in mind relative to prior performance, which can imply higher rather than lower multiples. The group is seeing a greater level of quality businesses coming into active deal opportunities, but no reduction in multiple expectations, and remains able to attract acquisitions within its disciplined multiples. 
Q : Does the improved order intake from minus 12% in H1 to minus 1% year to date imply Q3 orders are roughly plus 20%?

€100 million investment: supporting hydrogen production plant of Arkema France put into operation
2026-09-24 09:52:11 
Source:ChemNet 
中文 
On September 22nd, specialty materials company Arkema held a inauguration ceremony for its new hydrogen production plant at its Jarrie facility in Isère, France, marking a major milestone in the site's restructuring plan. This plant adopts the steam methane reforming (SMR) process and will specifically supply hydrogen feedstock for the Jarrie site.
Arkema is a leading global producer of hydrogen peroxide, with four production bases across Europe and North America. The Jarrie plant is the group's largest hydrogen peroxide production base and holds a core position in its global hydrogen peroxide industrial network.
The total investment of this project amounts to approximately 10 million euros , and it is the first phase of a large-scale investment plan that will run until 2028. The plant successfully completed its commissioning and went into production on schedule in July 2026 . The smooth realization of this project benefited from the close collaboration between the site team and its partners.
According to the site restructuring plan announced in January 2025 , the Jarrie site will focus its business on three strategic product lines: hydrogen peroxide, chlorates and perchlorates . New projects will also be launched successively between 2026 and 2027 as part of the site renovation works, to further optimize the on-site hydrogen pipeline network and raw material supply system.
The hydrogen peroxide produced at the Jarrie site has a wide range of downstream applications, including pulp and paper manufacturing, the electronics industry, and chemical synthesis intermediates. The plant also produces sodium chlorate and sodium perchlorate, serving water treatment and aerospace sectors, with Ariane Group being its long-term core customer.
Mathieu Brisson, plant director of the Jarrie facility, stated: "Hydrogen peroxide is a classic product of the Jarrie site. The inauguration of this hydrogen production unit is a key step in the site's transformation. Going forward, we will continue to advance project implementation, optimize hydrogen supply, and consolidate the site's competitiveness in hydrogen peroxide and chlorate businesses."

content_text:
(Image: ABB) 
ABB said on Sept. 23 that it has launched Infinitus, an integrated direct current (DC) solution designed to meet the high-density power demands of artificial intelligence (AI) data centers.
Infinitus is an integrated solution spanning the entire data center power infrastructure from the power source to server racks. It uses solid-state transformers (SSTs) and DC distribution and protection technologies to reduce power conversion stages, installation footprint and energy consumption. The solution can also be deployed in hybrid configurations combining conventional alternating current (AC) systems with DC.
ABB has been jointly developing an 800-volt (V) DC power architecture with Nvidia since October last year for gigawatt (GW)-scale AI data centers. The project aims to improve power delivery efficiency and scalability as next-generation AI chips require higher power density.
Key Infinitus products are scheduled to enter production within the next 12 months. The first DC-based data center using the full product portfolio is expected to be built within two to three years.
"Infinitus is a solution that supports the power delivery required by next-generation AI chips, from DC to AC-DC hybrid configurations," said Giampiero Frisio, president of ABB's Electrification business.

content_text:
Eco&Dream's Saemangeum campus. (Photo: THE ELEC) 
Eco&Dream will supply 17.7 billion won worth of high-nickel nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) precursors to Umicore. The materials will be used in batteries for electric vehicles produced in North America.
Eco&Dream said in a regulatory filing on Sept. 23 that it signed an NCM precursor supply contract with Umicore. The contracted volume will be supplied during October.
The contract is worth about 17.7 billion won, equivalent to about 12.5% of last year's annual revenue of 141.9 billion won. It represents 48.6% of the company's first-half revenue of 36.4 billion won this year.
Precursors are a key raw material for cathode materials, which determine battery performance. Cathode materials account for about 40% of battery costs, while precursors make up about 70% of cathode material costs. The precursors supplied by Eco&Dream will be used to produce Umicore's cathode materials. They will then be used by a South Korean battery maker to produce cells for electric vehicles manufactured in North America.
Eco&Dream said precursor orders are increasing as North American customers draw down inventories and electric vehicle demand recovers. The company expects annual precursor shipments to reach a record high next year.
The company is also expanding its product lineup. In addition to existing high-nickel precursors, it is developing lithium-manganese-rich (LMR) and high-voltage mid-nickel (HVM) precursors. It is also building a pilot line for lithium iron phosphate (LFP) precursors and plans to pursue customer evaluations.
"As North American electric vehicle demand enters a stabilization phase, we expect to post record-high shipments next year," an Eco&Dream official said. "We will diversify our products and markets to meet growing demand."

title: Merck reveals study success, and possible safety worries, for eye drug hopeful - BioPharma Dive

content_text:
Merck reveals study success, and possible safety worries, for eye drug hopeful
A medicine acquired in a $1.3 billion buyout came through in the first of two pivotal studies in diabetic macular edema, though language regarding the drug’s safety stirred debate among analysts.
Published Sept. 24, 2026
By 
Kristin Jensen
Share 
Copy link 
Email 
LinkedIn 
X/Twitter 
Facebook 
Print 
License 
Add us on Google 
Merck & Co. logo displayed on the exterior of their research facility in San Francisco, Calif., on Sep. 21, 2020.
Alamy 
Dive Brief:
Merck & Co. on Thursday said a drug it’s developing to treat diabetic macular edema succeeded in a late-stage trial , while also noting some potential safety concerns.
In the late-stage “Brunello” trial, the drug, called remigromig, reached the mark of “non-inferiority” when measuring patients’ visual acuity compared with those given Roche’s Lucentis , Merck said. But the company also said it’s conducting further analyses to understand higher rates of proliferative diabetic retinopathy, bleeding inside the eye and treatment discontinuations among those given remigromig.
The New Jersey-based drugmaker acquired remigromig in a $1.3 billion takeover of privately held EyeBio two years ago . The medicine, then known as Restoret, had already delivered positive results in a Phase 1b/2a study in patients with diabetic macular edema as well as those with the “wet” form of age-related macular degeneration.
Dive Insight:
Remigromig is one of many moving pieces in Merck’s plan to reach $70 billion in annual sales next decade even as it weathers the loss of market exclusivity for the top-selling cancer medicine Keytruda. The injection is part of a new class of medicines designed to restore the blood-retinal barrier by targeting a signaling pathway known as Wnt. 
While Merck got a modest 1% bump in its stock price on the results in early trading Thursday, shares of eye drug specialist Surrozen doubled after the announcement. The company is developing a similar treatment that analysts say has blockbuster potential.
For Merck, the results were “mixed,” RBC Capital Markets analyst Trung Huynh wrote in a note to clients. The efficacy results were encouraging and offer validation for targeting Wnt with a drug, he wrote. “However, the new safety disclosures give us some concern,” he added.
Another analyst, Evercore ISI’s Umer Raffat, was less worried. He noted that one-off vitreous hemorrhages have been seen in other eye drug trials. “This disclosure is made in classic Merck conservative fashion,” Raffat wrote to clients. In his opinion, “this is not a reflection of something bad that has happened.”
Merck didn’t release details in its announcement on Thursday, saying full results from the first year of the trial would be presented at a medical meeting on Oct. 10. Researchers are continuing to follow patients who in their second year will have more individualized treatments, potentially reducing the frequency of the eye injections administered every four weeks in the first year.
The drugmaker is also evaluating remigromig in a second pivotal trial focused on diabetic macular edema, as well as a Phase 2 proof-of-concept study in two other eye conditions. And Merck has also moved a different ophthalmic medicine acquired from EyeBio, MK-8748, into late-stage testing as well.
Traditionally known as a powerhouse in cancer, heart disease and vaccines, Merck has made several forays into the world of ophthalmology to expand its pipeline. A partnership with NGM Biopharmaceuticals on a geographic atrophy drug fizzled out after disappointing study results in 2022 . In 2024, the company moved onto the EyeBio acquisition, which came with the potential for an additional $1.7 billion in milestone payments on top of the initial $1.3 billion in cash.

PR Newswire
