Have an account? Log in . 
Do you fancy flying on the world's largest passenger jet ?
The Airbus A380 has awed passengers for nearly 20 years. With a 262-foot wingspan, the superjumbo jet wouldn't fit on an NFL field.
Business Insider has compiled all the routes that it will fly this winter, based on Cirium data for November's schedule.
You can search for different cities in this table, then scroll down for more details about the airlines operating the A380.
Airbus spent decades developing the double-decker airplane as an answer to the Boeing 747 . It announced the project in 1990, but the A380 didn't enter service until 2007.
It has had a turbulent life ever since, falling in and out of popularity.
The European planemaker expected high demand for enormous aircraft due to the rise of airport megahubs like Dubai. It was ideal for Emirates, which operates the overwhelming majority of A380s.
However, many airlines preferred to fly point-to-point. Twin-jet aircraft like the Boeing 777 and Airbus A350 offer plenty of seats, greater flexibility, and lower operating costs.
The COVID-19 pandemic also prompted many airlines to rethink their strategies amid cost pressures. Air France and Malaysia Airlines were among those to retire all their A380s.
Airbus built the last new A380 in 2021.
While COVID was a major blow, many airlines fell back in love with the superjumbo when lockdowns lifted.
Lufthansa retired all 14 of its A380s during the pandemic but has brought back eight of them since 2022. Etihad Airways reactivated six jets, too.
Meanwhile, Qantas restarted A380 flights between Sydney and Dallas/Fort Worth last August, for the first time since the pandemic. A year later, though, the Australian flag carrier said it was bringing forward its retirement of the planes to 2028.
Back in 2017, there were more than 10,000 flights a month operated by the A380. While that has since fallen to 7,500 for November, it seems there is still some life left in the superjumbo.
1. Emirates
Emirates' A380s have a bar on board. 
Bloomberg/Getty Images 
Dubai's airline is by far the world's largest operator of the A380, with over nine times as many as any other operator.
Emirates has a total of 117, of which 85 are actively flying as of September, according to fleet data from ch-aviation. 13 are in storage, and 19 are undergoing maintenance.
Like its rival Middle Eastern airlines, Emirates' A380 is highly luxurious — with business-class passengers able to visit the bar or even book a shower.
The airline's president, Tim Clark, told Business Insider last year that he'd like Airbus to build a new version of the A380 with more fuel-efficient engines.
Emirates' plethora of planes comes with a similarly broad route map. Brace yourself for an extensive list.
Emirates flies the A380 between Dubai and Amman, Jordan; Amsterdam; Auckland, New Zealand; Bangkok; Barcelona; Bengaluru, India; Birmingham, England; Brisbane, Australia; Cairo; Casablanca, Morocco; Copenhagen, Denmark; Denpasar, Indonesia; Düsseldorf, Germany; Frankfurt, Germany; Glasgow, Scotland; Guangzhou, China; Hong Kong; Houston; Istanbul; Jeddah, Saudi Arabia; Johannesburg; Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia; London; Los Angeles; Madrid; Manchester, England; Mauritius; Melbourne, Australia; Milan; Moscow; Mumbai, India; Munich; New Delhi; New York; Nice, France; Osaka, Japan; Paris; Perth, Australia; Prague; Rome; San Francisco; São Paulo; Seoul; Shanghai; Singapore; Sydney; Taipei; Tokyo; Toronto; Vienna; Washington, DC; and Zurich.
Emirates also operates three fifth-freedom flights with the A380, between Christchurch, New Zealand, and Sydney; Bangkok and Hong Kong; and Milan and New York.
2. British Airways
British Airways is retrofitting a new first-class suite for the A380. 
Pete Syme/Business Insider 
British Airways has 12 Airbus A380s. According to ch-aviation, two of those are undergoing maintenance, and another is in storage, as of September.
As part of a $9 billion "transformation program," BA is retrofitting its A380s with an upgraded first class.
"The A380 is an important part of our fleet and rightfully, incredibly popular with our customers," Neil Chernoff, BA's chief planning and strategy officer, previously told Business Insider.
BA flies the A380 between London Heathrow and Johannesburg, Miami, San Francisco, and Singapore
3. Singapore Airlines
Two first-class suites on a Singapore Airlines A380. 
ROSLAN RAHMAN/AFP via Getty Images 
Singapore Airlines also has a fleet of 12 double-decker jets, having retired seven due to the pandemic.
The carrier is one of just 10 to receive a five-star rating from Skytrax. It named Singapore Airlines' business class the second-best, behind Qatar Airways, but the best for first class.
The airline offers enormous suites on its A380s, each with an armchair and a bed. Two of these can also be uniquely combined to create a double bed.
Singapore flies the A380 between Singapore Changi Airport and Auckland, London, Melbourne, Mumbai, New Delhi, Shanghai, and Sydney.
4. Qatar Airways
A Qatar Airways Airbus A380. 
Nicolas Economou/NurPhoto via Getty Images 
Qatar Airways cleaned up at last year's Skytrax awards, winning both best airline and best business class.
Like Emirates, the airline's A380 includes a bar for business-class passengers. It also has huge bathrooms, but lacks showers.
Qatar's A380s, perhaps surprisingly, don't feature its flagship business-class product, the QSuite, which you'll find on the A350, Boeing 777, and 787.
Following delays to the Boeing 777X , Qatar reversed plans to retire the A380.
Its former CEO, Akbar Al-Bakar, said in 2021 that buying the planes was a "big mistake," given their high operating costs.
However, on the sidelines of 2024's Farnborough Airshow, his successor Badr Mohammed Al-Meer — who has since left the CEO position — said the quad-engine was getting a new lease of life.
Qatar has eight A380s, which it operates between Doha and Bangkok, London, and Paris.
5. Qantas
A Qantas Airbus A380. 
Sebastian Kahnert/Getty Images 
Australian flag carrier Qantas has 10 A380s.
It flies them from Sydney to Dallas/Fort Worth, Johannesburg, Los Angeles, and Singapore — from which it also continues to London.
Plus, the A380 is sometimes used on flights from Melbourne to Los Angeles.
A severe storm warning and "incredibly high" demand during Taylor Swift's Australian tour last year saw Qantas use a spare A380 to fly Swifties from Melbourne to Sydney.
6. Etihad
The Residence's bedroom on an Etihad A380. 
Etihad Airways via Getty Images 
Abu Dhabi's Etihad Airways is the third-most prominent operator in the Middle East, often overshadowed by Emirates and Qatar.
However, its A380s are unique in offering the most extravagant ticket in commercial aviation: The Residence .
For $24,000, you can book the only three-room suite on an airliner, complete with a bedroom and shower.
Etihad has 9 A380s, but one is in storage, according to ch-aviation.
It flies them from Abu Dhabi to Bangkok, London, Singapore, and Toronto.
7. Lufthansa
A Lufthansa Airbus A380 taxiing in Munich. 
Peter Kneffel/picture alliance via Getty Images 
The German flag carrier has a fleet of eight A380s.
It appears to prefer the only other double-decker jet, as Lufthansa operates the most Boeing 747 jets of any passenger airline.
Lufthansa initially retired all 14 of its A380s during the pandemic before changing its mind as travel demand bounced back. The other six were sold back to Airbus, Airways Magazine reported in 2023.
Lufthansa's A380s go between Munich and Bangkok, Los Angeles, New Delhi, San Francisco, and Washington, DC.
8. Korean Air
A Korean Air Airbus A380. 
Matej Divizna/Getty Images 
Korean Air is one of four airlines on this list, and 11 around the world, to be rated five stars by Skytrax.
It has five A380s, according to ch-aviation. It flies them on only one route: between Seoul's Incheon Airport and New York's JFK.
Back in 2021, CEO Walter Cho told FlightGlobal that its A380s would be retired by 2026, but delivery delays and high travel demand have seen their lifespan extended.
9. Asiana Airlines
An Asiana Airlines Airbus A380. 
Joan Valls/Urbanandsport /NurPhoto via Getty Images 
Asiana Airlines has six A380s, one of which is in storage and another undergoing maintenance as of September, per ch-aviation's fleet data.
During the pandemic, Asiana flew empty superjumbos to keep its pilots certified.
The second Seoul-based carrier on this list, Asiana, has merged with Korean Air. For now, it's operated as a subsidiary but will use the same name from 2027.
Until then, Asiana regularly flies these jets from Seoul to Bangkok, Los Angeles, Tokyo, and Sydney.
10. ANA
A ceremony celebrated the delivery of ANA's first A380 in 2019. 
JIJI PRESS/AFP via Getty Images 
ANA is the newest Airbus A380 customer , as its first was delivered in 2019.
The Japanese airline has three in total, which it flies between Tokyo's Narita Airport and Honolulu.
ANA is another five-star airline, with an impressive business-class product. But you'll need to fly on a Boeing 777 to experience "The Room" — or in first class, "The Suite," which includes a 43-inch TV.

Kolon Global Builds Tokyo Electron Chip Equipment Testing Hub Near SK hynix Site
Kolon Global's Tokyo Electron Site in Yongin
Building Designed to Support Equipment Operation
Process Checks Underway Ahead of January Completion
Bio Facility Experience Extended to Semiconductors
A Foothold to Broaden Non-Housing Business
Finance | Published 2026.09.20. 17:45:24 | Updated 2026.09.20. 20:21:23 
| By Woo Young-tak tak@sedaily.com 
| Summary | Save 
A A A 
Lee Jae-yeol, site manager at Kolon Global, explains the semiconductor research and evaluation facility. Photo courtesy of Kolon Global That was the scene on Sept. 18 at the construction site of Tokyo Electron Korea's (TEL) research and evaluation facility in Wonsam-myeon, Cheoin-gu, Yongin, Gyeonggi Province. With the Chuseok holiday about a week away, Kolon Global was in the thick of work on a total of 12 buildings — four main structures including a fab, an office, a parking tower and a daycare center, plus eight utility buildings for electricity, water supply and other services.
A clean room at Tokyo Electron Korea's semiconductor research and evaluation facility under construction by Kolon Global. Photo courtesy of Kolon Global 
The site is a research and evaluation base for TEL, the global semiconductor equipment maker. The company installs equipment identical to what it supplies to customer SK hynix and verifies performance under the same conditions as an actual production line. SK hynix's Yongin semiconductor cluster is going up about 1 kilometer away. "You can't keep testing equipment inside a customer's plant while it's in production," said Lee Jae-yeol, Kolon Global's site manager. "This is a facility that creates identical clean room conditions to evaluate and upgrade equipment." It is similar to a digital twin — which replicates a plant in virtual space — except implemented with real equipment.
Lee Jae-yeol, site manager at Kolon Global, explains the semiconductor research and evaluation facility. The building seen across the way is SK hynix's Yongin Semiconductor Cluster plant. Photo courtesy of Kolon Global Inside the evaluation building where the semiconductor equipment will be installed, even the floor differs from an ordinary structure. Panels are laid over a steel frame, with space secured underneath for piping and wiring. The core of the evaluation building is the clean room and air conditioning. For equipment to perform properly in semiconductor processes such as etching, deposition, photolithography and cleaning, fine contaminants must be filtered out and a stable environment maintained. Filter fan units in the ceiling supply clean air and keep internal pressure higher than outside to block contaminants. The basement houses equipment supplying ultrapure water and cooling water. The entire building is configured to support the operation of the equipment.
Construction began in July last year, with completion targeted for January next year. SK hynix moved up the completion of its plant from May to February next year, leaving little slack in the TEL facility's schedule as well.
The project is a stepping stone for Kolon Global's expansion into high-tech construction. The company is broadening its order pipeline around technology-intensive industrial facilities in semiconductors, pharmaceuticals and biotech. It gained experience in clean room and air conditioning installation at Daewoong Bio's cephalosporin antibiotics plant, and has also worked on semiconductor support infrastructure, including a discharge water temperature reduction facility at Samsung Electronics' Pyeongtaek campus and an integrated water supply project for the Yongin semiconductor industrial complex.
Competitiveness in high-tech construction comes from carrying such experience over to the next site. The TEL project will likewise serve as a track record for winning follow-on orders for semiconductor materials, parts and equipment facilities. Kolon Global aims to accumulate industrial construction credentials to reduce its dependence on the housing cycle and broaden its non-residential business base.
The closer completion comes, the more safety weighs on management. No accidents so far offers no guarantee for what lies ahead. "The more complex the site becomes, the more hands-on management it needs," Lee said, adding that safety management would continue at the site through the Chuseok holiday.

by 서 인주

Amkor Technology announced in June a plan to add six factory buildings on idle land within its Gwangju factory in the Cheomdan district of Buk-gu and to expand the site in phases through 2035. 
Whether Amkor Technology, a global semiconductor packaging company, will expand its investment in the South Jeolla-Gwangju region is drawing close attention. Having announced a 1 trillion won investment plan for Gwangju, the company is reportedly reviewing a further expansion into the Cheomdan 3 district, with an eye toward creating synergies with the 800 trillion won Honam semiconductor industry cluster and linking up with the AI sector.
With the launch of the South Jeolla-Gwangju integrated special city, which brings added administrative licensing support and broader investment infrastructure, observers are watching whether the investment will grow beyond its original scale.
Amkor Technology has also resolved a wastewater treatment problem that had long been a source of concern.
The South Jeolla-Gwangju integrated special city and Jangseong-gun signed a semiconductor wastewater treatment MOU at the Muan government complex on Friday to support Amkor Technology Korea's semiconductor factory investment.
The two sides agreed to work together to resolve the wastewater treatment issue, which had been identified as a major obstacle to expanding Amkor's semiconductor factory. The development stands in contrast to 2022, when Amkor shelved its Gwangju investment plan and instead expanded its production lines in Vietnam.
Amkor announced in June a plan to add six factory buildings on idle land within its Gwangju factory in the Cheomdan district of Buk-gu and to expand the site in phases through 2035.
The city had drawn up a plan to link Amkor's expanded wastewater output to the Gwangju No. 1 Sewage Treatment Plant, but the facility had in effect reached its capacity limit, creating an additional wastewater treatment problem.
The city then proposed connecting the wastewater to Jangseong-gun's public wastewater treatment facility. After Jangseong-gun accepted the proposal, the two sides concluded the agreement.
The two local governments plan to build the infrastructure needed to handle wastewater generated during semiconductor manufacturing in time for Amkor's large-scale investment, and to establish an administrative support framework.
They agreed to build wastewater treatment facilities on a schedule that will not disrupt factory operation timelines, and to cooperate at every stage — from licensing and facility construction to future operation and management.
South Jeolla-Gwangju Special City Mayor Min Hyeong-bae said the city would "focus its efforts on expanding essential infrastructure and providing administrative support so that Amkor's investment proceeds without a hitch."

content_text:
News 
Fortaegis Technologies Raises $50 Million Series A to Deploy Hardware-Rooted Quantum-Safe Secure Compute Architecture
September 19, 2026 · 1 min read
Share 
Copy link 
Amsterdam-based hardware security startup Fortaegis Technologies has closed an oversubscribed $50 million Series A funding round to accelerate commercial production and global deployment of its full-stack Secure Compute architecture. Led by returning investor Serendipity Capital , the syndicate includes strategic semiconductor, industrial, and defense backers TEL Venture Capital (the CVC arm of Tokyo Electron ), ASML , TNO , Prodrive Technologies , NP-Hard Ventures , NovaCapital , Access Ventures , and Coalition Capital .
The company’s executive leadership and board include Ilyas Khan (Founder of Quantinuum ) as Chairman, Boudewijn Wijnands as Founder and CEO, and Chris Miller (author of Chip War ) as a U.S. Board Member. Fortaegis’s technology addresses hardware security threats posed by high-throughput AI workloads and post-quantum decryption risks. The Fortaegis Silicon Platform provides a full-stack architecture spanning hardware, firmware, cryptography, and software that roots security directly in physical silicon properties.
[ Fortaegis Series A Financing & Architecture Overview ] 
Financing & Leadership Hardware & Cryptographic Architecture Deployment & Product Roadmap 
• $50 Million Series A 
• Lead: Serendipity Capital
• Strategic: ASML, TEL VC, TNO, Prodrive
• Chairman: Ilyas Khan (Quantinuum) • Physical silicon-rooted trust & identity
• Dynamic, quantum-safe key generation
• Machine-to-machine connections >200× faster
• Zero permanent on-chip key storage • Form Factors: Server rack, edge, embedded
• Commercial FPGA scaling across US, EU, SG, JP
• Dedicated custom ASIC roadmap development
• Targets: AI data centers, defense, telecom 
By extracting cryptographic entropy from microscopic physical manufacturing variations in silicon, the architecture generates dynamic, quantum-resistant encryption keys on demand without storing keys permanently on-chip, eliminating key-theft attack vectors. Fortaegis reports holding 17 patents (with 14 pending) and achieving secure machine-to-machine connection speeds over 200 times faster than conventional software cryptographic approaches in customer evaluations. Capital from the round will scale FPGA deployment and advance its custom ASIC development pipeline across data center, defense, telecommunications, and autonomous infrastructure markets.

Tungsten is a metal that attracts far less attention than rare earths but is no less vital to modern industry.

Nestled between a turquoise-colored lake and the soaring peaks of the Austrian Alps, Plansee Group is building one of the West’s most formidable critical minerals operations outside China.
The closely held company, based in the town of Reutte, sells tungsten, a metal that attracts far less attention than rare earths but is no less vital to modern industry. The material’s exceptional hardness makes it ideal for tools that cut and shape car parts. Its resistance to heat is crucial to semiconductor manufacturing. And its extraordinary density, nearly twice that of lead, gives armor-piercing ammunition much of its penetrating power. 
Few metals can match that versatility, but sourcing it comes with a familiar vulnerability: Beijing dominates the supply chain. A series of moves by China over the past two years — restricting exports, drawing in more raw material and, most recently, cutting off key shipments to Japan — has intensified a global scramble for tungsten. In turn, its cost has soared.

Semicon 2.0 Draws Rs 1 Lakh Cr Investment Commitments
2 min read 
4901 INTC 
Semicon 2.0 draws Rs 1 lakh crore investment commitments as India expands semiconductor design, fabs, packaging, R&D and talent development across the ecosystem 
India has received investment commitments of around Rs 1 lakh crore, or approximately USD 11–12 billion, under Semicon 2.0, as the government seeks to expand the country’s semiconductor ecosystem across design, manufacturing, equipment, advanced packaging, research and talent development. 
Electronics and IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the commitments are expected to generate close to 1 lakh new employment opportunities across the semiconductor ecosystem. The investments are expected to materialise over the next two to three years, subject to the required board and shareholder approvals. 
Speaking at SEMICON India 2026, Vaishnaw said Semicon 1.0 focused on establishing the foundation for India’s semiconductor industry, while Semicon 2.0 aims to build a broader ecosystem across the value chain. 
The second phase will focus on six areas — semiconductor design, machines and materials, fabs, advanced packaging, research and development, and talent development. 
Under the design pillar, the government is targeting 200 semiconductor design startups, compared with 105 startups supported during the first phase. Of these, 20 have already secured venture capital funding. The government also plans to help companies move from individual chip design towards systems design. 
The programme will also seek to develop domestic capabilities in semiconductor manufacturing equipment, materials, gases, chemicals, precision manufacturing and supply chains. The government plans to support fabs across display, memory, silicon, compound and logic technologies, along with advanced packaging capabilities. 
Semicon 2.0 will promote applied research involving industry, government and academic institutions. On talent, the government plans to train 1 lakh technicians over five years through partnerships with industry and international institutions, including Taiwan-based ITRI. 
The government also announced 11 MoUs and five announcements at SEMICON India 2026 covering semiconductor manufacturing, packaging, materials, equipment, design and workforce development. 
Key agreements include Tata Electronics’ partnerships with Nexperia for wafer manufacturing, assembly and testing, Ascendas First Space for a 363-acre vendor park in Dholera, Fujifilm and JSR for semiconductor materials, and BESI for advanced packaging. 
India Semiconductor Mission and Intel India also launched an ‘Introduction to Semiconductors’ course, while six ChipIN regional centres were announced to expand access to semiconductor design capabilities. 
Vaishnaw said the focus of Semicon 2.0 is to build a complete ecosystem around semiconductor manufacturing rather than individual facilities. SEMICON India 2026 is being held at Yashobhoomi in New Delhi until September 19, with more than 600 participating companies and representatives from 52 countries.

Corning to Hike Glass Substrate Prices 15% in Q4; TSMC, Samsung Race Into AI Packaging's New Frontier
Add preferred source 11 
Corning, the world's leading display glass maker, announced that starting in the fourth quarter of 2026 it will raise prices on yen-denominated display glass substrates by more than 15%, citing yen depreciation and surging costs. Chinese panel makers including TCL CSOT, BOE, and HKC have followed with their own price-increase notices to customers. With Chinese manufacturers controlling roughly 70% of the global LCD TV panel market, pricing power has clearly shifted. Meanwhile, glass substrates are emerging as a new frontier in AI advanced packaging, thanks to their low coefficient of thermal expansion, nanometer-level flatness, and low signal loss. TSMC, Intel, and Samsung are all aggressively advancing their respective programs. Research firms project the global glass substrate market will grow from $9.03 billion in 2024 to $16.81 billion by 2032, with penetration in advanced packaging reaching 30% by 2030. The upstream segment remains an oligopoly held by Corning, Schott, and AGC, while midstream players such as BOE and WG Tech have entered pilot or small-batch supply stages. Taiwanese equipment makers including Contrel Technology, Laser Tek Taiwan, and others are expected to be the first beneficiaries of equipment procurement momentum in 2026–2027.
Key Elements 
Corning Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing BOE TCL CSOT Intel Samsung Samsung Electro-Mechanics Sumitomo Chemical Nippon Electric Glass WG Tech AGC Ibiden Innolux NVIDIA 
Corning, the world's leading display glass maker, announced that due to the sharp depreciation of the Japanese yen and simultaneous surges in raw material, energy, and logistics costs, it will raise prices on yen-denominated display glass substrate products by more than 15% globally starting in the fourth quarter of 2026. The move has quickly triggered a chain reaction across the panel industry, with Chinese panel giants TCL CSOT, BOE, and HKC already issuing price-adjustment notices to customers — signaling a new round of pricing-power realignment for this mature material.
At the same time, the application prospects for glass substrates in advanced semiconductor packaging are drawing intense attention. As AI chip sizes continue to expand, traditional organic substrates are prone to warpage due to their high coefficient of thermal expansion, while silicon interposers remain constrained by persistently high costs. Glass substrates — with their low thermal expansion, nanometer-level flatness, and superior signal transmission characteristics — are becoming a new battleground where semiconductor giants such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (2330.TW), Intel, and Samsung are racing to stake their claims.
Display Panel Price Hikes: Corning Leads, Chinese Makers Hold Pricing Power
In its price-increase notice, Corning stated that the continued weakening of the yen against the U.S. dollar, combined with rising costs for key raw materials, precious metals, energy, and logistics, has exceeded what the company can internally absorb. Industry observers widely expect Japanese glass suppliers AGC and Nippon Electric Glass (NEG) to follow suit with their own price adjustments. This marks Corning's first display glass price increase in more than three years. In May 2023, the company raised prices by 20% across all regions and all generation sizes of display glass substrates, citing inflation; this time, the increase is limited to yen-denominated products.
Behind this wave of price hikes lies a profound structural shift in the global LCD TV panel industry. Average capacity utilization at TV panel makers held at a high level of 90% in the third quarter, and Chinese manufacturers now control roughly 70% of the global LCD TV panel market. With Korean and Taiwanese players having gradually exited, pricing power has clearly shifted into the hands of Chinese panel makers.
TCL CSOT was the first to act, sending a TV panel price-increase letter to downstream customers on September 10, directly attributing the move to rising upstream raw material costs. BOE followed with its own product price-adjustment notice, stating that procurement costs for key materials continue to climb and that it plans to adjust prices on its display product lines, also effective from the fourth quarter. HKC likewise issued price-increase notices to customers. Brand-side players including Samsung, LG, and Sony have all received the relevant correspondence.
However, market analysts caution that whether these price-increase notices can be fully realized still depends on actual fourth-quarter procurement appetite from brand customers. Some observers suggest the move is closer to a probe of pricing initiative, with the final magnitude of increases still subject to negotiation between supply and demand.
AI Packaging's New Frontier: The Physical Advantages of Glass Substrates
While glass substrates are stirring a price-hike wave in the display sector, their application in semiconductor packaging is drawing even greater market attention. The driving logic in the two arenas is entirely different: display is a repricing of a mature segment, while semiconductors represent a brand-new frontier that is only just getting started.
The relentless expansion of AI chip sizes is posing severe challenges for traditional packaging materials. Organic substrates have a relatively high coefficient of thermal expansion, making them prone to warpage as chip sizes grow; silicon interposers, while excellent in performance, remain prohibitively expensive. By comparison, glass substrates offer a thermal expansion coefficient of approximately 3.2 ppm — closely matched to silicon wafers — along with nanometer-level surface flatness and signal loss two to three orders of magnitude lower than silicon. They can also be formed into large-format substrates in a single pass using panel-level processes, striking a unique balance between cost and performance.
The accelerating growth in chip sizes makes this issue all the more urgent. According to TrendForce, citing supply chain information, NVIDIA's next-generation Rubin GPU has reached a reticle size of 5.5x, meaning a single 12-inch wafer can now accommodate only seven dies — and in some cases as few as four. Square panel formats can substantially improve area utilization and throughput efficiency, which is precisely the key driver pushing advanced packaging from round wafers toward square panels.
Research firms project the global glass substrate market will grow from $9.03 billion in 2024 to $16.81 billion by 2032. This figure is dominated by display glass substrates. Counterpoint separately estimates that the combined market for fan-out panel-level packaging (FOPLP) and glass substrates will expand from approximately $650 million in 2024 to more than $8.1 billion by 2030 — a roughly 12-fold increase over six years. The overall industry timeline is expected to see pilot line completion in 2026, small-batch commercialization in 2027–2028, and market penetration reaching 30% by 2030.
TSMC, Intel, and Samsung have all been aggressively advancing their respective glass substrate programs. TSMC has partnered with Japanese substrate leader Ibiden and Taiwanese panel maker Innolux (3481.TW) to advance feasibility verification of integrating glass substrates into its CoPoS advanced packaging technology.
Notably, the three companies are pursuing distinctly different technical routes. TSMC's CoPoS uses square glass panels with multi-layer RDL to replace the silicon interposer in its current CoWoS architecture. Intel unveiled the industry's first glass core substrate as early as 2023, directly replacing the core layer of ABF organic substrates with a glass core, with volume production planned between 2026 and 2030. Samsung, through its subsidiary Samsung Electro-Mechanics, has formed a joint venture with the Korean subsidiary of Japan's Sumitomo Chemical to produce glass core substrates.
Company Technology Replaces Positioning 
TSMC CoPoS Silicon interposer Advancing verification with Ibiden and Innolux 
Intel Glass core substrate Organic substrate core layer Unveiled 2023; volume production planned for 2026-2030 
Samsung Glass core substrate Organic substrate core layer JV between Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Sumitomo Chemical group 
TSMC Chairman C.C. Wei gave the first clear timeline at the company's shareholder meeting on June 4: the pilot production line has been completed, but it will take approximately two to three more years before volume production truly scales up. He emphasized that there are no shortcuts in advanced packaging and new material development, with the focus on joint verification with customers to ensure mass-production efficiency and yield targets are met.
Supply Chain Positioning: Upstream Oligopoly, Midstream Heavy Investment, Equipment First to Benefit
Positioning across the glass substrate supply chain roughly divides into three tiers, with barriers to entry rising the further upstream one goes.
Upstream glass raw sheet remains dominated by Corning, Germany's Schott, and AGC, with the oligopoly firmly entrenched. Chinese players are also actively moving in: Triumph Science & Technology is laying out low-dielectric high-borosilicate glass formulations suited for TGV (through-glass via) technology; Kibing Group is expanding chip-packaging glass capacity through a private placement; and IRICO Group established a semiconductor subsidiary on September 10 with registered capital of CNY 140 million (approximately $20.9 million), extending into semiconductor glass materials.
Midstream substrate manufacturing requires the heaviest investment. BOE has cumulatively invested CNY 1.4 billion (approximately $209.0 million) since launching preliminary research in 2020. Its glass-core packaging substrate pilot line achieved fully automated line operation on September 8, with a designed capacity of 1,000 panels per month. The line has already validated key processes including high-aspect-ratio via drilling, deep-hole copper filling, and multi-layer lamination, successfully producing 20-layer large-format samples, while also signing a three-year memorandum of understanding with Corning. WG Tech has also completed construction of a TGV production line and begun small-batch shipments. Japan's DNP holds patent advantages in semiconductor-grade micro-via metallization and interface treatment.
The equipment segment is considered closest to actual orders. Delphilaser's TGV laser micro-via equipment has already achieved batch shipments at both panel-level and wafer-level, holding roughly 40% of the domestic Chinese market. Delong Laser, Han's CNC, and Lyric Robot are also following suit. On the Taiwanese equipment side, Contrel Technology (8064.TW), Laser Tek Taiwan (6207.TW), C Sun Mfg (2467.TW), Grand Process Technology (3131.TW), Scientech (3583.TW), and others have all entered the glass substrate and TGV process space, and are expected to be the first to see tangible equipment procurement momentum as production lines transition from pilot to volume production in 2026–2027.
Japanese Materials Makers' Second Growth Curve
This new frontier is no spectator sport for Japanese materials companies. The Japanese players that compete with Corning in display glass have long been simultaneously positioning themselves in semiconductor glass substrates.
Nippon Electric Glass has developed two products: the GC Core glass-ceramic core substrate and a glass core substrate. Their defining feature is the use of CO2 lasers to directly process through-glass vias (TGV), enabling high-speed formation of crack-free holes without chemical etching, and the company has already produced large substrates measuring 515×510 mm. In November 2024, it signed a joint development agreement with laser processing equipment maker Via Mechanics. AGC has already commercialized alkali-free glass packaging substrates, offering both 500 mm square panels and 300 mm diameter wafers, achieving a thermal expansion coefficient perfectly matched to silicon across a range from room temperature to approximately 250°C.
That said, the journey from pilot to volume production for glass substrates still faces significant hurdles. Nippon Electric Glass identified three key challenges in its own technical documentation: the brittleness of glass makes yield improvement difficult, as stress in back-end processes or minor impacts during handling can cause open circuits or short circuits; the laser modification plus etching flow for TGV involves numerous steps and relatively long processing times; and laser and chemical processing equipment is expensive, with associated environmental and waste-liquid treatment facilities further raising the investment threshold.
Market Reaction and Outlook
Glass substrate concept stocks showed notable volatility after the price-hike news emerged. On September 11, the day Corning announced the increase, related concept stocks surged, with WG Tech touching its daily limit-up and Sanxia New Material locking in limit-up. However, some stocks subsequently gave back gains, indicating that market sentiment has become more divided after the initial euphoria.
It is worth noting that most companies laying out glass substrate businesses are still in the sampling verification or pilot stage, with limited actual earnings contribution. While the industry direction is clear, the path from samples to orders to revenue still involves two major hurdles: customer qualification and yield improvement. Market expectations often run ahead of fundamentals, and investors should be mindful of the associated risks.

content_text:
Mitsubishi Chemical deepens AI infrastructure bet with NLM Photonics investment 
Mitsubishi Chemical has invested in NLM Photonics through Diamond Edge Ventures as AI data-centre traffic strains optical networks. The Washington State startup is developing organic electro-optic materials aimed at faster, lower-power optical modulation, with the deal highlighting growing strategic interest in photonics and advanced materials. 
ETChemicals 
Published On Sep 18, 2026 at 12:15 PM IST
Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook 
Bookmark 
Generative AI is forcing data-centre operators to rethink one of the most overlooked parts of the digital stack: how data moves between chips, servers and racks. Against that backdrop, Mitsubishi Chemical Corporation has chosen to back a US startup building the materials that could help ease that pressure, according to Indian Chemical News . 
The investment, routed through Diamond Edge Ventures, Inc. , Mitsubishi Chemical 's corporate venture capital arm, forms part of NLM Photonics ' Series A2 round led by Pangaea Ventures . The deal signals how materials groups are moving closer to the AI infrastructure race, where performance gains increasingly depend on advances in photonics rather than only on semiconductors and cloud hardware. 
Why optical interconnects matter in the AI build-out 
The latest wave of AI deployment has sharply increased the amount of data that must be shifted inside data centres. That has lifted the importance of optical interconnects, the communication links that enable high-speed data transmission while helping manage energy use. As workloads grow heavier, these links are becoming a strategic bottleneck for operators trying to keep speed, latency and power consumption in balance. 
Mitsubishi Chemical said materials used in optical modulation are emerging as a critical area for differentiated device performance. In practical terms, that means the chemistry inside photonic devices is becoming as important as the hardware architecture itself, especially when the industry is trying to push more data through the same physical footprint without a matching rise in electricity demand. 
What NLM Photonics is building 
NLM Photonics is based in Washington State and develops organic electro-optic materials for next-generation optical communications. The startup was founded on more than two decades of research at the University of Washington , giving it a scientific base that has been shaped by academic work rather than by a conventional hardware manufacturing playbook. 
Its Selerion materials are designed for use with silicon photonic devices to form hybrid silicon-organic photonic integrated circuits, or PICs. These are intended to support optical modulation at higher speeds and with lower power consumption than older inorganic approaches. The pitch is straightforward: if the materials can be integrated reliably into semiconductor-style production, they could help make AI data movement faster and more efficient. 
Manufacturing realism is now part of the pitch 
The investment case is not being built only on laboratory promise. Curtis Schickner , president of Diamond Edge Ventures , said the attraction lies in the combination of scientific depth and manufacturability. He argued that optical interconnects have become one of the real constraints in AI infrastructure, and that the remaining gains are concentrated in the materials used in modulators. Schickner added that NLM has shown organic electro-optic materials can be processed in ways that fit how the semiconductor industry actually builds devices. 
That framing matters because many advanced materials programmes stall when they move from research to production. For venture investors and strategic backers alike, the question is no longer whether a material works in a lab setting, but whether it can be handled at scale, incorporated into existing supply chains and delivered with consistent yields. Mitsubishi Chemical's backing suggests it sees NLM as one of the rarer cases that may clear that hurdle. 
A strategic fit with Mitsubishi Chemical's broader agenda 
The investment also aligns with Mitsubishi Chemical's management vision, KAITEKI Vision 35, under which advanced data processing and telecommunications are among the identified business focus areas. The group said it wants to deepen its understanding of next-generation optical communications, including optoelectronic integration, while also pursuing new business opportunities through its materials technologies. 
That approach reflects a wider trend among large industrial groups: rather than waiting for the AI boom to flow only to chipmakers and cloud providers, they are looking for entry points in the enabling layers that make those systems faster, cooler and more power efficient. Materials science, once seen as a long-cycle support function, is increasingly being treated as a strategic lever in digital infrastructure. 
What the deal says about the next phase of AI infrastructure 
The transaction comes at a time when the economics of AI are being shaped as much by power and connectivity as by model quality. Data centres need more than compute capacity. They also need interconnects that can move data at scale without causing energy costs to spiral. That is why optical technologies are drawing more attention from strategic investors, especially those with deep materials or manufacturing expertise. 
For NLM Photonics, the round provides validation from a major industrial backer as it works to commercialise a niche with broad implications. For Mitsubishi Chemical, the move is a way to position itself closer to the next generation of telecom and computing infrastructure, where the winners may be the groups that can help solve the bottlenecks others overlook. 
As AI workloads continue to expand, the pressure on data-centre networks is unlikely to ease soon. Investments such as this point to a broader shift in which the race for AI advantage is no longer confined to software and chips. It is also moving into the chemistry of light, the design of modulators and the materials that make faster, lower-power communications possible.

Merck KGaA expands life science manufacturing hub in Bengaluru 
The move is the latest in a growing list of investments geared at bolstering India’s global footprint.
Josh Abbott , News Editor, BioProcess International September 18, 2026
schedule 2 Min Read 
stock.adobe.com 
link 
German life science and pharmaceutical company Merck KGaA has announced an expansion of its manufacturing facility in Bengaluru, India, to strengthen its production and supply operations in the Asia-Pacific region. 
Dhananjay Singh, managing director of Merck India’s Life Science business, said the company will invest €13 million (about US$15 million) in its Jigani, Bengaluru site to expand its biology and chemistry capabilities. 
According to a press release, the Jigani site will manufacture biological buffers and raw materials for diagnostic applications used in DNA research, cell culture, diagnostics, and drug manufacturing. 
The expansion will add about 2,900 square meters of new capabilities to Merck’s 40,460 square-meter campus. The site already has established capabilities in specialty and fine chemicals, custom synthesis, and catalog product manufacturing. 
“This investment will reinforce our global supply chain and support the ‘Make in India’ initiative,” Singh said. “We appreciate the continued collaboration from DPIIT, the Heavy Water Board, the Government of Karnataka, and Invest India as Merck expands Jigani.” 
Related: 53Biologics talks industry in Spain as company unveils $2.25m infrastructure expansion 
The country launched its Make in India initiative in 2014 to support its growth as a global design and manufacturing hub. 
“Merck’s Bengaluru manufacturing hub shows what the India–Germany partnership can achieve when world-class German enterprise meets India's manufacturing ambition,” added Shri Amardeep Singh Bhatia, IAS, secretary to the government of India, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry. “In the year we celebrate 75 years of diplomatic relations, Merck will make advanced materials in Bengaluru for pharmaceutical research and semiconductor manufacturing, for India and for the world, in the true spirit of Make in India.” 
Big moves in India 
“India is emerging as an increasingly important hub for life science innovation and manufacturing,” said Singh during his remarks about the Merck expansion. 
Indeed, the South Asian country is becoming one of the most exciting global biotech hubs to follow. In addition to attracting international investment from industry giants such as Merck, India is headquarters to a growing ecosystem of homegrown companies that are making big moves. Earlier this week, contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) Shilpa Biologicals announced a biosimilar licensing agreement with Saudi Arabia-based SPIMACO Bio. And as part of an effort to accelerate peptide manufacturing, Hyderabad-based Neuland Laboratories recently announced that its first commercial peptide manufacturing module is now operational, with further expansion in its capacity underway.

Leonardo DRS has announced a contract with Doosan Enerbility to provide the electric propulsion system for the Republic of Korea Navy’s KDDX destroyer program. The company said the lead ship is being built by Hanwha Ocean and the program is expected to include at least six destroyers.
Leonardo DRS press release:
Leonardo DRS, Inc. announced today that it has entered into a contract with Doosan Enerbility to provide the electric propulsion system for the Republic of Korea Navy’s KDDX destroyer program, the lead ship of which is being built by Hanwha Ocean. KDDX is a next-generation guided-missile destroyer, considered a cornerstone of South Korea’s future naval fleet requirements. The program is expected to deliver at least six destroyers and represents South Korea’s first indigenously designed and built destroyer program.
Under the award, DRS will supply an integrated electric power and propulsion solution featuring its power-dense 100-Series permanent magnet propulsion motors and matched high-performance, compact variable frequency drives. The system is designed to provide efficient, reliable propulsion in a compact configuration for next-generation naval platforms
Doosan Enerbility and DRS will collaborate on the destroyer’s integrated power and propulsion system, which includes electrical and mechanical equipment extending from the prime movers to the propellers.
The KDDX program is expected to introduce the Republic of Korea Navy’s first full-electric-drive surface combatants, as part of a planned class of next-generation destroyers designed to meet the demanding multi-mission requirements of a modern blue-water fleet. As navies worldwide move toward integrated electric propulsion to support advanced sensors, weapons and mission systems, the KDDX program represents a significant milestone in the adoption of full electric drive for front-line surface combatants.
“Modern naval platforms require electric power and propulsion systems that can meet current operational demands while providing the flexibility to support future mission needs,” said John Baylouny, president and chief executive officer of Leonardo DRS. “Our advanced electric-propulsion technologies are designed to deliver the power capacity, efficiency, reliability and adaptability required for advanced radars, advanced EW systems, directed energy systems, the charging of unmanned vehicles, the launch of drone swarms and other increasingly power-intensive mission capabilities.”
“DRS is proud to support the Republic of Korea Navy’s KDDX destroyer program with proven electric propulsion technology,” said Jon Miller, senior vice president and general manager of Naval Power Systems at Leonardo DRS. “For more than a decade our systems have supported Republic of Korea Navy FFX II/III/IV frigates, and we have demonstrated the ability to scale our electric-propulsion technology for the most demanding naval applications, including the COLUMBIA-class submarine program. This technology is designed to support efficient propulsion, compact installation and the electrical demands of advanced shipboard systems. We look forward to working with Doosan Enerbility and Hanwha Ocean in support of this important program.”
The DRS permanent magnet motor technology is designed to provide high torque density in a compact architecture, helping reduce size and weight compared with conventional electric machines. Paired with the company’s variable-frequency drive, the system delivers precise, and highly efficient propulsion control while reducing engine-room footprint and supporting greater flexibility in ship design. The system is designed, built, and delivered by DRS to meet applicable military requirements for power quality, shock, and vibration, as well as Republic of Korea Navy operational requirements.
This selection builds on a long record of DRS electric propulsion success with the Republic of Korea Navy, including hybrid electric drive systems provided for the 20 anti-submarine warfare frigates in the FFX Batch II, III and IV frigate programs. DRS is a leading provider of next-generation electric power and propulsion technology for the U.S. Navy and allied navies worldwide. The KDDX program reinforces the company’s role as a trusted provider of integrated electric drive solutions for the world’s most advanced naval platforms.

Toray Industries wins RO membrane order for Singapore’s Changi NEWater Factory
September 18, 2026 | By Mary Bailey 
Toray Industries, Inc. announced today that it has received an order for its low-fouling reverse osmosis (RO) membranes for wastewater treatment . The RO membrane elements will be used for the Changi NEWater Factory (CNF3), a large-scale used water treatment plant in Singapore.
Sanli M&E Engineering Pte. Ltd. (Singapore) was awarded the contract for the construction of CNF3 by national water agency PUB, with Toray Asia Pte. Ltd. (Singapore) supplying the RO membranes and providing sales and technical support. The plant will have a treatment capacity of 50 million gallons per day and is targeted to be completed by 2028.
Toray has supplied water treatment membranes for major water infrastructure projects in Singapore over the years, which includes several NEWater and desalination plants. This latest order reflects the proven long-term performance of Toray’s low-fouling RO membranes for wastewater reclamation.
The global RO membrane market continues to expand. This growth is driven by population growth, industrial development, worsening water shortages owing to climate change, and tougher environmental regulations. Toray will further strengthen its leadership in water treatment by reinforcing its advanced membrane technologies, enhancing its global production capabilities, and providing responsive and effective technical support.

content_text:
Semicon India: Tata Electronics to sign 16 pacts with firms across semiconductor supply chain, says Randhir Thakur 
These pacts will be with companies including Nexperia and Besi from Europe; JSR, Fujifilm, Sumitomo, Sojitz, and Enomoto from Japan; Kellington from Malaysia; Ascendas Firstspace from Singapore; L&T Semiconductors, Inox Air Products, Semi-Conductor Laboratory, and Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya from India; and other partners from the US, Europe, and India, all specialising in different parts of the semiconductor value chain, said Thakur. 
ETElectronicsWorld Desk 
ETElectronicsWorld 
Updated On Sep 17, 2026 at 05:18 PM IST
Read by 1101 Professionals
Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook 
Bookmark 
NEW DELHI: Tata Electronics will sign 16 Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with global and domestic ecosystem partners to bolster India's domestic semiconductor supply chain , according to a top company executive. 
The pacts span partners across key geographic regions including Europe, Japan, Malaysia, Singapore, and India, bringing specialised capabilities across different stages of the semiconductor value chain. 
"At Semicon India 2026 , Tata Electronics will be signing 16 MoUs,” said Randhir Thakur, CEO, Tata Electronics, at the inauguration of the Semicon India 2026 event, which is being organised from September 17 to September 19 here. 
These pacts will be with companies including Nexperia and Besi from Europe; JSR, Fujifilm, Sumitomo, Sojitz, and Enomoto from Japan; Kellington from Malaysia; Ascendas Firstspace from Singapore; L&T Semiconductors, Inox Air Products, Semi-Conductor Laboratory, and Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya from India; and other partners from the US, Europe, and India, all specialising in different parts of the semiconductor value chain, said Thakur. 
Thakur highlighted that rapid progress is underway across Tata Electronics' greenfield projects, noting that the semiconductor fab facility in Dholera, Gujarat, and the OSAT packaging facility in Jagiroad, Assam, are on track to meet scheduled government commitments. 
In Gujarat, the Tata Group company is establishing a semiconductor manufacturing facility with an investment of ₹91,526 crore, together with technology partner Taiwanese PSMC. The production capacity would be around 50,000 wafer starts per month (WSPM). 
In Assam, it is investing ₹27,120 crore in a manufacturing facility, which will use indigenous semiconductor packaging technologies with a production capacity of 48 million units per day. 
In Dholera alone, the firm has assembled more than 450 ecosystem partners spanning construction, specialised equipment, chemical, and industrial material supply, alongside a previously signed partnership with lithography leader ASML, said Thakur. 
The company stated that industrial and social infrastructure developments across Dholera and Jagiroad are building a foundation to help global partners grow their operational footprints within India. 
Highlighting workforce development under the India Semiconductor Mission, Thakur noted that 300 Indian engineering graduates are currently undergoing specialised fabrication training at partner PSMC’s facilities in Taiwan. 
Thakur expressed optimism for domestic youth entering the sector, stating that India's technical talent is positioned to provide global manufacturing leadership from classroom to cleanroom, wafer by wafer, and chip by chip. 
Across its operations, Tata Electronics has created over 1.5 lakh direct jobs, said Thakur, adding that women account for 65 per cent of the workforce, many recruited from remote villages and marginalised communities. 
Details of MoUs 
Later in the day, Tata Electronics said its partnership with Nexperia is structured around three areas of front-end wafer fabrication, back-end assembly and test, and technology and ecosystem development. 
As part of the front-end manufacturing collaboration, Nexperia and Tata Electronics are laying the groundwork for the production of Nexperia's MOSFET portfolio at Tata Electronics' upcoming 300mm semiconductor Fab in Dholera, Gujarat. In parallel, the partnership also includes collaboration on semiconductor assembly and test of Nexperia’s discrete semiconductor products at Tata Electronics’ packaging facility in Jagiroad, Assam. 
Furthemore, as part of a partnership, Japanese Fujifilm will develop and supply advanced semiconductor materials tailored to the requirements of Tata Electronics’ upcoming semiconductor fab in Dholera. Fujifilm and Tata Electronics are committed to enhancing India’s supply chain resilience, by localising the development of critical raw materials needed for semiconductor fabrication. The partnership will support Indian chemical manufacturers with technology, quality assurance and manufacturing process knowhow to facilitate the manufacture of high-purity chemicals. 
As part of the partnership, Tata Electronics will leverage Besi's extensive portfolio of advanced packaging equipment and technologies. Leveraging Besi’s extensive portfolio of advanced packaging solutions and global expertise, the collaboration will support the technology readiness of Tata Electronics’ semiconductor packaging facility in Jagiroad, while advancing its journey toward next-generation packaging capabilities. 
With Semi-Conductor Laboratory (SCL), Tata Electronics intends to jointly explore strategic collaboration across critical technology areas including chip design services for government and startup projects, technology node enablement to broaden access to advanced nodes. The partnership will also focus on supply chain localisation for a more resilient domestic ecosystem, and workforce skilling to build India’s semiconductor talent pipeline. 
Lastly, Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya and Tata Electronics will collaborate on skilling and talent development for the semiconductor industry under an MoU.

title: Depreciation Costs Weigh on Global Silicon Wafer Makers - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media
source: Google News: THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media
publisher: THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media
query: ("Shin-Etsu Chemicals" OR "Shin-Etsu Chemical") ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-09-01 before:2026-10-01
content_text:
(Photo: THE ELEC) 
Profitability at global silicon wafer makers weakened in the first half of this year as depreciation expenses from newly operational plants began to weigh on earnings. The companies are bringing new facilities online in stages, significantly increasing global wafer production capacity.
The earnings decline appears to stem not from weak industry conditions but from past capital expenditures translating into depreciation as mass-production lines begin operations. With semiconductor demand expected to continue growing over the next several years amid broader adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), the silicon wafer industry is also expected to see earnings recover quickly.
Industry sources said on Sept. 16 that Japan's SUMCO and Germany's Siltronic swung to operating losses in the first half from a year earlier. SUMCO posted an operating loss of 6.3 billion yen, down 13.7 billion yen from an operating profit of 7.4 billion yen a year earlier. Siltronic swung from an operating profit of 38.5 million euros to a loss of 104.3 million euros. Taiwan's GlobalWafers saw operating profit fall 42.4% to NT$2.898 billion.
Higher depreciation expenses directly contributed to the decline in operating profit. SUMCO's first-half depreciation rose by 11.6 billion yen to 60.3 billion yen from 48.7 billion yen a year earlier. Siltronic's depreciation increased 89.4% to 238.8 million euros. GlobalWafers' depreciation remained at a similar level from a year earlier, but annual depreciation rose 10.9% to NT$8.927 billion last year from NT$8.048 billion in 2024.
The increases are the result of expanded 300mm wafer production capacity. Depreciation expenses began to rise as new plants entered operation. Costs incurred while constructing plants and installing equipment are recorded as tangible assets, but depreciation begins once the facilities start operating. The costs are then recognized in installments over the assets' useful lives.
Major wafer makers decided on large-scale investments in 2021 and 2022, when semiconductor demand surged following the Covid-19 pandemic and a medium- to long-term wafer shortage was expected. The companies later delayed full-scale production from the expanded capacity amid a semiconductor industry downturn. They are now increasing utilization of the new facilities as wafer demand recovers.
Global 300mm silicon wafer production capacity is expected to increase from 10.69 million wafers per month this year to 11 million next year and 11.70 million to 11.76 million in 2028, according to industry sources. That would add more than 1 million wafers of monthly capacity by 2028.
SUMCO decided in 2021 to invest 228.7 billion yen to expand 300mm wafer capacity. In 2024, it completed major investments to establish new production facilities in Imari and Omura, Japan, among other locations. The company plans to gradually increase production capacity through 2027. Depreciation rose 44% to 111 billion yen last year from 77.2 billion yen in 2024. SUMCO said depreciation expenses will peak this year before declining from next year.
Siltronic decided in 2021 to invest about 2 billion euros to build a second 300mm wafer plant in Singapore. It completed customer qualification in July last year, and depreciation related to the operation of major equipment began in August. Depreciation rose 44% from a year earlier to 343.3 million euros last year. The figure is expected to increase to between 490 million euros and 520 million euros this year.
GlobalWafers decided in 2022 to invest NT$100 billion to expand its global production capacity. It built new plants or expanded facilities in Sherman, Texas; St. Peters, Missouri; Novara, Italy; and Utsunomiya, Japan. Annual depreciation is expected to rise 34% from last year to about NT$12 billion this year. Depreciation at its Sherman plant, which added monthly production capacity of 1.2 million wafers, began in April, increasing costs further in the second half.
Japan's Shin-Etsu Chemical also announced capacity expansion in 2022 and is taking delivery of ordered equipment in stages to meet long-term agreements (LTAs) extending through 2027 and 2028. Depreciation remained at about 100 billion yen annually, however, as depreciation on many existing assets ended in the fourth quarter of 2024. The company plans to determine when to begin depreciating new equipment based on customer orders.
SK siltron has invested about 2.3 trillion won since 2022 to expand its 300mm wafer production plant in Gumi, North Gyeongsang Province. Operations began in July, and depreciation on the new facilities is expected to be reflected in earnest from the second half.
The burden from depreciation is expected to gradually ease as shipment volumes increase and wafer prices rise. According to a market research firm, silicon wafer consumption for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is expected to increase 23% next year from this year, while consumption for advanced logic is expected to rise 12%.
By contrast, 300mm wafer production capacity is expected to increase just 3% next year. With supply constraints anticipated, major wafer makers are negotiating next year's supply prices with customers. Discussions are understood to center on price increases of about 10% to 15%, particularly for 300mm wafers.

Tata Electronics, a pioneering leader in India’s electronics and semiconductor manufacturing sector, and Besi, a leading Dutch provider of semiconductor assembly solutions, have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen advanced packaging capabilities in India.
Advertisment 
Add DQIndia Info As A Trusted Source
Tata Electronics is investing $3 billion for India’s first indigenous semiconductor packaging facility in Jagiroad, Assam. As part of the collaboration, Tata Electronics will leverage Besi’s extensive portfolio of advanced packaging equipment and technologies.  
The partnership aligns closely with the next phase of India’s semiconductor program, which seeks to establish a self-sufficient and globally competitive domestic OSAT industry. The partnership also reflects the growing momentum in India-Netherlands semiconductor cooperation following the MoU on partnership on semiconductors and related emerging technologies signed by the two countries. 
The partnership will assess opportunities to strengthen the local semiconductor equipment support ecosystem, facilitate technical collaboration, and enhance long-term equipment readiness for Tata Electronics' semiconductor packaging operations. Leveraging Besi’s extensive portfolio of advanced packaging solutions and global expertise, the collaboration will support the technology readiness of Tata Electronics’ semiconductor packaging facility in Jagiroad, Assam, while advancing its journey toward next-generation packaging capabilities.

Through this partnership, Besi will also evaluate initiatives to support engineering capability development, knowledge-sharing programs and specialized training and certification of Tata Electronics employees, to improve operational flexibility and efficiency. Both companies will work together to develop a shared technology roadmap and innovative processes to enable mutual, long-term growth and build a resilient and globally competitive supply chain in India.

We are delighted to partner with Besi, a global leader in advanced packaging equipment. ABL Diagnostics Becomes ABL Texcell Diagnostics
Business Wire 
September 17, 2026 3 min read 
ABLD.PA 
Shareholders confirm the continuation of the Company's listing on the regulated market of Euronext Paris as the most appropriate framework to support the Company's next phase of long-term development 
WOIPPY, France, September 17, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )--Regulatory News: 
ABL Diagnostics (Euronext Paris: ABLD – ISIN: FR001400AHX6) (the "Company"), a company specialized in molecular diagnostics solutions, healthcare software and services supporting clinical research, announces that its shareholders, meeting today in an Extraordinary General Meeting, approved the change of the Company's corporate name to ABL Texcell Diagnostics, reflecting the Company's evolution and the growing complementarity of its activities in molecular diagnostics, virology and life sciences. 
Shareholders also decided not to approve the resolution relating to the proposed transfer of the Company's shares to Euronext Growth Paris. 
A new identity reflecting the Company's evolution 
"The review conducted over the past several weeks enabled us to thoroughly assess the various options available to support the Company's development. Following this analysis, maintaining the Company's listing on the regulated market of Euronext Paris emerged as the most appropriate solution for our growth trajectory, our ambitions and the interests of all our shareholders," said Dr. Chalom B. Sayada, Chief Executive Officer of ABL Diagnostics and founder of parent company Advanced Biological Laboratories (ABL). 
"The adoption of the name ABL Texcell Diagnostics also marks an important milestone in the Company's evolution. This new identity reflects the complementarity of our activities, Texcell's international recognition and our commitment to creating sustainable value in the fields of diagnostics, virology and life sciences. We remain fully focused on executing our strategic roadmap, expanding our activities and pursuing profitable growth," added Dr. Sayada. 
The Company will therefore continue to pursue its development under its new identity, ABL Texcell Diagnostics, while benefiting from the standards and framework associated with the regulated market of Euronext Paris. The Company continues its efforts to enhance investor visibility, improve share liquidity and broaden its shareholder base, while maintaining the governance and transparency standards associated with a regulated market. 
About ABL Texcell Diagnostics (ABLTDx) 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics (ABLTDx) is an international company that specializes in innovative molecular biology tests and global solutions for its customers: 
Story Continues 
Molecular polymerase chain reaction (PCR) detection – UltraGene, and 
Genotyping by DNA sequencing – DeepChek®. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics markets its entire product range globally through its own sales team and a network of exclusive distributors active on all continents. ABL Texcell Diagnostics' customers are academic clinical pathology laboratories, private reference laboratories and researchers willing to implement innovative and robust microbiological content in constant expansion. 
Following the acquisition of TEXCELL's operations, ABL Texcell Diagnostics is expanding its activities in the life sciences sector by integrating expertise and services dedicated to virology, biosafety testing and biopharmaceutical development support. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics has been marketing the products and services of its sister company CDL Pharma since the second half of 2025 through an intra-group strategy agreement. 
An expanding portfolio of microbiology products: 
HIV – Drug resistance testing, including a whole genome kit. 
SARS-CoV-2, Tuberculosis, Hepatitis B and C – Advanced Detection Solutions. 
Microbiome and taxonomy – 16s/18s RNA-based analyses. 
Other viral and bacterial targets – Comprehensive molecular assays. 
Integrated Solutions 
Real-time syndromic PCR tests 
Nadis® – Patient Medical Record used in more than 200 hospitals in France for the management of HIV and hepatitis. 
ABL Texcell Diagnostics, headquartered in Woippy, is a public limited company listed on compartment B of the regulated market of Euronext in Paris (Euronext: ABLD – ISIN: FR001400AHX6). onsemi's 2030 outlook falls short; Stifel lowers target
2 min read 
ON 
onsemi ON held its Financial Analyst Day on Wednesday, and although Stifel was impressed with the company's strategy, they found the 2030 outlook potentially below expectations, prompting the firm to maintain its Hold rating and reduce its price target to $75 from $90. 
"We came away encouraged on strategy, specifically an end-to-end AI data center franchise taking content from ~$15K to ~$115K per rack by CY30, the Embedded Power Platform, physical AI at a $6bn TAM, and auto projected to outgrow SAAR by high single digits," Stifel analysts said in an investor note. "That said, the CY30 model of +12-14% revenue CAR, 53% GM and 38% OM is potentially below expectations (see changes vs. the prior LT model below). The NT to MT GM path also remains unclear, weighing on EPS power versus analog peers." 
onsemi shares edged up 2% during market trading on Wednesday. 
During the presentation , onsemi CEO Hassane El-Khoury explained power remains the last bottleneck to expanding the AI data center buildout. 
"We've seen the first limitation with compute," he said. "We've lived through it, and we've unlocked it with advancements in technology and capacity. And we've also seen it with memory. We're actually—I would argue we're living through it with memory with advancements that are going to break through." 
"But, to solve the power, it is not a new product," he added. "It is not a new technology. It is not a new system. It is a layering effect of a value stack that has to work across top to bottom to deliver on that power density with the efficiency that is required to scale, starting with the foundation of technology into a deployment of products that extract the capabilities of these technologies and together create these solutions that are going to solve these customer problems and deliver the systems with the value and scale that will solve those generational problems." 
"Management pointed to 800V and higher stepping down to 6V or less in AI data centers; 13.8kV to 34.5kV for industrial solid-state transformers; and 400V to 900V+ in xEV," Stifel noted. "ON sized its opportunity at a $213bn TAM, of which $118bn, or more than half, sits in power."
