title: Advanced monitoring coming soon to a machine near you with maxon MIND - Design World
query: ("Maxon" OR "maxon group") ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-09-01 before:2026-10-01
content_text:
Advanced monitoring coming soon to a machine near you with maxon MIND
By Lisa Eitel | September 17, 2026 
Soon, a new “ m otion in sights and d iagnostics” service from Swiss precision-drive specialist maxon called maxon MIND will help machine builders and plant engineers add condition monitoring and diagnostics capabilities to their equipment.
Electric motors are often the best sensor in a machine. After all, the motor signals a controller already reads reflect the condition of the entire drive system and its environment. maxon MIND turns those existing signals into diagnoses by monitoring the motor … and with it all the mechanical components connected downstream.
maxon MIND is a scalable service that works with standard components, so implementation is fast. Once running, maxon MIND yields machine condition-based-maintenance and AGV fleet-management capabilities to prevent personnel injuries and unexpected machine downtime. 
Developed in-house over years by an interdisciplinary team, maxon MIND works like this:
There’s an application already driven by a maxon motor, gearbox, encoder, and controller(s).
At the primary controller, a small software package installs and then runs a script to trigger a diagnostic cycle, generate references, record motor signals, and then enrich collected data with context and distillation for analysis.
The system then sends the collected and condensed data over a secure internet connection (via MQTT, for example) to the Cloud-based maxon MIND platform. Once there, the data is analyzed by a machine-learning model and compared to the drive’s reference state. Deviations and anomalies are flagged.
Integrated data, condition analyses, and historical trends are accessed through an interface made possible with an application programming interface (API) from maxon. So, personnel can pull results into plant dashboards and fleet-management systems. Diagnoses from the maxon MIND system are traceable, which is necessary in safety-critical design and regulated industries. Via the API, maxon MIND also integrates with the maxon Cloud.
Machine learning is commonly associated with massive data requirements, high computational demands, and expensive hardware. In contrast, maxon MIND builds models with fewer than 100 reference cycles and runs diagnostics on fewer than 20 cycles. So, a model of a design (such as the AGV shown here) can be created in less than 10 minutes … and condition diagnosis takes less than a minute. Image: maxon 
Once maxon MIND is officially released to the industry (expected in 2027), machine builders aiming to leverage the service will first consult with maxon on their design load profiles, usage cycles, and environmental conditions. Then rapid prototyping and early testing (followed by system testing and validation under real operating conditions) will inform changes and the calibration of models. Final implementation will include optimization and fine-tuning of parameters or reference cycles.
Cybersecurity is ensured through the way collected machine data is anonymized and secured with maxon privacy measures complementing Cloud and security services. In short, maxon MIND doesn’t need to know who the end user is or what specific application is running. To uniquely identify the corresponding machine learning model, maxon MIND only needs data that’s easily anonymized — for example, a drive’s part and serial number.
Q&A with maxon MIND program lead 
For more on how maxon MIND actually works, we asked business development manager and program lead for maxon MIND Claude Jaquemet a few questions. Here’s what he had to say.
Design World: Early literature detailing maxon MIND details how the software logs machine data during regular operation (and compares it to mechatronic system models) with a frequency that depends on the application and machine builder. But the maxon MIND system needs relatively small data volumes (not enormous datasets) thanks to the “integration of domain-specific expertise into the models” of how a motor, gearbox, and load physically relate.
What does domain-specific expertise mean in this context? 
Jaquemet: In maxon MIND, domain-specific expertise means incorporating the known physical relationships and operating context of the mechatronic drive system into the model. This includes knowledge of the motor, controller, mechanical load, motion cycle, configuration, and relevant environmental conditions. It is interdisciplinary application knowledge, based on the long experience of maxon.
maxon MIND software embeds into the machine builder’s existing user interfaces, so the latter keeps its own look and feel while maxon MIND works in the background. Through the software, end users can view recurring issues, long-term trends, and ways to optimize operations. What’s more, maxon MIND has modest computing power and memory needs. Image: maxon 
Design World: With this offering, a machine learning model is trained on the OEM’s own data about actual system behavior … plus, the models can be tuned so that a condition warning is genuinely a warning.
How does maxon MIND differentiate a real problem from slight and acceptable wear over time? 
Jaquemet: With application-tailored models and high sensitivity. Therefore, maxon MIND doesn’t apply one universal wear threshold. It tracks the drive system relative to its application-specific initial state and visualizes the progression over time. Together with the machine builder, the model sensitivity and the boundary between acceptable condition and action-required condition are validated for the particular application. The result supports condition-based maintenance decisions.
Design World: We understand the architecture can be configured for different levels of complexity … and sensitivity can be adjusted for challenging situations involving cleanrooms, assemblies subject to vibrations, and extreme temperatures.
How exactly does maxon MIND distinguish problems from normal operating conditions? 
Jaquemet: maxon MIND doesn’t rely on a universal definition of normal. A machine-learning model is created for the specific motor in its actual application and is trained on an initial reference state. Later measurements are compared with this application-specific model to detect deviations and wear trends. Also, various potential fault-modes are considered in the training of the initial reference state, to which the application is continuously compared. For example, to compensate for temperature effects, the applicable payload, the reference cycle itself, and the drivetrain configuration need to remain consistent during data acquisition.
Design World: Potential applications include those in laboratory automation (to protect sample integrity and throughput while holding quality consistent); medical devices (to prevent any situations capable of jeopardizing patient safety); and general industrial automation — for avoiding downtime, minimizing the waste of spare parts, and boosting overall equipment effectiveness (OEE).
In more general terms, what are the target applications? 
Jaquemet: maxon MIND is designed for critical applications where an unexpected drive-system failure could affect personal safety, reliability, availability, process quality, or the user experience. Relevant application areas include medical devices, industrial and laboratory automation, and logistics. Technically, the application must allow repeatable diagnostic cycles under controlled and comparable load conditions. maxon MIND generally performs best where high sensitivity of the condition indication is required.
Design World: Can the motor signals reflect the condition of the whole powertrain, and how can the engineer localize a problem to one component? 
Jaquemet: The electrical motor signals contain information influenced by the motor, gearbox, encoder, coupling, and driven mechanics. maxon MIND therefore assesses the condition of the complete drive system rather than only the motor. Component-level detection of faults is generally feasible, but it depends on the particular drivetrain. Beyond general component failure patterns, application-specific validation against known faults, inspections, or service findings help with the interpretation of the condition indication.

India India Secures Up to $12 Billion in Semiconductor Investment Pledges Under Semicon 2.0 
September 17, 2026 651 1 minute read 
Facebook X LinkedIn Tumblr Pinterest Reddit VKontakte Odnoklassniki Pocket 
New Delhi — India has secured semiconductor investment commitments worth between $11 billion and $12 billion under Semicon 2.0, the second phase of the government’s semiconductor program, Union Electronics and IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said Thursday.
Speaking at Semicon India 2026, Vaishnaw said the commitments cover semiconductor equipment, materials, gases, chemicals and substrates, with the investments expected to materialize over the next two to three years.
The minister said companies will decide where to locate their semiconductor projects based on factors including policy certainty, government support and the strength of the surrounding ecosystem.
“Industry chooses the location depending upon where they feel more comfortable, how much policy certainty they see, what kind of support they see from governments, from the other ecosystem fields,” he said.
Semicon 2.0, approved with an outlay of Rs 1.27 lakh crore, focuses on chip design, semiconductor equipment and materials, fabrication plants, advanced packaging, research and development, and workforce development.
At the event, Tata Electronics signed an agreement with Ascendas First Space to develop a 363-acre vendor park that will support the supplier ecosystem surrounding its semiconductor fabrication plant in Dholera, Gujarat.
Tata Electronics also signed agreements with Fujifilm to localize critical semiconductor materials and with JSR Corporation for photoresists and advanced chemicals for the Dholera plant.
The program could attract about Rs 4 lakh crore in investment and support roughly Rs 2 lakh crore in semiconductor production over its duration, according to a recent report.
Fiscal incentives include 40% capital expenditure support for silicon fabrication plants on a pari-passu basis and up to 75% combined central and state government support for research, development and talent initiatives. (Source: IANS)

Robigo Bio eyes commercialization for its ag biologicals with Leaps by Bayer investment
September 17, 2026 | Jennifer Marston 
Agtech 
Biomanufacturing & biologicals 
Investing 
Startups & funding 
US & Canada 
Dr. Andee Wallace, Founder and CEO of Robigo. 
Image credit: Robigo Bio 
Robigo Bio has closed a Series A financing round to accelerate the commercial launch of its crop biological products, which the company claims can match or outperform synthetic chemistries instead of merely complementing them.
Importantly, these products will be simple for growers to integrate into their existing operations, says Dr. Andee Wallace, founder and CEO of Robigo.
“Growers shouldn’t have to choose between a product that works and one that’s affordable or sustainable. If you go out and talk with growers, you know what they want: something that’s simple that works with what they’re doing today.”
This, she adds, is exactly what Robigo aims to do with its engineered microbes.
Leaps by Bayer led the round, with participation from Illumina Ventures , SVG Thrive , Congruent Ventures , and Endeavor8 . Financial terms were not disclosed.
Cambridge, Massachusetts-based Robigo has two products currently gearing up for commercial launch. One, an engineered microbial seed treatment for soybean Sudden Death Syndrome, is slated for launch in 2028. A second, which targets fusarium wilt in lettuce and berries, will launch in 2029.
Funding will also support the company’s expansion into work on soil-borne pathogens in broad-acre crops, which Robigo claims is a $10 billion market.
Close up of soybean sudden death syndrome. Image credit: Robigo 
Engineering vs wild-type microbes 
Nearly all commercial microbial products on the market today use wild-type organisms—naturally occurring microbes selected for a useful characteristic, such as antifungal properties or nitrogen-fixing bacterium. Product development is more about finding the right strain of such microbes rather than engineering something.
Robigo takes a different approach. Instead of finding a microbe with fungal-fighting properties, it chooses one then “programs” it to produce the desired active ingredients. Robigo starts with microbes chosen for their shelf stability and manufacturing economics, then engineers in new traits computationally, including both the active bioingredients and safety parameters, claims Wallace.
“We identify microbes that serve as a really solid foundation to build high-performing products on top of — they have the shelf stability, they have the manufacturing capabilities to be cost-effective — and then we engineer in these new traits that allow us to be much higher performing than what biologicals are doing today, and also have a really improved safety profile,” she adds.
It is, she claims, “an entirely different way to develop microbial and biological products from what’s been historically done.”
These engineered microbes are applied as a one-time seed treatment and continuously produce and deliver active ingredients throughout the season, with no change to existing grower workflows. Critically, Robigo says they don’t require cold-chain storage, which has been a longstanding logistical headache for ag biological products.
The company’s proprietary ARGO platform ties these capabilities together across three components: microbial strain engineering, strain selection, and computational design of the bioactive compounds the microbes produce. Together, Robigo claims the platform can take a new biological product from design to field-tested in under 20 months. The industry norm is roughly three to five years.
Robigo’s first field trials last year marked what it believes is a regulatory first: field deployment of a living engineered microbe expressing new traits, cleared through the USDA and the EPA.
Early data from those trials has been encouraging, says Wallace. The soybean SDS treatment is on track to match the performance of commercially available chemistries at half the cost. That’s no small feat at a time when SDS causes an estimated $200–$500 million in annual losses for U.S. soybean farmers.
The fusarium wilt product for specialty crops showed a 3x yield increase compared to untreated controls.
Dr. Andee Wallace in the lab. Image credit: Robigo Bio 
Building a biologicals engine 
The new investment is the next step in a multi-year relationship between Robigo and Leaps, Bayer’s venture arm.
“They are not just developing a single product but rather building an engine that can rapidly address diverse soil-borne pathogens across broadacre crops,” Dr. Juergen Eckhardt, EVP and head of Leaps by Bayer, noted in a statement.
Robigo raised its seed round at the end of 2022, closing in early 2023. Wallace acknowledged the difficulty of the current climate but said the company’s ability to put field data on the table made the difference.
The Series A will also fund continued registration work. Robigo has already initiated the regulatory process for its soybean seed treatment product, another milestone Wallace flagged as significant for an engineered-organism product category that is still defining its regulatory path.

DuPont de Nemours, Inc. DD benefits from its innovation-driven investment, productivity actions and acquisitions amid uneven construction demand and persistent cost pressure. 
DD's shares are down 45.6% in the past year compared to the Zacks Chemicals Diversified industry's 3.3% decline. 
Zacks Investment Research Image Source: Zacks Investment Research 
Let's find out why DD stock is worth retaining at the moment. 
Productivity, Innovation & Acquisitions Aid DD Stock 
DuPont remains focused on organic growth through innovation, commercial execution and targeted acquisitions. Its innovation-driven investment is focused on several high-growth areas. DD's portfolio is exposed to healthcare, water, aerospace and electric vehicle (EV) applications, which supported 4% organic sales growth in second-quarter 2026. The company is expanding its innovation pipeline through direct lithium extraction solutions in Water, Liveo products for biopharma and new solutions for electric vehicles and battery energy storage. 
The acquisition of Spectrum Plastics Group, a leading manufacturer of specialty medical devices and components, strengthened DuPont's position in stable and fast-growing healthcare end markets. It is also in sync with its focus on high-growth, customer-driven innovation for the healthcare market. The buyout of Donatelle Plastics also enhances DD's exposure in healthcare, expanding its expertise in the medical device market segments.
DD said in August 2026 that it still had more than $1 billion available for potential mergers and acquisitions and was evaluating opportunities in water and healthcare. It also indicated that prospective acquisitions should add to the company's growth algorithm and meet disciplined return thresholds. These actions support a more focused portfolio while retaining flexibility for selective growth investments and shareholder returns.
DuPont is also benefiting from cost synergy savings and productivity improvement actions. Its operating system is producing measurable cost and execution gains. In second-quarter 2026, net productivity improved and contributed to operating leverage. Management is targeting net productivity equal to 3% of cost of goods sold and expects to reach that run rate within about 18 months from August 2026. The 80/20 program is also moving from pilot work to implementation across four Diversified Industrials businesses, with a few million dollars of EBITDA benefit expected in second-half 2026. Full-year 2026 operating EBITDA guidance of $1.75-$1.77 billion implies continued benefits from organic growth and productivity. 
Story Continues 
Construction and Cost Headwinds Weigh On DuPont 
DuPont's Building Technologies business remains exposed to a mixed construction backdrop. Organic sales rose in the low single digits in the second quarter as residential and non-residential demand improved, led by Asia Pacific, but management said single-family housing remained soft. 
DD expects Building Technologies sales to increase only slightly for full-year 2026, indicating that the broader recovery remains limited. The company also noted that residential performance was above its underlying market in second-quarter 2026, which may make sustained growth more dependent on favorable market mix and end-market stabilization. This leaves Diversified Industrials exposed to uneven construction conditions even as aerospace and EV applications provide offsets.
Higher oil and gas-related input costs remain a margin drag in 2026 even though DuPont expects pricing to offset the dollar impact. Management said about $90 million of pricing is planned for full-year 2026, with most of it in the second half. Price-cost dynamics reduced second-quarter 2026 operating EBITDA margin by 30 basis points. The company expects a 50-basis-point margin drag in second-half 2026 and a 30-basis-point drag for the full year.

GoldHaven Highlights Landmark US$450 Million U.S. Government Investment to Secure Tungsten Supply Chain
Investing News Network 
September 17, 2026 
GoldHaven Resources Corp. ("GoldHaven" or the "Company") highlights the recent announcement of a US$450 million U.S. government investment in The Elmet Group aimed at expanding domestic tungsten capacity and securing America's tungsten supply chain.
The landmark commitment provides another powerful indication of tungsten's growing strategic importance to national security, defence, aerospace and advanced manufacturing.
Highlights 
US$450 million U.S. government investment in The Elmet Group announced to strengthen America's domestic tungsten supply chain.
More than 800 metres drilled at GoldHaven's historic Kuhn tungsten system in northern British Columbia.
Broad skarn intervals encountered , including approximately 20 metres of skarn in the second drill hole. Assays are pending.
Historical drilling returned 13.0 metres grading 0.55% WO₃ and 11.3 metres grading 0.59% WO₃ with 0.10% MoS₂.*
Historical estimate of approximately 616,500 tonnes grading 0.48% WO₃ across four modelled lenses.*
"Tungsten is increasingly recognized as one of the world's most strategically important critical minerals," said Rob Birmingham, President and CEO of GoldHaven. "The message coming out of Washington is increasingly clear: securing reliable and diversified sources of tungsten is now a national-security priority. This landmark investment comes at an exciting time for GoldHaven as we advance drilling at the historic Kuhn tungsten system within our 100%-owned Magno Project in northern British Columbia."
GoldHaven's maiden diamond drill program at Kuhn is targeting the geometry, continuity and potential extensions of the historically documented tungsten-bearing skarn system. More than 800 metres have now been drilled from the first drill pad, with laboratory assay results pending.
Current drilling at the Kuhn tungsten system and representative core from the program are shown below. Core descriptions are based on visual observations; laboratory assays are pending.
Kuhn drill site, Magno Project — diamond drilling underway at the Kuhn tungsten system, northern British Columbia.
GOH26-02, 60.50–60.75 m — reddish garnet skarn with visible molybdenite blebs and widespread chlorite alteration.
Historical drilling at the Kuhn tungsten system reportedly returned intercepts including 13.0 metres grading 0.55% WO₃ and 11.3 metres grading 0.59% WO₃ and 0.10% MoS₂ . Historical work also outlined an estimate of approximately 616,500 tonnes grading 0.48% WO₃ across four modelled lenses at the Kuhn–Dead Goat system. These historical results and estimates pre-date NI 43-101 and have not yet been independently verified through GoldHaven's current drilling program.
The historical estimate and drilling results pre-date NI 43-101 and should not be considered a current mineral resource or mineral reserve. A Qualified Person has not completed sufficient work to classify the historical estimate as a current mineral resource, and GoldHaven is not treating the historical estimate as a current mineral resource. Historical results are not necessarily indicative of future results.
Located in British Columbia's established Cassiar mining district, the Magno Project provides GoldHaven with exposure to tungsten, alongside silver, lead, zinc, copper, gold and indium, within a stable and strategically aligned North American jurisdiction.
GoldHaven believes the announcement reinforces the importance of developing secure mineral supply chains outside traditional sources of supply and highlights the potential strategic relevance of tungsten projects located in the United States and allied jurisdictions, including Canada.
As governments continue directing substantial capital and policy support toward strengthening domestic and allied mineral supply chains, GoldHaven believes the tungsten sector is entering an increasingly important period of investment, development and consolidation.
The race to secure critical minerals is no longer a future story—it is happening now. 
The US$450 million investment relates specifically to The Elmet Group. GoldHaven is not a recipient of the investment and has no relationship with The Elmet Group.

GoldHaven Resources Corp. is a Canadian junior exploration company focused on advancing highly prospective mineral projects in North and South America. The Company's flagship asset is the district-scale Magno Project in the Cassiar District of northern British Columbia. GoldHaven also owns the Three Guardsmen copper-gold project in British Columbia and the Copeçal Gold Project in Mato Grosso, Brazil. In addition, the Company holds a portfolio of critical mineral projects in Brazil.

content_text:
Project NEWBORN achieves hydrogen-electric propulsion milestone for aircraft
September 17, 2026 
11:11 am 
MRO & Production 
Honeywell Aerospace , Pipistrel 
NEWBORN develops and demonstrate the TRL 4 ground demonstrator of the overall propulsion system using fuel cells technology for electricity generation © NEWBORN 
Honeywell Aerospace said its engineering team in Brno, the Czech Republic, has successfully integrated the main subsystems of a hydrogen fuel-cell power source capable of generating and supplying electricity for an aircraft, marking progress in a European project aimed at developing low-emission aviation technology.
The work is part of Project NEWBORN, launched in 2023 and funded by the European Union through the Clean Aviation Joint Undertaking. The project brings together 18 companies and research organisations from ten European countries to develop an aerospace-qualified hydrogen fuel cell propulsion system capable of delivering power in the megawatt class.
The completed integration brings together fuel cells and other electrical and supporting systems into a functional hydrogen power source. The next stage will be a ground demonstration of the complete propulsion system, in which hydrogen fuel cells and batteries will provide electricity to a megawatt-class electric motor driving an aircraft propeller.
Honeywell has developed a dedicated test platform to replicate a range of aircraft functions and assess the hydrogen power source under controlled conditions. The platform is installed at the research and engineering facility operated by ÚJV Řež near Prague and includes power generation, fluid distribution, electrical and control systems, safety equipment and heat-rejection systems.
Engineers have tested the integrated system for electrical functionality, leak tightness, fluid operating parameters, interaction between subsystems, control algorithms and protection mechanisms. Further testing will focus on increasing the system’s power range and improving its stability and resilience, Honeywell said.
The project involves multiple teams working on hardware, software, modelling, simulations and integration. Companies and research institutions including PowerCell, Fraunhofer, Test-Fuchs, Siemens Industry Software, KU Leuven, Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg and CIRA have contributed to different elements of the programme.
The hydrogen power source will now be transferred to Gorizia, Italy, where the next phase of testing will take place. There, it will be connected to battery systems supplied by Pipistrel and a megawatt-class electric propulsion system jointly developed by the University of Nottingham, Honeywell Aerospace and Pipistrel.
The project is intended to bring together technologies developed across Europe and demonstrate their operation as an integrated hydrogen-electric propulsion system, a step towards the use of hydrogen fuel cells in future aircraft.

title: Oral Obesity Drugs Are Coming: Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly File for South Korean Approval, Setting Up Launch Race Next Year - BigGo Finance
query: ("Eli Lilly and Company" OR "Eli Lilly") (Korea OR Korean) after:2026-09-01 before:2026-10-01
content_text:
Oral Obesity Drugs Are Coming: Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly File for South Korean Approval, Setting Up Launch Race Next Year
Add preferred source 
Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly have each filed for marketing authorization with South Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety for their oral obesity treatments, Wegovy Pill and Foundayo. Domestic launches could come as early as next year. Wegovy Pill touts weight-loss efficacy using the same peptide-based ingredient as its injectable counterpart, while Foundayo emphasizes dosing convenience as a small-molecule compound. Both products launched in the U.S. at $149 per month, significantly below the roughly $1,000 price tag for injectable versions. Meanwhile, Hanmi Pharmaceutical's domestically developed injectable obesity drug EPPE is in the final stages of the approval process with an October target, setting the stage for a multi-layered competitive landscape in South Korea's obesity treatment market across formulation, price, and efficacy.
Key Elements 
Novo Nordisk Eli Lilly Wegovy Pill Foundayo Hanmi Pharmaceutical EPPE South Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety Semaglutide Orforglipron GLP-1 
Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly, the two companies that have dominated the global obesity treatment market, are preparing for another head-to-head battle in South Korea—this time with oral obesity drugs. With both companies recently filing for marketing authorization with South Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, South Korean consumers could have pill-form obesity treatments available as early as the second half of next year.
According to industry sources on the 17th, Novo Nordisk has filed for approval of Wegovy Pill (active ingredient: semaglutide), while Eli Lilly has submitted Foundayo (active ingredient: orforglipron). Given that it typically takes about a year from filing to market launch, a domestic launch next year is highly likely. However, neither company has disclosed specific launch timelines.
A 'Game Changer' That Eliminates Injection Hassles
Oral obesity treatments have long been viewed as products that could reshape the obesity drug market. Existing injectable treatments like Wegovy and Mounjaro require refrigeration and must be injected once a week into the abdomen or thigh—a significant inconvenience. Pill formulations dramatically reduce these burdens.
Pricing is also substantially lower than injectables. Both oral treatments launched in the U.S. at $149 per month (approximately ₩210,000) at the starting dose. That's roughly 85% cheaper than the $1,000 (approximately ₩1.4 million) U.S. starting price for injectable Wegovy and Mounjaro.
Efficacy vs. Convenience: Divergent Strategies
Both products act on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptors that induce satiety, but they differ markedly in drug composition and dosing requirements.
Wegovy Pill uses the same peptide-based ingredient as injectable Wegovy, positioning weight-loss efficacy as its primary strength. In April, Novo Nordisk reported that Wegovy Pill's weight-loss effect was on average about 3 percentage points higher than Foundayo's. The company also disclosed its own analysis showing that the likelihood of treatment discontinuation due to adverse reactions was about four times higher with Foundayo.
Foundayo, by contrast, is a synthetic drug made from small-molecule compounds and is considered superior in dosing convenience. As a peptide-based drug, Wegovy Pill is poorly absorbed in the stomach and requires an absorption enhancer; it must be taken on an empty stomach with water, followed by a period of avoiding food intake. Foundayo is free from such restrictions.
Will a Wider Range of Options Expand the South Korean Market?
With more choices in dosing method, duration, and price, observers suggest the obesity treatment market itself is likely to expand. One pharmaceutical and biotech industry source said, "There are many patients with a body mass index (BMI) of 27 or higher who qualify for obesity treatment but haven't received it. In South Korea, even in diabetes treatment, many patients have opted for oral medications over insulin or GLP-1 injections—this could break down similar psychological barriers."
However, some believe oral treatments won't quickly replace injectables. Unlike once-weekly injections, pills must be taken daily. A 37-year-old office worker who has been on Wegovy for about three months said, "I usually inject once on the weekend, but if I had to take it every day, I'd probably need to set an alarm. Unless the price drops dramatically, I'll stick with the injectable."
Domestic Drug 'EPPE' Joins the Fray—A Three-Way Battle Looms
In the South Korean market, latecomer Hanmi Pharmaceutical's injectable obesity drug EPPE is poised for launch as early as next month, further complicating the competitive landscape. Hanmi Pharmaceutical is in the final stages of the approval process with an October target for EPPE's marketing authorization from the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, and is preparing to bring the product to market within about a month of approval. The official launch target is within this year.
The key question is EPPE's pricing. Currently, the four-week starting-dose wholesale prices are ₩216,000 for Wegovy 0.25mg and ₩278,000 for Mounjaro 2.5mg. Industry observers suggest that EPPE, as a latecomer, could launch in the ₩100,000 range (approximately $72) for a four-week supply. Hanmi Pharmaceutical has drawn a line, stating, "No price has been determined at this time."
Industry insiders believe price competitiveness will be crucial for EPPE to break through the two-horse race between Wegovy and Mounjaro, which have accumulated extensive global clinical data and prescribing experience. A source with over a decade in the pharmaceutical industry said, "Hanmi Pharmaceutical has a sales network targeting local clinics that foreign pharmaceutical companies would find hard to match. If they also have price competitiveness, they could rapidly expand market share, particularly in the primary care segment."
There is already precedent for latecomer entry driving down prices of existing products. In August of last year, ahead of Mounjaro's South Korean launch, Novo Nordisk cut Wegovy's wholesale prices by approximately 10–40% depending on dosage. The starting dose of 0.25mg for a four-week supply dropped from ₩372,000 to ₩216,000—a reduction of over 40%—making it ₩62,000 cheaper than Mounjaro's starting dose of 2.5mg for four weeks. Depending on the price tag EPPE carries, the market dynamics could shift again.
EPPE's arrival could also broaden the patient base for obesity treatments. Beyond existing users switching to EPPE, people who never started treatment due to cost burdens could enter the market. Lee Seung-kyu, vice chairman of the Korea Biotechnology Association, said, "If it launches in the ₩100,000 range, that's nearly half the price of current products, making it an attractive option for people who couldn't afford treatment. New demand could expand the market itself."
Hanmi Pharmaceutical is touting EPPE's clinical data from Korean patients as a key differentiator. In a Phase 3 trial conducted at multiple university hospitals in South Korea involving 448 obese patients, EPPE demonstrated an average weight reduction of 9.75% after 40 weeks of treatment. Notably, in the subgroup of women with a BMI below 30, the average reduction was 12.20%. The company emphasizes that it has directly secured efficacy and safety data in Korean obese patients. EPPE will be produced at the Pyeongtaek Bio Plant for domestic supply.
With oral obesity drugs entering the South Korean market and a domestically developed injectable launching simultaneously, the country's obesity treatment market is expected to be reshaped into a multi-layered competitive landscape across formulation, price, and efficacy starting next year.

REUTERS/Annegret Hilse/File Photo NEW DELHI: German chipmaker Infineon Technologies said on Wednesday that it has entered into an agreement to sell its NOR FLASH and F-RAM business in a $1.12 billion all-cash deal to Winbond . 
The business serves customers across automotive, industrial and infrastructure markets. 
Subject to obtaining the required regulatory approvals, the companies expect to conclude the transaction in the second half of 2027, as per a joint statement. 
“The transaction represents a highly compelling strategic outcome for all stakeholders,” said Peter Schiefer, president of Infineon’s Automotive Division. “It allows Infineon to further focus its portfolio and capital allocation on its core growth drivers. At the same time, it enables our NOR Flash and F-RAM business to unlock its full potential.” 
The combination of Winbond’s existing memory portfolio and Infineon’s NOR Flash and F-RAM business will provide customers with a broad and complementary portfolio of NOR Flash and F-RAM products, the statement added. 
Winbond will operate the acquired business as a standalone entity with headquarters in Silicon Valley in the United States. 
Infineon will continue to offer a portfolio of specialty memory solutions, including SRAM, HYPERRAM, nvSRAM, and SONOS-based radiation-hardened memory solutions. 
These technologies remain an important part of Infineon's portfolio across automotive, industrial, infrastructure, aerospace, and defense applications, including a product offering of high-reliability memory solutions for space missions.

Semicon 2.0 secures $12 billion in investment pledges: Ashwini Vaishnaw
Union Electronics and IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on Thursday that the Central government has secured investment commitments of $11-12 billion under Semicon 2.0, the second phase of its semiconductor programme.
Speaking at Semicon India 2026, Vaishnaw said the commitments span semiconductor equipment, materials, gases, chemicals and substrates and investments expected to materialise over the next two to three years.
The minister said it is the prerogative of the companies to decide where their semiconductor projects would be based, considering factors such as policy certainty, government support and the strength of the surrounding ecosystem.
“Industry chooses the location depending upon where they feel more comfortable, how much policy certainty they see, what kind of support they see from governments, from the other ecosystem fields,” he said.
Semicon 2.0, approved with an outlay of Rs 1.27 lakh crore, targets chip design, equipment and materials, fabs, advanced packaging, R&D and talent development.
The event also saw Tata Electronics signing a deal with Ascendas First Space to develop a 363‑acre vendor park to build the supplier ecosystem around its semiconductor fab in Dholera, Gujarat.
It also signed pacts with Fujifilm for localisation of critical semiconductor materials and JSR Corporation for photoresists and advanced chemicals for the Dholera fab.

The company introduced its Embedded Power Platform and highlighted vertical gallium nitride and silicon carbide technologies to improve power density, efficiency and thermal performance across AI, automotive and industrial applications. 
onsemi set ambitious 2030 financial targets: 12%–14% annual revenue growth, nearly $11 billion in revenue, 53% gross margins, 38% operating margins and more than $3.5 billion in free cash flow, while planning to return 100% of free cash flow to shareholders after investments and acquisitions. 
3 Robotics Stocks Under $10: Value, Momentum, or Bet? 
onsemi (NASDAQ:ON) outlined a strategy centered on power-density technologies for artificial intelligence data centers, electric vehicles, industrial systems and "Physical AI," while setting long-term revenue, margin and free-cash-flow targets through 2030. 
At the company's analyst event, President and CEO Hassane El-Khoury said AI infrastructure is increasingly constrained not only by compute and memory, but by the ability to efficiently deliver and manage power. He said future systems will require power that is distributed, efficient and able to operate under sustained peak loads. 
→ IonQ and NVIDIA Just Cracked a Major Quantum Computing Bottleneck 
MarketBeat Week in Review – 08/03 - 08/07 
"More power is really not enough," El-Khoury said. "We need better power." 
Embedded Power Platform and high-voltage technologies 
The company introduced its Embedded Power Platform, or EPP, which it described as a platform rather than a single product. EPP uses a silicon wafer as an active package and embeds heterogeneous semiconductor products, including silicon carbide and gallium nitride components, into a wafer-level architecture. onsemi said the approach is intended to improve electrical, thermal and mechanical performance simultaneously while reducing system-development time. 
→ 2 Stocks Breaking Out Post-FOMC With One Thing in Common 
The AI Chip Stock Making a Quiet Move Toward Dominance 
El-Khoury said EPP is already being sampled for automotive, industrial and AI data-center applications using the company's existing 12-inch manufacturing process. He said the platform can be used with onsemi's high-voltage technologies and its Treo intelligence platform, which is designed to support modular power-control solutions across voltage levels and end markets. 
Story Continues 
The company also highlighted vertical gallium nitride, or vGaN, technology. El-Khoury said onsemi has developed, sampled and manufactured vertical GaN devices that have been placed on customer boards for automotive, industrial and AI data-center applications. He said production is supported by the company's Syracuse facility and would not require a new greenfield fab investment. 
→ Generac Plugs into Amazon for an $8B AI-Powered Deal 
Subaru said it is evaluating onsemi's embedded power module technology for future vehicle platforms. A Subaru representative said the technology could offer higher power density, dual-sided cooling, improved electrical control and system-level cost reductions, though the automaker said it continues to evaluate how the technology may fit into its vehicle plans. 
AI data-center opportunity 
Achyut Shah, president of onsemi's Power Solutions Group, said AI processors are moving from consuming hundreds of watts toward kilowatt-scale power requirements, while rack-level power needs are rising from tens of kilowatts toward megawatts. He said this transition will require a shift from traditional AC distribution architectures to high-voltage DC systems extending from the grid to computing equipment. 
Shah said the initial transition toward higher-voltage rack designs and sidecar architectures is expected to begin ramping in the next 12 to 18 months. He said broader adoption of solid-state transformers could begin around late 2028 or early 2029. 
According to Shah, onsemi estimates its semiconductor content opportunity could increase from about $15,000 per rack to more than $115,000 per rack as data-center infrastructure transitions to higher-voltage architectures. He said the company expects AI data-center revenue to exceed $500 million in 2026, more than double from the prior year, and to double again in 2027. The company's long-term model assumes AI data-center revenue grows at least 10 percentage points faster than the underlying market through 2030. 
Using a hypothetical 40% market compound annual growth rate, Shah said onsemi projects its AI data-center revenue could grow at least 50% annually from a $500 million base in 2026 to more than $2.5 billion in 2030. 
The company cited several claimed product-performance benchmarks, including an 800-volt-to-6-volt or 12-volt conversion system using vGaN that it said offers 20% better efficiency and 20% lower size than competing solutions. It also described an EPP-based silicon carbide JFET solid-state circuit-breaker design that it said is 50% smaller and operates 20% cooler than the nearest competing product. 
Shah also announced that onsemi won a "major" Vcore socket, with revenue expected to begin by the end of 2026. 
Automotive and industrial growth plans 
Sudhir Gopalswamy, group president for Intelligent Sensing and Analog and Mixed-Signal Group, said onsemi expects automotive revenue to grow about 9% annually from 2026 through 2030, despite the company's assumption that global light-vehicle production, or SAAR, remains flat during that period. 
The automotive strategy is built around electrification, autonomous-driving content and software-defined vehicles using zonal electrical architectures. Gopalswamy said the company plans to continue advancing silicon carbide performance, increase device-voltage capability toward 1,400 volts to support 1,000-volt batteries, and introduce intelligent current controllers for traction inverters.

For EPP-based traction inverters, Gopalswamy said the platform could double power while using half the area, resulting in four times the power density. He also projected that onsemi's opportunity across electrification, advanced driver-assistance systems and zonal architectures could reach up to $2,000 of content per vehicle. 
In industrial markets, the company is targeting 10% growth through 2030, supported by grid upgrades, energy infrastructure, industrial automation and the broader AI-driven demand for power systems. Gopalswamy said Physical AI applications, excluding automotive, represent a potential $6 billion addressable market for onsemi by 2030. He said humanoid robots could represent about $900 of potential company content per unit by that year. 
Financial targets and capital allocation 
CFO Thad Trent said onsemi has invested $8.7 billion over the past five years, including $3.6 billion in research and development, $800 million for five tuck-in acquisitions and $4.3 billion in capital expenditures. He said the investments were directed toward power platforms, sensing, silicon carbide, vertical GaN and manufacturing capacity.

Trent said the financial model excludes the proposed Synaptics transaction. He said onsemi expects Synaptics, if the deal closes, to grow at more than 15% over the long term, generate gross margins above 55% and produce more than $200 million in synergies over the first 18 months. 
The company said it plans to continue investing in organic growth and acquisitions, maintain balance-sheet flexibility and return 100% of free cash flow to shareholders after those priorities. Trent said onsemi has $5.3 billion remaining under its existing share-repurchase authorization.

Vishal Sikka's Hang Ten Systems Raises $53 Mn In Fresh Seed Funding
2 min read 
ENR 2222 MU 
Temasek-backed Xora-led round comes as Hang Ten rapidly expands enterprise AI engagements with global companies including Aramco and Siemens Gamesa 
AI services startup Hang Ten Systems founded by former Infosys CEO Vishal Sikka, has raised an additional USD 53 million in seed funding led by Xora, a Temasek-backed investment firm, taking its total funding to USD 85 million, the company said on Thursday. 
Mayfield, which led Hang Ten's first seed round, and Aramco Ventures also participated in the latest round. The company did not disclose its valuation. 
The two seed rounds were completed five weeks apart, as Hang Ten moved rapidly from fundraising to securing multi-million-dollar contracts with global enterprises, the company said. 
The company said it has signed several contracts spanning advisory and software development work, with projects ranging from short-term consulting assignments to multi-year development programmes. Some projects are already being delivered, while others have been completed. 
Hang Ten provides advisory, transformation and applied-AI services to large enterprises. Its delivery model combines agentic code generation, a reusable library of AI-enabled skills and domain expertise to build, modify and operate enterprise software. 
The company said its approach is aimed at reducing the cost and time required for enterprise software implementation compared with traditional systems integration models. 
The new funding will be used to expand delivery capacity for projects already underway, grow its engineering and consulting teams and develop its platform, infrastructure and library of agentic skills, it said. 
"Enterprise technology has long been one of the largest cost lines in essential industries," said Phil Inagaki, managing partner and chief investment officer at Xora. He said the challenge for enterprises was not simply adopting AI but implementing it securely and economically at scale. 
Hang Ten is already working with Saudi Aramco on applications across several business functions, while Siemens Gamesa Renewable Energy is also among its enterprise customers. 
Mahdi Aladel, CEO of Aramco Ventures, said the breadth of Hang Ten's approach had led Aramco teams to identify multiple potential AI applications across its operations, with projects already being scoped. 
Siemens Gamesa CEO Vinod Philip said the company began working with Hang Ten two months ago on a limited set of outcomes and subsequently expanded the engagement after the startup delivered what was expected in terms of speed and quality. 
Hang Ten was founded by Sikka, who previously served as CEO of SAP from 2014 to 2019. The company's investor base also includes Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan, Micron Technology chairman and CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, and Yahoo co-founder and AME Cloud Ventures founding partner Jerry Yang. 
Yang has joined Hang Ten's board of directors. 
Sikka said the company's focus was on applying AI to critical enterprise systems while maintaining reliability. 
"AI can be the most powerful amplifier we have ever built," Sikka said. "But in the enterprise, AI's power must go hand-in-hand with reliability."

Physical AI drives autonomous driving upgrade; three efficiency factors lift AI accelerator demand
Jasper Jiang , Analyst
End-to-end autonomous driving has become the mainstream technology path, and the inference demand created by Physical AI in autonomous driving systems is, in turn, reshaping automotive system-on-chip (SoC) design.
Abstract
End-to-end autonomous driving has become the mainstream technology path, and the inference demand created by Physical AI in autonomous driving systems is, in turn, reshaping automotive system-on-chip (SoC) design. DIGITIMES presents a 3x3 matrix of key automotive SoC indicators for the AI era, organized around underlying hardware specifications, mid-layer efficiency performance, and upper-layer solution compatibility, as an evaluation framework for next-generation automotive SoC solutions. DIGITIMES believes that the AI accelerator will become the compute core of next-generation automotive SoCs, meeting the low-latency, low-system-power, and low-memory-bottleneck requirements of AI inference in autonomous driving systems.
As global industry consensus gradually forms around the three stages of AI evolution, attention is also shifting to the underlying engineering, core tasks, and key metrics for each stage, with hardware requirements differing accordingly. In the Agentic AI stage, AI systems must handle not only inference but also auxiliary tasks such as task scheduling and tool calling, so they rely on the compute strengths of the central processing unit (CPU), which is supporting demand for CPUs. Looking ahead to Physical AI, AI systems will need to perform real-time, accurate inference in diverse and changing physical environments. DIGITIMES believes the neural processing unit (NPU) will become the main compute core for Physical AI development.
This report covers how physical AI evolution is impacting automotive SoC design and the specifications offered by major vendors such as Nvidia, Qualcomm, and Mobileye.

TOPPAN Group Inaugurates New BOPP Film Manufacturing Line at Irplast in Italy
Enhancing supply capabilities using simultaneous biaxial orientation technology to bolster global supply of sustainable solutions
Tweet 
Tokyo – September 17, 2026 – TOPPAN Inc. (TOPPAN), a TOPPAN Group company and wholly owned subsidiary of TOPPAN Holdings Inc. (TYO: 7911), and its Italy-based film manufacturing subsidiary Irplast S.p.A. (Irplast), today announced the inauguration of a new manufacturing line for high-performance biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) films, marking the occasion with a ceremony on September 15, 2026.
An overview of this development will be included at the TOPPAN booth (East Hall 2, Booth No. 2R10) during TOKYO PACK 2026, to be held at Tokyo Big Sight from Wednesday, October 14 to Friday, October 16, 2026.
Background and Objectives
In its packaging business, the TOPPAN Group is accelerating the establishment of its global supply network for recycle-ready mono-material packaging to meet tightening environmental regulations - such as the EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) - and to drive the transition toward a circular economy.
Irplast, a TOPPAN Group company, is a premium film manufacturer equipped with advanced simultaneous biaxial orientation technology. Its unique expertise in minimizing thermal shrinkage provides BOPP films with exceptional heat resistance, mechanical strength, and superior transparency.
Through the operation of this line, together with existing capabilities, the plant will be able to establish an overall supply infrastructure of up to 30,000 tonnes per year for high-performance BOPP films. This deployment expands the TOPPAN Group’s production capabilities and enhances manufacturing efficiency, ensuring a stable, local supply to meet the surging demand for sustainable packaging in Europe and beyond.
Features of the New Manufacturing Line
・Developing High-Value Applications through Simultaneous Orientation Technology: 
The films produced on this line offer uniform physical properties and high dimensional stability achieved through the LISIM 1 simultaneous stretching process. Leveraging this robustness, TOPPAN and Irplast will actively develop high-end packaging applications that require durability even under demanding conditions, such as retort sterilization.
・Reducing Environmental Impact through Package Down Gauging: 
Utilizing the film’s superior mechanical strength, development will be focused toward "down gauging" (reducing film thickness). This enables a steady and continuous reduction in plastic consumption while maintaining essential packaging functions, directly supporting resource conservation goals.
Future Activities
The new line is expected to commence full commercial operations by late 2026, supplying high-performance BOPP films to packaging converters and global brand owners.
The combination of Irplast’s BOPP film manufacturing expertise and the TOPPAN Group’s broad base of technologies and solutions will expand sustainable solutions worldwide by driving use as a next-generation substrate in transparent GL BARRIER 2 films as well as unlocking new possibilities for high-performance, sustainable packaging solutions that contribute to a circular economy.
1 LISIM is Bruckner’s simultaneous stretching technology utilized by Irplast.
URL: https://www.irplast.com/bopp-film-division/ 
2 GL BARRIER is TOPPAN’s proprietary brand of transparent film products that deliver world-class barrier performance. Stable performance is enabled by a multi-layer structure combining a unique coating layer with a high-quality vapor-deposited layer. In recognition of their numerous outstanding features, GL BARRIER products are used in a wide variety of fields, including the food, healthcare/pharmaceutical, and industrial materials sectors. Combining the functions of the printing and barrier substrate layers into a single layer provides an alternative to aluminum foil with a streamlined layer structure.
https://www.toppan.com/en/living-industry/packaging/products/barrier_film/ 
About the TOPPAN Group
Established in Tokyo in 1900, the TOPPAN Group is a leading and diversified global provider committed to delivering sustainable, integrated solutions in fields including printing, communications, security, packaging, décor materials, electronics, and digital transformation. The TOPPAN Group’s global team of more than 50,000 employees offers optimal solutions enabled by industry-leading expertise and technologies to address the diverse challenges of every business sector and society and contribute to the achievement of shared sustainability goals.
https://www.holdings.toppan.com/en/

content_text:
Skyworks Just Told the Street the $22B Chip Merger Is Almost Done
Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) spent Tuesday acting like a company that can finally see the finish line on a deal Wall Street has been babysitting for almost a year.
The stock ripped about 14% to roughly $90. Qorvo (QRVO) climbed about 9% with it. Random RF-chip bounces do not move both names like that. This looked like the market pricing a merger that suddenly feels less like a regulatory maze and more like a calendar problem.
CEO Phil Brace has been saying the quiet part out loud. The combination with Qorvo is in its final stages. He told investors the company is preparing to close inside the calendar year, and maybe even inside Skyworks' current fiscal year that ends September 30. Markets do not hand out 14% days for polite conference chatter. They hand them out when the remaining risk starts to look procedural instead of existential.
## The Deal the Street Already Knows by Heart
Skyworks and Qorvo announced the combination back in October 2025. The structure is simple enough to write on a napkin. Qorvo shareholders get $32.50 a share in cash plus 0.96 Skyworks shares for each Qorvo share. Fixed exchange ratio. That is why QRVO now tends to move with SWKS when the close story improves.
Both stockholder groups already voted yes in February. U.S. antitrust is no longer the main fight. The HSR waiting period expired, and the FTC let a timing agreement lapse without further action. Foreign investment clearances are done where filings were required.
What still sits on the table is China's State Administration for Market Regulation and Korea's Fair Trade Commission. Two doors. Not twenty. That is a very different risk map from the one investors lived with through the second-request summer.
Skyworks also extended exchange offers on Qorvo notes into mid-September, which is the kind of plumbing work companies do when they still believe the merger can close on a live clock.
## Why the Stock Finally Woke Up
RF front-end chips are not a romance story. Skyworks and Qorvo sell the radio hardware that makes phones, base stations, and a growing pile of non-mobile gadgets actually talk. Alone, each company fights for design wins. Together, Brace has framed the math as scale plus diversification: roughly a $5.5 billion mobile business and a $2.5 billion to $2.6 billion non-mobile book, with about $500 million of targeted synergies once the machines are under one roof.
That story only matters if the deal closes. For most of 2026 the market treated close timing like weather. Some days it looked near. Some days China risk put frost on the chart. Tuesday's move says investors finally put more weight on Brace's "final stages" language than on the leftover regulatory checklist.
It also says something about how tired the pair trade had become. When a fixed-ratio deal sits for months, arbitrage spreads and skepticism do the talking. A hard up day on both names compresses that doubt in one session.
## What Can Still Break the Mood
China and Korea are not rubber stamps just because the United States is clear. Either jurisdiction can slow the clock, demand conditions, or force a rewrite that messes with the synergy math. Brace can prepare to close. He cannot force a foreign regulator's calendar.
There is also ordinary integration risk after the ribbon. Combining two RF suppliers means customer overlap, product roadmaps, and the usual culture tax that never shows up in the press release. Synergy targets sound clean until procurement and engineering start arguing over which die and which package wins.
And the phone cycle still matters. Even a bigger combined company lives on Apple and Android design seasons. A soft handset build can make a "correct" merger feel expensive for a while.
## Bottom Line
Skyworks did not invent a new product on Tuesday. It sold the Street a shorter path to a $22 billion combination that already cleared U.S. antitrust and most foreign-investment gates. A roughly 14% jump is the market saying the remaining China and Korea reviews look like finish-line work, not a redo of the whole deal.
Watch the regulatory notices and whether QRVO keeps tracking SWKS on the fixed exchange ratio. If the spread blows out again, timing doubt is back. If both stocks keep acting like close is the base case, this week's rip was the repricing investors had been waiting to make all summer. Either way, stop treating the Skyworks-Qorvo story like an open-ended maybe. The market just stopped doing that.

Apollo Funds Complete €3 Billion Capital Solution for Bayer
September 16, 2026 3:00am EDT 
Download as PDF
KKR joins Apollo as a minority participant
NEW YORK and LEVERKUSEN, Germany, Sept. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Apollo (NYSE: APO) today announced that Apollo-managed funds and affiliates (“Apollo”) have successfully closed a €3 billion capital solution for Bayer, previously announced on July 10. KKR has joined Apollo as a significant minority participant in the investment.
Under the transaction, Apollo, together with KKR, have invested equity capital into a newly established entity holding Bayer's long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARC) business. Bayer retains a majority stake in the entity and continues to exercise full operational control over the business; there are no changes to the LARC strategy as a result of the investment.
Apollo Partner Jamshid Ehsani said, “We are proud to serve as a capital partner to Bayer, originating and leading a multi-billion-euro capital solution tailored to their needs. Bayer, a global life sciences leader and iconic German company, represents the types of large, blue-chip companies we serve through our High Grade Capital Solutions business.”
Ehsani added, “Apollo has committed to deploying more than $100 billion in Germany over the coming decade, and Bayer exemplifies the kind of strategic, long-term partnership we seek to build with the country's most important companies.”
Centerview Partners served as financial advisor to the Apollo Funds. Latham & Watkins LLP, Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP, and NautaDutilh N.V. are legal counsel to the Apollo Funds.
About Apollo 
Apollo is a high-growth, global alternative asset manager. In our asset management business, we seek to provide our clients excess return at every point along the risk-reward spectrum from investment grade credit to private equity. For more than three decades, our investing expertise across our fully integrated platform has served the financial return needs of our clients and provided businesses with innovative capital solutions for growth. Through Athene, our retirement services business, we specialize in helping clients achieve financial security by providing a suite of retirement savings products and acting as a solutions provider to institutions. Our patient, creative and knowledgeable approach to investing aligns our clients, businesses we invest in, our employees and the communities we impact, to expand opportunity and achieve positive outcomes. As of June 30, 2026, Apollo had approximately $1.05 trillion of assets under management. To learn more, please visit www.apollo.com.
About Bayer 
Bayer is a global enterprise with core competencies in the life science fields of health care and nutrition. In line with its mission, “Health for all, Hunger for none,” the company’s products and services are designed to help people and the planet thrive by supporting efforts to master the major challenges presented by a growing and aging global population. Bayer is committed to driving sustainable development and generating a positive impact with its businesses. At the same time, the Group aims to increase its earning power and create value through innovation and growth. The Bayer brand stands for trust, reliability and quality throughout the world. In fiscal 2025, the Group employed around 88,000 people and had sales of 45.6 billion euros. R&D expenses amounted to 5.8 billion euros. For more information, go to www.bayer.com.
About KKR 
KKR is a leading global investment firm that offers alternative asset management as well as capital markets and insurance solutions. KKR aims to generate attractive investment returns by following a patient and disciplined investment approach, employing world-class people, and supporting growth in its portfolio companies and communities. KKR sponsors investment funds that invest in private equity, credit and real assets and has strategic partners that manage hedge funds. KKR’s insurance subsidiaries offer retirement, life and reinsurance products under the management of Global Atlantic Financial Group. References to KKR’s investments may include the activities of its sponsored funds and insurance subsidiaries. For additional information about KKR & Co. Inc. Envision Energy Earns Two Spots on Recharge's 2026 Wind Power 40 Under 40, Recognising Leadership in Wind Technology and Global Growth
By Envision, Dist.by K.K.Kyodo News 
- Sep 16, 2026 - 10:44 
Release 
SHANGHAI, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Envision Energy, a global leader in green technology, has earned two spots in Recharge's 2026 Wind Power 40 Under 40 Global List, with Huang Hu and Winston Xu named among the emerging leaders shaping the future of the global wind industry. With two honorees, Envision ranks among the organizations with the strongest representation on this year's list.
The Wind Power 40 Under 40 brings together emerging leaders from across the wind industry, spanning turbine manufacturers, project developers, professional and certification services, industry organisations and emerging technology companies. With two honourees, Envision is among the organisations with the highest representation on this year's list, alongside Siemens Gamesa, Ørsted, Shanghai Electric Wind Power, RWE, DNV and the Global Wind Energy Council (GWEC).
Huang Hu, Vice President of Wind Turbine and Equipment Product Platform at Envision Energy, has contributed to advancing next-generation wind turbine technology across drivetrain engineering, system reliability and advanced turbine platforms. He has also helped develop AI-enabled wind technologies and integrated wind-and-storage solutions, extending innovation toward greater lifecycle value and system-level optimisation.
Winston Xu, General Manager for Southeast Asia and Central Asia at Envision Energy, has helped expand Envision's wind business across emerging international markets. He has played a role in establishing and scaling the company's presence in Vietnam, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, while advancing opportunities in Sri Lanka, the Philippines and Azerbaijan. Combining global perspective with local execution, Xu is helping bring advanced wind technologies to new markets.
Together, Huang and Xu represent two complementary capabilities at the heart of Envision's global wind business - advancing the technology and taking it global. The broader 2026 list reflects the increasingly diverse capabilities shaping the future of wind power. While turbine manufacturers and major developers remain prominent among the 40 honourees, the list also includes leaders from industry organisations, research and professional services firms, as well as emerging companies working across areas including AI, floating wind, advanced blades and energy digitalisation.
For Envision, the recognition comes as the company continues to expand its global wind business while advancing turbine technologies designed to address different wind conditions, grid requirements and customer needs. By bringing together technology development, local market expertise and global business experience, Envision aims to deliver greater value to customers and partners while supporting the continued growth of renewable energy around the world.
The recognition of Huang Hu and Winston Xu provides further visibility into the talent and capabilities supporting Envision's technology development and international growth, helping advance wind power as a more intelligent, integrated and strategic pillar of the Future Energy System.

Good morning, moomoo users! Here is an overview of this morning's market open. Thank you for your support. 
Market Overview 
On the Tokyo stock market on September 16, $Nikkei 225 (.N225.JP)$ stocks rebounded at the open, with the opening price up 188.03 yen from the previous day to 63,672.13 yen. In the US market the previous day, $Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ the Nikkei 225 fell for a second consecutive session, dropping $328.09 to $52,093.11, and the yield on US 10-year Treasury bonds briefly rose to the 5% range. However, buying on dips driven by the weakening yen and perceived value became dominant in the Tokyo market. 
By sector, petroleum and coal products, mining, marine transportation, electric and gas utilities, and banking stocks rose. $Shin-Etsu Chemical (4063.JP)$ Shin-Etsu Chemical rebounded after announcing a commemorative dividend for its 100th anniversary, $Hitachi (6501.JP)$ while Hitachi was bought up on news of building a new transformer factory in the US. $Metaplanet (3350.JP)$ Metaplanet showed signs of selling pressure, weighed down by the decline in Bitcoin following the US Senate's rejection of crypto-related bills. 
Top News 
Shin-Etsu Chemical – Rebounds; Raises interim dividend forecast by 20 yen; Implements commemorative dividend for 100th anniversary 
$Shin-Etsu Chemical (4063.JP)$ Shin-Etsu Chemical rebounded. On the 15th, the company announced it would raise its interim dividend forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027 from 58 yen to 78 yen. To commemorate its 100th anniversary, it will add a 20-yen commemorative dividend to the regular 58-yen dividend. The full-year dividend forecast is now 136 yen (up from 106 yen in the previous fiscal year). The year-end dividend forecast remains unchanged at 58 yen. 
Hitachi – Rebounds; Builds new transformer factory in the US with $528 million investment 
$Hitachi (6501.JP)$ rebounded. The company's subsidiary, $Hitachi (6501.JP)$ Energy announced on the 15th that it will build a new transformer factory in Gulfport, Mississippi, USA. The investment amount is $528 million. The scale will be more than double that of the existing plant, and production capacity will also be more than doubled. The company aims to start transformer production in 2029. 
Baby Calendar – Temporarily hit limit up. Makes Orange Page a subsidiary by acquiring all shares from JR East 
$baby calendar (7363.JP)$ temporarily hit limit up. On the 15th, the company announced that it would $East Japan Railway (9020.JP)$ acquire all shares of Orange Page held by [JR East] and make it a consolidated subsidiary. The share transfer is scheduled for November 2. The acquisition price is approximately 507 million yen. Orange Page engages in publishing businesses, including the magazine "Orange Page," as well as e-commerce, events, and courses. 
Metaplanet - Sell signals amid Bitcoin decline; US crypto-related bill rejected by Senate 
$Metaplanet (3350.JP)$ is under selling pressure. Following the rejection of the US crypto-related bill in the Senate, cryptocurrency prices plummeted across the board. Yesterday, Bitcoin touched the $79,000 level, but has recently fallen to the $75,000 range. Selling pressure is also emerging for the company, which invests in Bitcoin. 
NTT – SBI raises target stock price. Sense of bottoming out in Docomo's profits increases likelihood of achieving medium-term plan 
$NTT (9432.JP)$ rebounded. SBI Securities maintains its "Buy" rating and raised the target stock price from 167 yen to 210 yen. Operating profit for Q1 of fiscal 2027 was 425.1 billion yen (YoY +5%), with core businesses performing in line with company expectations. NTT Docomo's Q1 operating profit was 246.2 billion yen (YoY +3%), marking two consecutive quarters of profit growth, suggesting a bottoming out in mobile communication service revenue. 
SUMCO – Daiwa raises target stock price. Steady mix improvement leads to profit expansion through reduced depreciation 
$SUMCO (3436.JP)$ declined. Daiwa Securities maintains its investment rating of "3 (Neutral)" and raised the target stock price from 1,300 yen to 2,900 yen. Sales volume of 300mm wafers is expected to increase due to the expansion of advanced products such as those for AI. The company forecasts operating profit of 40 billion yen for fiscal Dec 2027 and 89 billion yen for fiscal Dec 2028, stating that it is entering a phase of profit expansion driven by the increased sales of advanced products and reduced depreciation burden. 
Stock Market Outlook for the 16th: Consolidation expected; wait-and-see mood ahead of BOJ, Fed, and PBOC policy meetings 
Amid a wait-and-see mood, the Tokyo stock market on the 16th is expected to see the Nikkei Average consolidate around the mid-63,000 yen level. With the FOMC results announcement imminent, market attention is focused on whether the Fed will implement another rate hike within the year. In the Tokyo market, a rate hike is widely anticipated at the Bank of Japan's Monetary Policy Meeting held through the 18th. 
Howa Kogyo reverses gains; TSE imposes margin trading restrictions 
$Howa Machinery (6203.JP)$ reversed its gains. The Tokyo Stock Exchange announced that, effective from the 16th, the margin requirement for new long and short positions in the company's stock via margin trading will be raised to 50% or higher (with at least 20% in cash). Selling pressure has emerged amid views that inflows from individual investors will dry up. Japan Securities Finance also announced that it would raise the loan collateral ratio to 50% (with 20% in cash collateral) from the same date. 
Leopalace, GO, and ABEJA show buy indications

In addition, $Abeja (5574.JP)$ or $TriIs (4840.JP)$ The stock is also raising its pre-open buy order price. On the other hand, $SANNO (3441.JP)$ which hit the lower price limit the previous day, continued to attract top sell orders totaling 300 million yen today (with 80 million yen in buy orders), lowering its special sell indication. $Liberta (4935.JP)$ or $Wolves Hand (194A.JP)$ Sell orders are significantly outweighing buy orders, suggesting that ask prices could be marked down, potentially driving the stock to its lower circuit breaker limit. Hexagon refocuses on automation options
The report provides gradual automation choices from turnkey inspection cells to customized production workflows
Sept. 16, 2026
3 min read 
Add Us On Google 
An engineer programs or repairs a high-tech industrial robot. This smart factory uses AI-driven automation for advanced manufacturing or microchip production. 
Hexagon reported Sept. 14 that manufacturers know automation is essential for staying competitive. However, according to its upcoming “Americas state of manufacturing survey,” when it comes to automation, only 24% believe they are ahead of competitors, 46% are keeping pace, 30% are behind or have not started. Meanwhile, 85% report at least one barrier to accelerating AI and automation.
For years, manufacturers often had to choose between buying an off-the-shelf automation system that might not fit their production requirements or investing in a custom automation project that required added engineering resources, systems integration and upfront investment. As a result, Hexagon reports many automation initiatives stall before they begin.
Consequently, Hexagon’s portable metrology division has refocused on more practical, achievable, gradual automation. Rather than asking users to leap into automation all at once, it’s giving them options for expanding automation as their production requirements increase. This is expected to help users automate at a pace that aligns with their production needs with pathways ranging from ready-to-deploy inspection cells to fully customized automation solutions built with integration partners.
"Automation shouldn't require manufacturers to choose between a rigid, one-size-fits-all system and an overwhelming custom engineering project,” says Joel Martin, product management director in Hexagon Manufacturing Intelligence’s portable division. "Our goal is to give manufacturers practical options that let them automate today, while leaving room to grow tomorrow."
To lower the barriers to adopting automation, beyond simply reducing costs, Hexagon adds it’s making automation easier to deploy, operate and integrate into day-to-day production, particularly for manufacturers that may not have dedicated automation expertise. This means creating more entry points into automation, while giving users the flexibility to scale as their needs evolve.
For example, Hexagon’s Presto standardized, robotic inspection cells, combine industrial robotics, metrology technology and automation software to bring automated quality inspection closer to production. More specifically, Hexagon is previewing its Presto XS entry point to automated metrology within Presto’s Quality Stations ecosystem at this week’s International Manufacturing Technology Show in Chicago.
Designed for small, complex parts, Presto XS brings industrial metrology into a compact, mobile system that can move closer to production, and operate in space-constrained environments with minimal infrastructure changes. Its intuitive, plant-floor interface lets user create and edit inspection routines without robot programming expertise, enabling users to implement automated inspection without typical automation complexities.
Presto XS also supports flexible, two-in-one workflows, which let manufacturers use it as an automated cobot or handheld scanner as inspection demands change. This flexibility lets users reduce inspection cycle times and transport delays, free skilled metrology experts from repetitive scanning tasks, and standardize quality processes across multiple stations.
Hexagon adds its IMTS exhibit will also demonstrate how automation doesn't have to begin with a robot. Manufacturers can start by using portable metrology systems, including handheld scanners, laser trackers and optical measurement technologies for manual inspection. As production volumes increase, those measurement technologies can be integrated into robotic inspection cells or automated workflows without requiring users to replace sensors they already invested in. This approach reduces retraining, preserves existing measurement workflows, and provides a practical path from manual inspection to automation at each user’s own pace.
The exhibit will also feature Hexagon's Leica Absolute Tracker ATS800 two-in-one laser tracker integrated on an autonomous mobile robot (AMR), which will show how optical measurement technology can support customized automation workflows for large-scale manufacturing applications. Designed for industries such as aerospace and shipbuilding, where moving large parts to a fixed inspection station is often impractical, ATS800 illustrates how manufacturers can bring inspection directly into production, enabling quality data to guide manufacturing decisions earlier in the process, rather than waiting until after production.
