The government of Chile  is seeking to attract more private capital to lithium mining and forge new public-private partnerships as part of its strategy to strengthen the sector, increase production and create jobs, said minister of mining and economy Daniel Mas in London.
The secretary of state highlighted some strategic pillars of the first six months of José Antonio Kast's administration, focused on boosting mining potential through legal certainty and  tax incentives .
The authority mentioned that it resubmitted two applications for operating contracts (CEOL) to the Office of the Comptroller General and that three more would be submitted soon. Mas was referring to CleanTech Lithium and its Laguna Verde project worth US$748 million (mn) , whose CEOL application was submitted through Atacama Salt Lakes , and to Salar de Ascotán, a project submitted by Minera Ascotán, a joint venture between state-owned Codelco  and Quiborax .
In August, the government already granted its first CEOL to Quiborax , authorizing it to carry out its US$70mn initiative, aimed at recovering lithium from mining waste .
Another central focus in Mas's speech at the second edition of ChileDay, held in the capital of England, was the alliances that Codelco has with private companies — among them Freeport , Teck , SQM , Anglo  and Rio Tinto  — as a model to replicate.
"The state-owned company and private capital can complement each other. We want more of that," the minister said. 
Meanwhile, progress is being made on regulatory modernization. "Of the 400 permits, today 50 are sworn statements and by the end of the year there will be 90," said the authority, while also promising that another 40 tax-related permits would be eliminated.  
One of Kast's main initiatives is the proposed Reconstruction Law , which has already been approved and includes incentives such as tax stability for large-scale projects and gradually reduces the corporate tax from 27% to 23%.
In addition, the  Capital Market bill is being promoted to encourage early-stage exploration by facilitating access to financing for junior companies, and changes to the mining patent reduction system are being promoted to benefit small-scale mining.
Reversing the stagnation in copper production is another strategic objective: Chile has remained for years at around 5.5 million tonnes (Mt), with a 7% decrease expected for 2026.
However, the government aims to exceed 6 Mt in the short term. This optimism is accompanied by a renewal of investor confidence: "63% of the investment that has entered environmental assessment this year corresponds to mining projects ," said Mas.
Patricio Céspedes, president of the Antofagasta Mining Association, highlights the efforts being made. "We have had low exploration activity in the country for nearly 15 years, leaving exploratory work practically relegated to small-scale miners. This is largely due to the lack of confidence among large companies to invest," he told BNamericas.
Céspedes believes that Kast’s regulatory changes may be favorable for the sector, at a time when demand for copper and lithium is growing strongly as the world advances in new technologies.
"In a country where mining accounts for more than 50% of total exports, the current market context is a tremendous opportunity for our economy," he added.

Joby Slips and Is Down 53% This Year as the eVTOL Trade Keeps Unwinding; Archer Dips, EHang Eases
The eVTOL sector keeps bleeding out, and Joby, Archer, and EHang are all hovering near 52-week lows with no single catalyst to blame. What happens next depends on a certification outcome that could either reprice the entire thesis overnight or…
By David Moadel 
Published September 15, 2026, 12:41pm ET · 3 min read 
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel .
𝕏 
f 
⧉ 
© Shutterstock 
Shares of Joby Aviation ( NYSE:JOBY | JOBY Price Prediction ) are down 2% to $6.18 in midday Tuesday trading, extending a slide that leaves Joby stock down 53% year to date (YTD). The broader market is softer today too, but nowhere near this pace, with the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust ( NYSEARCA:SPY ) down 0.5% to $757.14.
Archer Aviation ( NYSE:ACHR ) stock is also easing, down 2% to $5.38, with Archer now down 28% YTD and trading below its 50-day moving average of $5.47. Meanwhile, EHang Holdings ( NASDAQ:EH ) stock is down 1% to $4.45, and EHang is the worst performer of the group as it’s down 66% YTD.
Joby, Archer, and EHang all build electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft , and Tuesday’s session reads more like continued drift out of a theme that’s been unwinding for months than a fresh shock. Each name sits close to its 52-week low, with Joby’s low at $6.18, Archer’s at $4.30, and EHang’s at $4.345.
Continued Sector Drift
No announcement from Joby, Archer, or EHang accounts for today’s declines. All three are pre-revenue or early-revenue aircraft developers whose value rests on certification timelines and future commercial service rather than on current results, which makes them unusually sensitive to the cost of capital and to investor patience.
The recent overhang on EHang is more concrete. EHang withdrew its full-year 2026 revenue guidance of RMB600 million after a late-June piloted light-sport aircraft accident in China led regulators to slow low-altitude aviation approvals, and the Pomerantz law firm issued an investigation notice on EHang on September 3.
Joby and Archer have leaned into different narratives to defend their names. Archer has bolted on defense exposure through the Halo and Thunder platforms and the pending Wisk, Insitu and SkyGrid acquisition from Boeing ( NYSE:BA ), while Joby has emphasized certification progress and the Blade passenger business as a way to book revenue before the core air taxi service launches.
Certification Timing and Cash Burn
Joby’s August 5 quarterly release showed Q2 2026 revenue of $38.64 million against a $30.38 million consensus, but the core eVTOL air taxi business is still pre-revenue and Blade contributed $36.2 million of the top line. Joby guided second-half 2026 cash usage of $385 million to $415 million against $629.861 million in cash, and reported FAA type-certification progress at 83%/77% on Stage 3 and 20%/10% on Stage 4.
Archer widened its Q2 net loss to $263.2 million, held $1.56 billion in liquidity, and announced a deal to acquire Boeing’s Wisk Aero, Insitu, and SkyGrid businesses in exchange for a strategic Boeing equity stake. Insitu alone is expected to add more than $200 million in annual revenue once the transaction closes by year-end, and Archer’s Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA is guided to a loss of $170 million to $200 million.
EHang delivered only 36 eVTOL units in Q2 2026 versus 52 a year earlier, and posted revenue of $11.56 million, down 46.6% year over year (YoY). EHang authorized a $30 million ADS repurchase program in June, but the withdrawn guidance has been the more consequential number, and EHang’s 50-day moving average of $5.21 now sits well below its 200-day average of $9.72.
What to Watch Next
Joby’s first eIPP flights are targeted for Dallas-Fort Worth in September, and the company is still aiming to carry its first paying passengers this year. The average analyst price target on Joby sits at $10.68, well above the current quote, and Archer and EHang carry comparable targets of $10.61 and $10.19 respectively, so the sell-side view across the group still assumes commercialization actually lands on time.
For Joby, the bull case is that certification is binary and a single approval reprices the whole thesis. The bear side argues that each quarter without eVTOL revenue makes the next capital raise more expensive for shareholders already in the name.
Investors can watch for whether the Dallas-Fort Worth eIPP demonstrations convert to paid service before year-end, and should keep their exposure to pre-revenue eVTOL names small enough that a delayed certification doesn’t wreck the plan (we wrote a free playbook on speculating with just 5% of a portfolio here: Small Stakes, Big Swings ).

Mayo Clinic teams with Thermo Fisher to form biomedical data group Precure
By
Joseph Keenan 
Sep 15, 2026 11:46am 
Mayo Clinic 
Thermo Fisher Scientific 
partnership 
Big Data 
The Mayo Clinic and Thermo Fisher Scientific formed a group to reap data that could lead to the development of new treatments, devices and diagnostics. ()
The Mayo Clinic has partnered with Thermo Fisher Scientific to launch a new group focused on reaping large-scale data that could lead to the understanding and development of new treatments, devices and diagnostics.
The newly formed Precure LLC is tasked with creating one of the largest biomedical datasets using human multi-omics data generation that integrates proteomic, genomic and longitudinal clinical data to help identify early biological signals of disease, the clinic said in a release.
The goal is to better understand and identify early biological signals that develop before a disease is clinically diagnosed. By connecting molecular and clinical data early on, researchers could get a head start that could lead to faster drug development and earlier diagnosis across a wide range of diseases, including cancer, cardiometabolic disease, neurological disorders and immune-mediated disease. 
Related
Thermo Fisher Scientific teams up with Nvidia, TetraScience for next-gen AI workflow projects 
“Precure has the potential to create a step change in how we generate and apply multi-omics data to improve human health,” Marc Casper, Thermo Fisher Scientific’s chair and CEO, said in a statement. 
“By combining Thermo Fisher's leadership in scientific technology with Mayo Clinic's leadership in clinical care, research and innovation, we can create new opportunities at unprecedented scale to detect disease earlier, accelerate drug development and enable more precise therapies.”
The newly formed group is designed to complement Mayo Clinic’s Precure Research, which is part of an effort to gain insight into biological changes that happen as people move from health toward disease.
Precure Research looks to identify early disease signals while Precure LLC would provide the scale and infrastructure for collecting molecular data that could lead to new diagnostics, therapies and other solutions.
Mayo Clinic said any financial returns it earned from the endeavor would be used to further its mission of patient care, research and education.

EDGE, Safran to Build Sovereign Missile Propulsion Systems in Brazil 
Rojoef Manuel September 15, 2026 1 minute read

UAE’s state-owned company EDGE Group has signed an agreement with France’s Safran Electronics & Defense to establish solid rocket motor development and production capabilities in Brazil.
The initiative focuses on building local propulsion and guidance technology at EDGE’s Brazilian offshoot SIATT, which operates in the southeast city of São José dos Campos.
The cooperation will encompass other products such as guided weapons, loitering munitions, coastal defense, and core subsystems, including inertial navigation, GNSS receivers, actuators, optronic sights, and seekers.
According to the businesses, the move is expected to reduce external supply chain reliance for Brasília’s broader defense programs, including its armed forces’ Blue Amazon Management System or SisGAAz maritime surveillance network initiative.
It will also strengthen Safran’s long-standing position as an industrial partner for Brazil in almost five decades.
“This agreement extends our global partnership network to Brazil, bringing Safran Electronics & Defense together with SIATT to build solid rocket motor capabilities on Brazilian soil,” said Hamad Al Marar , CEO and managing director at EDGE Group.
He added that the deal reflects EDGE’s commitment to “strengthening sovereign defence capability for our partners.”
Alexandre Ziegler , head of the Defense Business Unit at Safran Electronics & Defense, echoed that sentiment, saying that the arrangement pushes forward the consortium’s “complementary expertise” to advance defense solutions across the region.
Other Projects
The deal follows a series of milestones for EDGE in Brazil as it grows its footprint in South America.
The Emirati group recently integrated an engineering segment through the acquisition of local firm AKAER and inaugurated a new SIATT production headquarters in the country.
The enterprise also established a cyber defense center with the Brazilian Army and expanded maritime project agreements with the Brazilian Navy .

Old Wind Turbines Could Become The Next Big Source Of Rare Earth Materials
By Sead Fadilpasic 
Sept. 15, 2026 10:47 am EST 
Pedrosala/Getty Images 
Add BGR on Google:
Preferred Source 
Google Discover 
No matter how amazing wind power is, it's not flawless. Wind turbines generally take decades to pay off , and last around 25 to 30 years, at best. So, the question is: what happens with all those old wind turbines? The tall, steel towers are obvious candidates for recycling, but the massive blades — constructed from polymers — are not recyclable. Fortunately, scientists and a wide array of companies are finding ingenious ways to reuse them. Repurposing the blades as bridge girders is just one example, as a company in Europe is also turning the wind turbine blades into cute little houses .
Furthermore, decommissioned turbines are also a valuable source of rare earth minerals, according to Luke Wray, senior VP at Paladin Envirotech. Wray points out that direct-drive turbines, and more precisely their generators, hold a significant amount of rare materials, such as neodymium. Neodymium magnets are necessary for everything from audio devices to smartphones, so old turbines could technically become a valuable secondary source of this material.
It doesn't end there, either. The circuit boards used for wind turbines may contain expensive precious metals, such as palladium, silver, and gold. Considering that the demand for these rare earth minerals and metals will only grow as renewable energy (and other tech) becomes more common, decommissioned turbines are literal gold mines for recyclers.
How to recycle neodymium magnets?
Grassetto/Getty Images 
Building tiny houses made from wind turbines is an unhinged concept. Scrapping interiors of wind turbines for neodymium, not as much. Take the EU, for example. As far back as 2019, scientists there were developing hydrogen technologies to separate the neodymium and purify it — dubbed the FP7 Remanence project. Fast forward to today, and the progress in this field is measurable.
The Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap (HPMS) was developed by MMG and HyProMag at the University of Birmingham as a method of extracting and recycling rare-earth magnetic materials like neodymium from all sorts of decommissioned products. HPMS separates and demagnetizes neodymium magnets and transforms them into alloy powder in just a few hours. This powder can be processed further without using any chemicals, and it can later be turned into other rare-earth alloys or new magnets.
This approach allows decommissioned wind turbines to become more valuable, as companies can extract useful materials from them. Countries that employ this approach can technically cut down on their mining activities, and more importantly, minimize imports.

The new agreement expands that relationship into the joint development and manufacturing of photonics wafers targeting AI data communications applications. 
The announcement did not include financial terms, production volumes or a timetable for potential capacity expansion. 
Aeluma Results Due September 16 
Aeluma is scheduled to report its fiscal fourth-quarter and full-year 2026 financial results on September 16. 
According to the supplied information, the single analyst covering the company has a $30.50 price target on the stock. Analyst price targets represent forecasts and do not indicate future share-price performance. 
Aeluma shares were trading at $13.42 following Tuesday's premarket increase, compared with a stated 52-week high of $31.79. 
Broader US equity futures were trading close to unchanged, with the S&P 500, Dow Jones and Nasdaq all moving by less than 1% in premarket activity.

Asahi Kasei Launches VANTIJ SU-VFC Benchtop
New platform streamlines small-scale virus filtration for biopharma and gene therapy workflows. 
September 15, 2026 
By: Charlie Sternberg 
Associate Editor , Contract Pharma 
Save 
The VANTIJ SU-VFC Benchtop. 
Asahi Kasei Bioprocess , a subsidiary of diversified global company Asahi Kasei , has introduced the VANTIJ SU-VFC Benchtop, expanding its VANTIJ family with the line’s first benchtop-scale platform.
The compact system is designed to streamline small-scale virus filtration by bringing the automation, repeatability, and operator-focused design principles of the broader VANTIJ portfolio to benchtop workflows. It supports 0.12 m² or 0.3 m² Planova 35N virus-removal filters and provides the process control and data-focused capabilities needed for modern biopharmaceutical development.
Initially designed for gene therapy manufacturing, the VANTIJ SU-VFC Benchtop addresses common development challenges such as long production timelines, complex regulatory requirements, operator training demands, and therapy-specific process needs. The platform is built to reduce those burdens through a guided shadow-board layout, tool-free tube set installation and replacement, intuitive connection points, and recipe-driven software. It also enables batch reporting and supports consistent execution of critical filtration processes.
“The biopharmaceutical industry continues to pursue more efficient pathways for bringing innovative therapies to patients,” said Chris Rombach, President of Asahi Kasei Bioprocess America. “The VANTIJ SU-VFC Benchtop reflects Asahi Kasei Bioprocess’s commitment to supporting manufacturers with solutions that simplify critical process steps while delivering the confidence and reliability associated with Planova virus filtration and the Asahi Kasei name.”
The launch highlights Asahi Kasei’s broader push to support the growth of cell and gene therapies, among the biopharmaceutical industry’s fastest-evolving segments. As a strategic focus within the company’s Healthcare sector, these emerging modalities remain central to Asahi Kasei’s Life Science growth strategy.

Mayo Clinic and Thermo Fisher Scientific launch Precure, LLC to identify signs of disease before symptoms appear
By
Tom Millikin
September 15, 2026 
Share this:
Pioneering initiative will generate data at the frontier of healthcare to help transform early biological signals into new opportunities for prevention, diagnosis and treatment 
ROCHESTER, Minn. and WALTHAM, Mass. — Mayo Clinic today announced the launch of Precure, LLC, with founding partner Thermo Fisher Scientific, the world leader in serving science, to help transform how the life sciences community understands the biological changes that occur as people move from health toward disease.
Precure, LLC will create one of the world’s leading biomedical datasets through one of the largest human multi-omics data-generation efforts, integrating proteomic, genomic and longitudinal clinical data to help researchers identify early biological signals of disease and provide a foundation for new discoveries in disease biology, diagnostics and therapeutics.
Many diseases begin developing biologically years before symptoms lead to a clinical diagnosis. By connecting molecular and clinical data over time, Precure, LLC has the potential to help researchers better understand these early changes, accelerate drug development and create new opportunities for earlier diagnosis, intervention and more personalized care across a wide range of diseases, such as cancer, cardiometabolic disease, neurological disorders and immune-mediated disease.
Precure, LLC will bring together molecular data generated from one million biospecimens, linked with longitudinal clinical information collected over several years, integrating genomic and proteomic information with Mayo Clinic’s clinical data and expertise in a highly standardized setting. Advanced AI and large-scale data-analytics will be integral to identifying patterns within these complex datasets and translating them into actionable insights. Mayo Clinic will serve as the majority owner of Precure, LLC. Thermo Fisher joins the partnership as a minority owner.
"At Mayo Clinic, we are committed to transforming patient care through innovation," says Gianrico Farrugia, M.D. , president and CEO, Mayo Clinic. "By harnessing the full potential of multi-omics data, Precure, LLC aims to help us better understand disease before symptoms appear, accelerating discoveries that can lead to earlier diagnoses, more targeted treatments and better outcomes for patients."
Together, the organizations contribute complementary expertise designed to generate the molecular and clinical data needed to accelerate discovery and translate new insights into advancements in patient care:
Mayo Clinic combines world-class clinical and research leadership with advanced AI and data science capabilities, extensive biospecimens and longitudinal de-identified clinical data to accelerate discovery and translate insights into advances for patients.
Thermo Fisher brings industry-leading proteomics expertise and solutions, including its cutting-edge proteomics platform, Olink™ Explore HT, and Thermo Scientific Orbitrap Mass Spectrometry, kits and reagents to help build Precure, LLC’s multi-omics ecosystem.
“Precure LLC has the potential to create a step change in how we generate and apply multi-omics data to improve human health,” said Marc Casper, Chairman and CEO, Thermo Fisher Scientific. “By combining Thermo Fisher’s leadership in scientific technology with Mayo Clinic’s leadership in clinical care, research and innovation, we can create new opportunities at unprecedented scale to detect disease earlier, accelerate drug development and enable more precise therapies.”
Precure, LLC complements Precure Research, Mayo Clinic’s investigator-led scientific effort to understand the biological changes that occur as people move from health toward disease. Precure Research advances the science of identifying and understanding early disease signals, while Precure, LLC provides the scale, infrastructure and collaborations needed to generate population-scale molecular data and help translate discoveries into new diagnostics, therapeutics and other healthcare solutions. Mayo Clinic provides the pathway to validate discoveries and ultimately brings meaningful advances into patient care.
Mayo Clinic's involvement in Precure, LLC is intended to advance its nonprofit mission. Any financial returns to Mayo Clinic would be reinvested in its mission of patient care, research and education.
Visit mayo.edu/research/precure for more information. 
###
About Precure, LLC 
Precure, LLC is a Mayo Clinic-controlled company established to generate and responsibly integrate population-scale molecular data with longitudinal clinical information. Precure, LLC creates the infrastructure and scale needed to enable external collaborations, disease-focused discovery and the development of new diagnostics, therapeutics and other healthcare solutions. It complements Mayo Clinic’s investigator-led research and clinical translation activities.
About Mayo Clinic 
Mayo Clinic is a nonprofit organization committed to innovation in clinical practice, education and research, and providing compassion, expertise and answers to everyone who needs healing. Visit the  Mayo Clinic News Network  for additional Mayo Clinic news.  
About Thermo Fisher Scientific  
Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. is the world leader in serving science, with annual revenue over $45 billion. Our Mission is to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. Whether our customers are accelerating life sciences research, solving complex analytical challenges, increasing productivity in their laboratories, improving patient health through diagnostics or the development and manufacture of life-changing therapies, we are here to support them. Our global team delivers an unrivaled combination of innovative technologies, purchasing convenience and pharmaceutical services through our industry-leading brands, including Thermo Scientific, Applied Biosystems, Invitrogen, Gibco, Fisher Scientific, Unity Lab Services, Patheon and PPD. For more information, please visit www.thermofisher.com .

content_text:
NIO Stock Rises Overnight: Nio Capital Joins Sequoia China And SMIC-Linked Backers In Robot-Sensor Bet
2 minutos de lectura 
NIO 
Puntos clave:
Gongwang makes inductive encoders that measure movement inside robot joints and industrial equipment. 
Its sensors resist magnetic interference, require no permanent magnets and may reduce rare-earth supply exposure. 
Nio Capital’s portfolio also spans CATL, CALB, Seyond, ClearMotion and Alibaba-backed Dexmal. 
U.S.-listed shares of Nio, Inc. (NIO) rose overnight as a William Li-founded investment fund expanded its robotics exposure with a 10.87% stake in Gongwang, while the EV maker’s flagship ES8 approached 150,000 deliveries within its first year. 
Nio’s U.S.-listed shares slipped 0.5% on Monday, after Friday’s gain snapped a seven-session losing streak. 
Nio Capital Bets On Precision Robotics Sensors 
The investment puts Nio Capital alongside prominent Gongwang backers including Sequoia China and SMIC-linked Zhongxin Juyuan. Xiamen Tungsten and solar-inverter giant Sungrow also participated in the robot-sensor maker’s nearly 100 million yuan ($14.9 million) Series A round last month, EV noted. 
The buyer is Hefei Nio Industrial Development Equity Investment Partnership, a Nio Capital-managed fund that previously invested in autonomous-driving company Momenta’s chip unit. Nio Capital is an independent private-equity firm founded in 2016 by Nio CEO William Li and Ian Zhu. Li remains a managing partner. 
Founded in 2023, Wuxi Gongwang Sensing Technology makes inductive rotary encoders, which measure angle and position inside robot joints, servo motors and industrial machinery. 
Earlier investor Honghui Fund called Gongwang the “first company in China to mass-produce inductive position sensors.” Its founders bring nearly two decades of experience from industrial-drive maker INVT and German encoder specialist Heidenhain. 
Inductive encoders offer durability and resistance to the magnetic interference generated inside crowded robot joints. Unlike magnetic encoders, they also contain no permanent magnets, reducing exposure to rare-earth supply risks. The tech can additionally support steer-by-wire and brake-by-wire vehicle systems. 
Nio Capital Pushes Further Beyond EVs 
Gongwang extends Nio Capital’s portfolio beyond traditional EV investments. The firm has backed battery makers CATL and CALB, lidar company Seyond and U.S. suspension specialist ClearMotion, whose technology is used in Nio’s ET9. 
Its wider technology portfolio includes robotics startup Dexmal, which later attracted Alibaba, and consumer-hardware company Ruyuan Technology, founded by former DJI research and development executive Brett Wang. 
Nio itself has registered robotics trademarks and reportedly formed a roughly 20-person team focused on four-legged robots. Its Hefei F2 factory uses 310 automated guided vehicles and 941 industrial robots. Still, Li has said Nio is not rushing to enter robotics as a standalone business, unlike XPeng and Xiaomi, which have made humanoid robots a more visible part of their strategies. 
ES8 Closes In On 150,000 Deliveries 
Meanwhile, Nio expects its third-generation ES8 to reach 150,000 cumulative deliveries this week, less than a year after deliveries began in September 2025. The large electric SUV crossed 140,000 deliveries on Aug.21, suggesting the latest 10,000 units were delivered in about one month, CnEVPost reported. 
Nio delivered 11,001 ES8s in August, up 6.9% from July and marking a second consecutive month above 10,000. Through August, the model accounted for 62.2% of main-brand deliveries and 38% of Nio’s companywide volume in 2026. The ES8 and higher-end ES9 together generated 17,480 deliveries in August, representing 82.6% of the main Nio brand’s total. 
How Do Retail Traders Feel About NIO? 
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for NIO dipped to ‘bearish’ from ‘neutral’ levels a day ago amid a 278% jump in 24-hour message volumes. 
One bearish user said , “$NIO I have been saying my initial buy level is 3.50 but for now i have revised it to ~3. If the current macro's keep it up NIO might get there. I want NIO to succeed because I used to be such a huge bull but i dont see it.... Yet” 
View this Stocktwits post 
Another user said, “$NIO Another great day to add shares, just like the institutions are doing, little by little in order to not increase the share price. Since the company is obviously doing so well and has such a great future it's a no-brainer to add as time goes by.” 
View this Stocktwits post 
Nio’s U.S.-listed shares have declined 41% over the past year.

Shinhan Asset Management's SOL U.S. Dividend Dow Jones ETF Surpasses ₩500 Billion in Retail Net Buying
Add preferred source 
Retail investors' cumulative net purchases of Shinhan Asset Management's "SOL U.S. Dividend Dow Jones" ETF have reached ₩501.4 billion (approximately $368.6 million), surpassing the ₩500 billion mark. The fund's net assets stand at ₩1.0118 trillion (approximately $743.8 million). Despite net assets declining by ₩44.1 billion over the past month, retail investors continued buying with ₩12.3 billion in net purchases during the same period. The product tracks the "Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100," a U.S. dividend growth index, and applies a monthly distribution structure based on the same underlying index as SCHD. The sustained buying is attributed to investor demand for regular cash flow amid heightened market volatility. The asset manager offers a diverse lineup including a currency-hedged version and products eligible for retirement pension accounts.
Key Elements 
Shinhan Asset Management SOL U.S. Dividend Dow Jones Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100 SCHD Kim Jung-hyun Korea Exchange SOL U.S. Dividend Dow Jones (H) SOL U.S. Dividend U.S. Treasury Mix 50 
Retail investors' cumulative net purchases of Shinhan Asset Management's "SOL U.S. Dividend Dow Jones" exchange-traded fund (ETF) have surpassed ₩500 billion. The milestone reflects steady inflows from individual investors seeking cash flow through dividends even amid expanding market volatility.
According to Korea Exchange data as of the 9th, retail investors' cumulative net purchases of the product reached ₩501.4 billion (approximately $368.6 million). Net assets stand at ₩1.0118 trillion (approximately $743.8 million). Over the past month alone, net assets declined by roughly ₩44.1 billion (approximately $32.4 million), but retail investors net purchased ₩12.3 billion (approximately $9.0 million) worth of shares during the same period. The decline in net assets is attributed to market price adjustments, and the fact that retail buying continued even during the price downturn is noteworthy.
Shinhan Asset Management explained that the domestic stock market correction and heightened global market volatility have increased interest in dividend stocks. The analysis suggests that as demand grows not only for capital gains from share price appreciation but also for regular dividend income, attention has shifted to high-quality U.S. dividend growth companies with strong payout capacity and financial soundness.
The product uses the "Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100," a leading U.S. dividend growth index, as its underlying index. It tracks the same index as SCHD, widely known as a U.S. dividend growth ETF, while applying a monthly distribution structure designed to pursue both capital growth and regular cash flow.
Kim Jung-hyun, head of Shinhan Asset Management's ETF business group, said, "Retail investors' cumulative net purchases surpassing ₩500 billion reflects the trust investors have built in the management approach of investing in U.S. dividend growth companies." He added, "In an environment of uncertain market direction, consistent dividends can serve as an important foundation for sustaining long-term investment."
Beyond this product, Shinhan Asset Management operates a diverse lineup investing in U.S. dividend growth assets, including the currency-hedged "SOL U.S. Dividend Dow Jones (H)" and "SOL U.S. Dividend U.S. Treasury Mix 50," which can be included as a safe asset in retirement pension accounts. Investors can select products based on their currency outlook, risk appetite, and account type.
Distribution dates vary by product. SOL U.S. Dividend Dow Jones and SOL U.S. Dividend Dow Jones (H) use the last day of each month as the record date and pay distributions in early the following month. SOL U.S. Dividend U.S. Treasury Mix 50 and SOL U.S. Dividend Dow Jones No. 2 pay in the middle of each month. By combining products with different distribution dates, investors can receive distributions twice a month.
Market observers note that the environment of heightened uncertainty—with South Korea's KOSPI volatility index (V-KOSPI) rising to approximately 2.7 times the level of the same period last year and the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield climbing to 4.9%—has supported the preference for dividend growth stocks. A Shinhan Asset Management official stated, "Since listing, we have maintained the principle of investing in U.S. dividend growth companies and continued reasonable monthly distributions utilizing dividend resources." The official added, "Going forward, we will strengthen our product lineup and management competitiveness so that investors looking to reinvest monthly distributions in pension accounts and accumulate dividend assets can select products suited to their investment preferences and objectives."

Kyoto Fusioneering announces strategic investment of up to £3m in UK fusion energy sector to boost breeder blanket technology
Michael Shanks (left), Minister of State at the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ), and Kiyoshi Seko (right), President and COO of Kyoto Fusioneering 
・Investment aimed at strengthening company’s solid breeder blanket technology capabilities and core fusion plant engineering design focus 
・Kyoto Fusioneering to rapidly expand its team of fusion engineers in the UK 
・UK fusion sector receives timely boost that will contribute to international collaboration between Japan and the UK 
C ULHAM , UK 15 September 2026 —Kyoto Fusioneering (KF), a leading global fusion energy engineering company based in Tokyo, has announced a strategic investment of up to £3m in the UK’s burgeoning fusion sector that represents a clear signal of intent by the company to grow and invest in one of the leading markets for fusion energy research and development. 
The investment will enable KF to design and manufacture a lithium oxide (Li₂O) solid breeder blanket experiment and initiate irradiation testing with online tritium measurement capability. Indeed, the experiment has been designed to deliver tangible progress for the STEP programme while further advancing the understanding of lithium ceramic breeder materials under irradiation, supporting both UK and international fusion projects.
The funding enables KF to grow its Culham-based team to provide the UK’s growing fusion sector including the prestigious STEP project with solutions to some of the most difficult challenges in fusion plant engineering from plasma heating systems to plant-wide system design, thermal-hydraulic analysis, and tritium breeding and recovery systems.  
Since its inception in 2019, KF has developed world-class expertise in the field of fusion energy providing technology and know-how through partnerships with government agencies, research institutions, and organisations around the world including UKAEA (UK Atomic Energy Authority). KF has collaborated with UKAEA already in the fields of plasma heating systems, tritium capabilities, and fusion materials development, and foresees its investment as a pillar of Japan-UK collaboration under the auspices of the Japan-UK Memorandum of Cooperation on Fusion signed in June 2025.
The investment comes at the start of the inaugural ‘UK Fusion Week’ that brings together British and international fusion leaders to discuss important issues related to fusion’s development such as policy initiatives related to international collaboration, funding and supply chain development.
According to Kiyoshi Seko, President and COO of Kyoto Fusioneering: 
“Our strategic investment represents a step change for Kyoto Fusioneering in the UK as it enables us to grow our team and its capabilities as well as put down a marker for further country expansion.  With the STEP project progressing and strong British Government backing for fusion, we are incredibly positive about the UK’s fusion market given its 40+ year track record of pushing scientific barriers. Kyoto Fusioneering aims to contribute to the success of UK fusion by strengthening its footprint here, and we are grateful to the UK Government for their consistent support of the sector.”
Dr Colin Baus, Managing Director of Kyoto Fusioneering UK and VP of Blanket Science, Kyoto Fusioneering, stated: 
“We are delighted to announce our strategic funding programme as we enter a crucial time for UK fusion where the STEP programme and private fusion initiatives require ever more complex solutions including blankets and advanced fuel cycle systems for a new generation of reactors. This investment from Japan will enable core capabilities to be developed in the UK and allow us to respond to this national endeavour. We look forward to working further with the Government and UKAEA as key partners on emerging technologies that could deliver clean, abundant energy for generations.”
Michael Shanks, Minister of State at the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) remarked: 
“Fusion has the potential to provide virtually limitless clean energy while supporting more than 10,000 jobs across the UK by 2030, attracting investment and creating major opportunities for British businesses. We’re accelerating the race to commercial fusion, turning cutting-edge research into economic growth and cementing Britain’s position as a world leader in fusion energy.”
Professor Amy Gandy, Head of Materials Science and Engineering at UK Atomic Energy Authority (UKAEA) said:  
“The tritium breeder blanket is one of the most challenging components for future fusion power stations, with a range of concepts and technologies in development around the world. KF’s investment provides an exciting and novel opportunity to test potential solid breeder concepts in fusion-relevant conditions. Tritium breeder blankets comprise many different materials, not just the fuel source (in this case Li₂O). KF’s project aims to replicate and irradiate a complete breeder blanket module, providing invaluable information not only about tritium production but also how these very different materials will interact with, and affect, each other.” 
About Kyoto Fusioneering: 
Kyoto Fusioneering is the world’s premier fusion technology and integrated systems developer. It delivers plasma heating, tritium fuel cycle, and tritium breeding blanket and thermal cycle systems that advanced fusion programs worldwide depend on, regardless of confinement approach. KF operates globally across Japan, the United Kingdom, the United States, Germany, and Canada. Visit us at  kyotofusioneering.com .

From electronics to agriculture: How 3M film technology is helping manage light in new ways
Sep 15, 2026
Print current page.

For decades, 3M has applied optical film technology to help manage light in precise and useful ways, including in electronic devices and displays where light control can support brightness, clarity and energy efficiency. Now, that same expertise is being adapted for a new challenge: filtering sunlight to help support agriculture while also helping generate renewable energy.
Through an ongoing partnership with Voltiris , 3M is helping advance spectral-filtering solar technology designed to selectively manage sunlight above crops. The approach aims to let plants receive the light they need for growth while redirecting other portions of the light spectrum they don’t to help generate electricity.
Building on work in greenhouse agriculture, the companies recently launched an outdoor pilot in the Canary Islands to test how Voltiris’ Voltimax spectral-filtering module performs in open-field conditions.
For 3M, the pilot is part of a bigger story: applying an existing technology platform in a new way through external collaboration.
Your browser does not support the video tag. 
A new use for a core 3M technology platform 
3M’s role in the Voltiris partnership is rooted in its long-standing expertise in optical films, materials science and light management.
Optical films are designed to control how light is transmitted, reflected or redirected. In this pilot application, that expertise helps support a system that filters sunlight above crops, balancing two goals that are often in tension: protecting plants from excess heat while capturing solar energy.
That capability is what makes the collaboration different from a traditional solar installation. Rather than simply placing panels near agricultural land, the technology is designed to work with the growing environment by managing the spectrum of light reaching the crops.
For growers, that could create a valuable combination: improved growing conditions and renewable energy generation from the same footprint.
Why the Canary Islands pilot matters now 
The new pilot is in Gran Canaria, Spain, over a banana farm operated by Grupo FSM, the largest banana producer and exporter in Europe.
Bananas are central to the region’s agricultural economy, but they are grown in a challenging environment with high solar irradiance and significant heat stress. A large share of irrigation relies on desalinated water, where production requires substantial amounts of energy. In the Canary Islands, the electricity used for desalination represents a significant share of the total cost of banana production.
That makes the region a strong test case for a solution designed to address multiple pressures at once.
The pilot will explore whether spectral-filtering solar technology can help reduce heat stress for crops while also generating electricity that is expected to partially supply a desalination plant used for irrigation.
From greenhouse innovation to open-field agriculture 
3M and Voltiris have been working together for several years to help move the technology from concept toward broader application.
The solution has already been deployed at industrial scale in greenhouses across Europe. The Canary Islands pilot represents the next step: testing how the technology performs outdoors, where conditions are less controlled and durability, system performance and environmental exposure become even more important.
That shift from greenhouse to open-field agriculture is a meaningful expansion of the opportunity.
It also reflects how 3M works with partners to advance innovation: combining 3M’s science, technology platforms and application expertise with external companies developing new market solutions.
“In high-tech greenhouses across Northern Europe, where every percentage point of light matters, our technology has demonstrated that crops can thrive beneath Voltiris modules. Results show plant temperatures reduced by around 4°C and irrigation needs lowered by approximately 20%,” said Jonas Roch, chief technology officer and co-founder of Voltiris. “As heatwaves become more frequent and intense, our agrivoltaic solution helps make agriculture more resilient. We are now bringing the same principle outdoors, with the potential to deliver similar - or even greater - benefits while also protecting crops from wind, frost, hail, and heavy rain.”
Innovation through partnership 
“The collaboration with Voltiris demonstrates the value of combining 3M’s materials science expertise with external innovation to help accelerate emerging technologies,” said Mark Copman, senior vice president of 3M Ventures. “Together, we are advancing solutions that have the potential to support both agriculture and energy, while reflecting 3M’s ongoing commitment to applying science to complex global challenges.”
The partnership is an example of the way 3M works with innovators across industries: taking core technology platforms and applying them in new ways to help solve customer and market challenges.
In this case, 3M’s optical film expertise is helping enable a new approach to agricultural solar technology - one that could support crop environments, help generate renewable power and address resource pressures in regions where sunlight is abundant but conditions are increasingly demanding.
FAQ 
What is 3M’s partnership with Voltiris? 
3M is working with Voltiris to help advance spectral-filtering solar technology for agriculture. The collaboration combines Voltiris’ solar module innovation with 3M’s materials science and optical film expertise to explore new ways of managing sunlight above crops.
What role does 3M technology play? 
3M contributes expertise in optical films and light management. In this application, that technology helps support a system designed to filter sunlight so crops can receive the light they need while other portions of the spectrum are redirected to generate electricity.
What is new about the Canary Islands pilot? 
The Canary Islands pilot is the first outdoor deployment of Voltiris’ Voltimax spectral-filtering solar module for open-field agriculture. It provides a real-world test in a region where banana growers face high solar exposure, crop heat stress and energy-intensive irrigation needs.
How does this reflect 3M innovation? 
The partnership shows how 3M can apply a core technology platform in a new way through collaboration. By adapting optical film expertise for agriculture and renewable energy, 3M is helping advance a solution designed to address multiple challenges at once: crop conditions, energy generation and resource efficiency.

content_text:
Fortaegis Technologies has announced an oversubscribed $50 million Series A, led by returning investor Serendipity Capital, as the company accelerates its transition from technology validation into commercial production and global deployment of its Secure Compute architecture across AI infrastructure, defense and autonomous systems, advanced manufacturing, telecommunications, critical infrastructure and automotive.
AI is revolutionizing the pace and autonomy of computing, while quantum computing is challenging the cryptographic foundations on which today’s systems rely. At the same time, control over compute, data and critical infrastructure is becoming a strategic imperative for governments and industry. Fortaegis is pioneering Secure Compute for the demands of this new era.
The Fortaegis Silicon Platform is a full-stack Secure Compute architecture spanning hardware, firmware, cryptography and software. By rooting security in the physical properties of silicon and extending identity, security, policy and orchestration across every enabled node, the architecture is designed to establish trust at machine speed and scale across millions of devices and agents while being naturally and entirely quantum-safe. 
“The security and prosperity of the West and its allies increasingly depend on who controls the foundations of compute. AI and quantum are making that question more urgent. Fortaegis was founded on the conviction that security cannot remain something we add on top of digital systems — it must become part of the foundations of compute itself. This investment allows us to accelerate that mission globally,” said Boudewijn Wijnands, founder and CEO of Fortaegis Technologies.
“Computing infrastructure is the central arena of geopolitical and economic competition today. As AI advances and quantum computing takes off, security and control of computing foundations are essential. Fortaegis is addressing that challenge at the architectural level,” said Chris Miller, US board member of Fortaegis Technologies and author of Chip War.
Since its inception in October 2023, Fortaegis has expanded across Europe, the United States and Asia and is working with more than 25 enterprises and governments across semiconductor infrastructure, defense, AI infrastructure, telecommunications and other critical industries. The company has filed 17 patents, with a further 14 in the pipeline, and has demonstrated connection performance more than 200 times faster than conventional approaches in internal and customer testing, while being quantum-safe by design. The same hardware-rooted architecture supports multiple deployment methods — server rack mounted, ruggedized edge, compact edge and embedded silicon — through one unified infrastructure: the Fortaegis Silicon Platform.
“AI and quantum computing are not incremental shifts; they are changing the architecture of computing itself. Having founded and then built Quantinuum, I have seen how technologies that begin at the frontier can become foundational infrastructure. Fortaegis has the technology and ambition to do the same for Secure Compute — making security intrinsic to computing from silicon upward — and will become one of the hottest companies around as it becomes integral and essential for the rollout of compute in the next decades. Remember the name!” said Ilyas Khan, chairman of Fortaegis Technologies and founder of Quantinuum.
The investment will enable the company to scale production and commercial deployment of its FPGA products across the United States, Europe, Singapore and Japan and to advance its ASIC roadmap, while growing its engineering and commercial capacity.
“Secure Compute will become increasingly important across many industries. Fortaegis has developed a strong foundational technology, and we are committed to supporting its transition to scalable production and deployment,” said Peter Janssen, founder and CTO of Prodrive Technologies.
The Series A brings together investors spanning critical technology, semiconductors, industrial infrastructure, research, quantum computing, AI, defense, space and geopolitics. Strategic, supply-chain and industrial participation includes TEL Venture Capital (the CVC of Tokyo Electron) and TNO, alongside Prodrive Technologies. Other investors include NP-Hard Ventures, NovaCapital, Access Ventures and Coalition Capital. Individual participants include Ilyas Khan, Quantinuum founder and Fortaegis chairman; Ian Fujiyama, head of global aerospace, defense and government at Carlyle; and Peter Frankopan, professor of global history at Oxford University and author of The Silk Roads.
“The most consequential deep-tech companies do more than improve an existing category — they create a new layer of infrastructure. We invested in Fortaegis because it is building exactly that: an architecture spanning silicon, hardware and software for a security challenge that becomes more important as AI, autonomy and quantum computing scale. We believe Secure Compute will own the foundational layer across both commercial and national-security infrastructure,” said Rob Jesudason, founder and CEO of Serendipity Capital.
Founded in October 2023, Fortaegis operates across Europe, the United States and Asia and is working with more than 25 enterprises and governments across semiconductor infrastructure, defense, AI infrastructure, telecommunications and other critical industries.

Fertiglobe, Covestro and MB Energy sign MoU to explore ammonia supply chain
September 14, 2026 | By Mary Bailey 
Fertiglobe Plc (Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates), Covestro AG (Leverkusen, Germany) and MB Energy Holding GmbH & Co. KG (Hamburg, Germany) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to explore collaboration across the ammonia value chain in Germany and Europe. The MoU was signed during the visit to Germany of His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, President of the United Arab Emirates.
The collaboration brings together Fertiglobe’s global ammonia production and supply capabilities, MB Energy’s energy infrastructure and logistics expertise, and Covestro’s position as a major industrial consumer of ammonia in Germany.
Under the MoU, Fertiglobe, the world’s largest seaborne exporter of urea and ammonia, will explore the potential supply of ammonia through an import terminal proposed to be built and operated by MB Energy at Blumensand in Hamburg. As part of the collaboration, Fertiglobe will also explore a potential equity investment in the Hamburg terminal.
Covestro, one of the world’s leading manufacturers of high-quality polymer materials, will evaluate the potential offtake of ammonia delivered through the terminal for use as feedstock in its production and/or to meet hydrogen supply requirements.
By developing an additional route for ammonia imports into Germany, the collaboration has the potential to diversify supply options and strengthen the resilience of supply chains serving European industry. The parties will also explore opportunities to serve other industrial customers across Europe.
The parties will jointly assess the commercial, technical and logistical requirements for the potential supply of ammonia via Hamburg, including terminal capacity, volumes, delivery arrangements and onward transportation to industrial customers. They will also evaluate enabling infrastructure and logistics, including pipelines, barges and rail transportation.
Ammonia is an essential feedstock for the chemical industry and can also serve as a carrier of hydrogen. Access to reliable and competitive lower-carbon and renewable ammonia could help reduce the carbon footprint of chemical production and support the industry’s energy transformation. Import, storage and transport infrastructure will be critical to making such supplies available at an industrial scale.
The collaboration will consider conventional, lower-carbon and renewable ammonia, including the carbon intensity of potential supply and alignment with applicable regulatory and certification frameworks, such as the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and relevant low-carbon and renewable hydrogen requirements.
Ahmed El-Hoshy, Chief Executive Officer of Fertiglobe, said: “This MoU marks an important step in strengthening Fertiglobe’s connectivity with industrial customers in Europe and expanding routes to market for our global ammonia platform. Together with Covestro and MB Energy, we see an opportunity to support the development of a reliable and competitive ammonia supply chain through Hamburg, in line with our Grow 2030 focus on customer proximity and disciplined growth in lower-carbon ammonia.”
Dr. Markus Steilemann, CEO of Covestro, added: “Ammonia is an essential building block for the chemical industry – and its carbon footprint matters for the transformation of our production. Securing reliable, competitive and increasingly low-carbon ammonia is therefore a strategic priority for Covestro. Together with Fertiglobe and MB Energy, we are exploring an additional supply route that could support our path toward climate neutrality while strengthening supply resilience in Germany and Europe.”
Jonathan Perkins, CEO of MB Energy, commented: “Europe’s energy transition depends not only on low-carbon molecules, but on reliable infrastructure to reach industrial customers at scale. This MoU brings together complementary capabilities across supply, logistics and demand to explore a credible ammonia value chain through Hamburg. With MB Energy’s long-standing infrastructure and logistics capabilities, we aim to strengthen supply security while enabling the progressive introduction of lower-carbon ammonia in Germany and across Europe.”

New optical tracking system combines fully wireless operation, dynamic tracking and portability to simplify shop floor and field-based inspection

A 3D scanner. The Hyperscan SR is designed to simplify high-accuracy 3D scanning on the shop floor and in the field.
(Provided by Dragonite_East/iStock Photo) 
Hexagon’s Manufacturing Intelligence Business Area previewed HYPERSCAN SR, a fully wireless optical tracking 3D scanner and the new entry point to its HYPERSCAN series , shown for the first time at IMTS 2026 (Booth #134102).
Manufacturers increasingly need to inspect parts where the work happens, whether that's on the production line, across multiple facilities or out in the field. While optical tracking makes it possible to capture accurate measurements even when parts or their surroundings are moving, traditional systems often require cables, time-consuming setup and specialized operators. HYPERSCAN SR removes those barriers, making high-accuracy optical tracking more practical for everyday manufacturing. 
Natively fully wireless, with WiFi 6 connectivity and battery power, HYPERSCAN SR deploys quickly and is straightforward for non-specialist operators to run. Its dynamic tracking follows both the part and the scanner at once, so movement and vibration do not interrupt the scan.
A wide scanning area, multiple scanning modes with hole flash capture and edge detection, and target-free scanning make it productive across a broad range of parts, and it is ready for integration onto a cobot or industrial robot.
HYPERSCAN SR joins HYPERSCAN Ultra and HYPERSCAN Super to complete Hexagon's optical scanning portfolio . HYPERSCAN SR offers a fully wireless, highly portable entry point, HYPERSCAN Ultra is designed for everyday production scanning, and HYPERSCAN Super delivers maximum range and performance for large-scale parts and automated inspection.
All three systems share the same workflows and coordinate system, making it easy to scale as measurement needs evolve. 
"Dynamic optical tracking keeps a scan stable even when the part moves or the setup vibrates, because the scanner and the part are tracked together in one coordinate system," said Darren Goh, Product Director, Handheld 3D Scanners, Hexagon’s Portable Metrology division. "HYPERSCAN SR builds that into a fully wireless system, with WiFi 6 and battery power native to the device rather than added on. It's quick to deploy and simple enough for everyday operators to run, so teams can bring it into limited-access and power-limited areas that a larger, cabled setup can't reach." 
HYPERSCAN SR is designed for applications where mobility matters most, including on-site and in-field inspection, supplier and incoming-goods verification, field service and maintenance, tooling and fixture inspection, and decentralized quality control. It is well suited for manufacturers across automotive, rail, energy, construction, industrial equipment, consumer products and general manufacturing. 
"North American manufacturers are inspecting more parts on the shop floor and in the field than ever before, and they want technology their own teams can deploy with confidence,” said Joel Martin, Director of Product Management, Portable Division, at Hexagon Manufacturing Intelligence.
“HYPERSCAN SR meets that need with a fully wireless design that's quick to set up, easy to operate and provides a straightforward path into optical tracking without the complexity of traditional systems.”
HYPERSCAN SR is on display at IMTS 2026 at McCormick Place, Chicago, from 14 to 19 September at Booth #13410. The product will be officially launched, with availability and pricing details later this year – register here to find out more.

content_text:
HS Hyosung Energy Solution Korea a joint venture between HS Hyosung Group and Belgian materials company Umicore, will invest 1.2 trillion won to build a silicon anode materials production base in Ulsan.
​HS Hyosung Energy Solution Korea said Sept. 14 that it signed a memorandum of understanding with Ulsan Metropolitan City to build a silicon anode materials production plant. The company plans to invest a total of 1.2 trillion won through 2030 at the Ulsan-Mipo National Industrial Complex.
​The investment will be carried out in three phases. In the first phase, the company will invest 300 billion won to build MPK-1, a silicon anode materials plant with an annual capacity of 5,000 tons, by the first quarter of 2028. Further investment will follow to establish a mass-production system.
​Silicon anode materials have a higher energy density than conventional graphite-based anode materials, allowing electric vehicles to travel farther and charge faster.
​HS Hyosung Energy Solution Korea was established by HS Hyosung Group and Umicore for the silicon anode materials business, with an 80% to 20% ownership split. The venture is the first new business pursued by HS Hyosung Group since its separation from the wider Hyosung Group.
​Lee Ki-soo, chief executive officer of HS Hyosung Energy Solution Korea, said, "As we have selected Ulsan as our first investment site, we will grow together with the region by building an advanced production base and creating jobs."

Samsung Opens Advanced Semiconductor Packaging Lab in Japan
by Binay Konwar · September 14, 2026 · News

Add as preferred source Add SammyGuru as a preferred source and Google shows more of our articles in Top Stories when we have fresh coverage of what you search for. You still see other sites, and you can change your picks at any time. Follow on Google Discover 
Samsung is investing heavily in developing advanced semiconductor packaging technologies. The company has opened a new research lab in Japan to test next-gen packaging processes and build prototypes. The facility will allow the Korean firm to tap into the country’s semiconductor ecosystem.
New Japan Lab could speed up chip packaging research
Samsung recently held an opening ceremony for its Advanced Package Lab (APL) in Minato Mirai, Yokohama. The facility is part of the company’s five-year, 40 billion yen investment plan that kicked off in 2024.
The APL covers around 6,600 square meters and features cleanrooms similar to semiconductor production lines. Currently, 95 researchers from South Korea and Japan work at the facility. The company plans to grow the team to more than 100 researchers by 2027.

For the uninitiated, the APL is a global R&D hub. Samsung will use it to research new packaging technologies, test different materials and processes, and make prototypes.
One key area Samsung aims to focus on at the facility is 3.xD chiplet technology. The company will also research bonding, interposer, and substrate mounting technologies. These technologies are becoming more essential for AI chips because they need to connect logic chips with HBM quickly and reliably.
Samsung is using the facility to take advantage of Japan’s semiconductor ecosystem. The country has several companies that specialize in semiconductor materials, components, and equipment.
For example, Ibiden makes high-performance package substrates, while Namics produces underfill materials that fill the space between a chip and its substrate. Likewise, Tokyo Electron provides wafer bonding equipment, and DISCO specializes in equipment for grinding and cutting wafers.
Samsung already works with more than 50 Japanese companies, and the APL will let it quickly test their materials and processes. It will also reduce the time needed to bring new materials to Korea, cutting the evaluation process from up to two months.

content_text:
Fortaegis Raises $50 Million to Secure AI Infrastructure at The Silicon Level
By Matt Swayne · 14 September 2026 · 5 min read 
Fortaegis raised $50 million to commercialize chip-based security technology for AI infrastructure, autonomous systems and connected machines. 
Insider Brief 
Fortaegis raised $50 million to commercialize chip-based security technology for AI infrastructure, autonomous systems and connected machines. 
Its architecture uses the unique physical properties of silicon chips to generate changing encryption keys and verify identities across networks. 
The funding will support commercial production, FPGA deployments and development of application-specific chips in the U.S., Europe and Asia.
Dutch startup Fortaegis has raised $50 million to commercialize a security architecture that uses the physical properties of silicon chips to protect AI infrastructure, autonomous systems and connected machines.
The oversubscribed Series A was led by Singapore-based Serendipity Capital , according to the company. Participants included TEL Venture Capital , the corporate venture arm of chip-equipment maker Tokyo Electron, as well as TNO , Prodrive Technologies , NP-Hard Ventures , NovaCapital , Access Ventures and Coalition Capital .
Fortaegis plans to use the funding to move from technology testing into commercial production and deployment. The company expects to begin commercial manufacturing in 2027, the Financial Times reported.
Founded in October 2023, Fortaegis says it is working with more than 25 companies and governments across AI infrastructure, defense, telecommunications, semiconductor manufacturing and other critical industries. Its government work includes organizations in the U.S., U.K., Japan, Singapore, Germany, France and the Netherlands, according to the FT.
“The security and prosperity of the West and its allies increasingly depend on who controls the foundations of compute. AI and quantum are making that question more urgent. Fortaegis was founded on the conviction that security cannot remain something we add on top of digital systems — it must become part of the foundations of compute itself. This investment allows us to accelerate that mission globally,” founder and CEO Boudewijn Wijnands said in the announcement.
Ilyas Khan, chair and founding shareholder of Fortaegis, said the architecture could become a widely used security layer as AI and quantum technologies develop.
“AI and quantum computing are not incremental shifts; they are changing the architecture of computing itself. Having founded and then built Quantinuum, I have seen how technologies that begin at the frontier can become foundational infrastructure. Fortaegis has the technology and ambition to do the same forSecure Compute — making security intrinsic to computing from silicon upward — and will become one of the hottest companies around as it becomes integral and essential for the rollout of compute in the next decades. Remember the name!” said Khan, who is also founder of the quantum computing company Quantinuum.
Security for Autonomous AI
Fortaegis is positioning its technology as a way to establish trust among AI systems, devices and data-center equipment without relying entirely on software.
That issue could become more important as companies deploy autonomous AI agents that can make decisions, access information and interact with other systems with limited human supervision. Large networks of agents and devices must be able to verify one another’s identities and determine whether instructions and data are authentic.
The Fortaegis Silicon Platform spans hardware, firmware, cryptography and software. It uses tiny physical variations created during semiconductor manufacturing to give each chip a unique digital fingerprint.
Fortaegis extracts information from that fingerprint to generate and frequently change encryption keys. The company says the keys are not permanently stored on devices, reducing the opportunity for attackers to locate and steal them.
The architecture is designed to extend identity checks, security policies and system management across potentially millions of devices and AI agents. Fortaegis says it can be deployed through data-center server racks, ruggedized systems for military, industrial and other demanding environments, compact edge devices or technology embedded directly into chips.
“Computing infrastructure is the central arena of geopolitical and economic competition today. As AI advances and quantum computing takes off, security and control of computing foundations are essential. Fortaegis is addressing that challenge at the architectural level,” said Chris Miller, a Fortaegis U.S. board member and author of “Chip War.”
AI and Quantum Risks Converge
The growth of AI is increasing the amount of sensitive information moving among data centers, processors, sensors and autonomous devices. At the same time, future quantum computers could undermine widely used encryption methods that protect much of that information.
Fortaegis describes its architecture as naturally quantum-safe because its keys are derived from the physical properties of silicon rather than generated solely through mathematical processes. Wijnands told the FT that a quantum computer would not have a mathematical model it could use to reconstruct those keys.
The quantum-safe claim will require broader independent analysis. The FT reported that national laboratories in several countries have validated the technology, but the article did not identify all the laboratories or provide detailed test results and threat models.
TNO, the Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research, has tested the technology. Marc Zegveld, head of the TNO group that conducted the assessment, told the FT that researchers used aggressive hacking methods but could not penetrate the integrated architecture.
Moving Toward Commercial Production
Fortaegis said customer-funded development programs are progressing from technical validation into production qualification and commercial deployment. The company has filed 17 patents and has another 14 in development.
The new funding will support production of Fortaegis products built with field-programmable gate arrays, or FPGAs, across the U.S., Europe, Singapore and Japan. FPGAs are chips that can be configured for particular tasks after manufacturing.
The company will also advance its development of application-specific integrated circuits, or ASICs. These are chips manufactured to perform defined functions and could allow Fortaegis to embed its security architecture more directly into commercial products.
“Secure Compute will become increasingly important across many industries. Fortaegis has developed a strong foundational technology, and we are committed to supporting its transition to scalable production and deployment,” said Peter Janssen, founder and chief technology officer of Prodrive Technologies.
Fortaegis says internal and customer testing has demonstrated connection performance more than 200 times faster than conventional approaches. The company and the FT did not provide detailed benchmarks identifying the protocols, hardware or network conditions used in that comparison.
The startup is also working with ASML and Eindhoven University of Technology on a security framework for autonomous AI systems. It is in talks with U.S. hyperscale cloud providers and AI laboratories, according to the FT.
“The most consequential deep-tech companies do more than improve an existing category — they create a new layer of infrastructure. We invested in Fortaegis because it is building exactly that: an architecture spanning silicon, hardware and software for a security challenge that becomes more important as AI, autonomy and quantum computing scale. We believe Secure Compute will own the foundational layer across both commercial and national-security infrastructure,” Serendipity Capital founder and CEO Rob Jesudason said.

Department of War Announces a $450 Million Investment in The Elmet Group to Secure America's Tungsten Supply Chain

The Department of War's Office of the Assistant Secretary of War for Industrial Base Policy, in partnership with the Economic Defense Unit, announced today a $450 million redeemable preferred equity investment in The Elmet Group through the Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment program. This strategic investment will strengthen domestic tungsten capacity, bolster U.S. industrial resilience and military readiness, and help secure an essential material for the defense industrial base.
"This investment reflects the Department's commitment to rebuilding critical industrial capacity in the United States," said assistant secretary of War for industrial base policy Hon. Mike Cadenazzi. "Expanding domestic tungsten processing will strengthen supply chain resilience, support high-quality manufacturing jobs, and reinforce the production base behind essential defense systems."
The Elmet Group is the only U.S.-owned, fully integrated producer of tungsten and molybdenum materials and components, supports more than 100 Department of War programs, including the F-35, Patriot PAC-3, Trident D5, NGI, PrSM, and Virginia- and Columbia-class submarines. Tungsten is a foundational input for the defense industrial base, prized for its hardness, heat resistance, density, and durability, and used in critical components across missiles, munitions, aerospace, propulsion, naval, undersea, electronics, and industrial manufacturing applications.
"The Economic Defense Unit was created to identify critical industrial chokepoints before adversaries can exploit them and before they become battlefield risk," said George K. Kollitides II, director of the Economic Defense Unit. "Tungsten is essential to the systems that protect American warfighters and sustain deterrence, and this investment helps secure a domestic processing capability the United States cannot afford to leave exposed. By pairing targeted Department support with a disciplined preferred equity structure, we are strengthening the supply chain behind more than 100 defense programs while protecting taxpayers and delivering for the joint force."
The Department's investment into Elmet will also establish the only independent ammonium paratungstate facility in North America, which is a key step for tungsten processing and one of the largest chokepoints across the U.S. industrial base. By expanding U.S.-aligned refining and processing capacity, this investment will help reduce reliance on adversary-dominated supply chains in markets where China currently dominates global supply, including an estimated 85 percent of tungsten and 40 percent of molybdenum.
The Department's investment is expected to generate substantial economic benefits, including new high-tech jobs across Coldwater, Michigan, and Lewiston, Maine, preserving high-paying manufacturing jobs in Euclid, Ohio, and increasing demand for upstream mining jobs in Nevada.
It is also expected to support approximately 1,200 downstream jobs across manufacturing, engineering, and logistics networks tied to major defense suppliers.
The investment reflects the Department's broader strategy to secure critical industrial inputs, protect the defense supply chain, and ensure the United States can produce the materials required for sustained military advantage.

SAIPAN, Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands — Leaders from U.S. Pacific Command and Joint Task Force-Micronesia met with leaders from the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands at the quarterly CNMI Stakeholders Meeting in Susupe, Sept. 9-10.
Over the two-day meetings, leaders received updates on military activities and efforts throughout the CNMI to include recovery efforts from Super Typhoons Sinlaku and Bavi, military construction progress and proposed developments, planned military exercises and training, business development, biosecurity and the future of the CNMI Stakeholders Meetings.
CNMI Governor David Apatang shared his appreciation to the military and CNMI stakeholders for their continued hard work, commitment, and support.
“This continued collaboration is important as our commonwealth continues to navigate challenges, from powerful typhoons and recovery efforts to ongoing economic pressures,” he said. “These meetings provide an opportunity for the CNMI’s voice to be heard. We must ensure that the needs of the commonwealth remain part of these discussions. That means prioritizing locally available resources, creating opportunities for local businesses, and strengthening partnerships that allow the CNMI to play a greater role in supporting regional and national priorities. Through continued cooperation, we can advance shared objectives while building a stronger, more resilient commonwealth.”
U.S. Navy Rear Adm. Josh Lasky, commander, Joint Task Force-Micronesia attended the meeting virtually from Guam.
"Joint Task Force-Micronesia values the trust and collaboration we share with the Commonwealth," he said. "Meetings like this ensure our efforts are aligned with the needs of the CNMI, and that as we build capability and resilience together, the commonwealth and its people remain at the center of that work."
U.S. Air Force Maj. Gen. Christopher Faurot, mobilization assistant to the commander, U.S. Pacific Command thanked participants for their attendance and commitment to the partnership between the CNMI and armed forces.
“National security, economic security, and energy security are inseparable," he said. "A resilient CNMI strengthens our ability to defend the homeland, and investments that strengthen military readiness should also strengthen the communities that make that readiness possible. When the CNMI is more resilient, our Joint Force—and our nation—are more resilient.”
Following the meetings in Saipan, a delegation of Department of War officials traveled to Tinian, where they shared updates to military activities on the island.
Joint Task Force - Micronesia will synchronize operations and activities across all domains, enabling a robust warfighting posture while enhancing partner nation capacity. Dedicated to promoting regional stability, our mission performs Homeland Defense, Defense Support to Civil Authorities, and Foreign Humanitarian Assistance through a whole of government approach within its assigned joint operations area.
