AI-designed bespoke mRNA therapy reduces melanoma recurrence, metastasis, and death 
Merck and Moderna’s Phase III clinical trial demonstrates the effectiveness of bespoke mRNA therapy, hinting at potential treatments for other cancers.
Søren Hough , Editor, Drug Modalities September 7, 2026
schedule 10 Min Read 
Unsplash/okeykat 
link 
When Katalin Karikó began her work on mRNA technology , her first idea wasn’t to create a vaccine – it was to treat disease. A few years, a pandemic, and one Nobel Prize later, a late-stage human trial has finally confirmed that mRNA can be given to patients as a therapeutic. 
Last month, Moderna and Merck & Co. (known as MSD outside of North America) announced positive results from its Phase III INTerpath-001 trial ( NCT05933577 ). The study investigated the efficacy of Moderna’s mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) therapeutic intismeran autogene (also known as mRNA-4157 or V940) in combination with Merck’s checkpoint inhibitor antibody, pembrolizumab (Keytruda). The unpublished results suggest that the two-pronged approach dramatically improved treatment and survival when compared with the antibody alone. 
This positive signal for an mRNA therapeutic could portend a sea change in cancer treatment. This is the first mRNA immunotherapy to pass the final hurdle of a Phase III clinical trial. Intismeran is also the first bespoke (patient-specific) cancer immunotherapy that has a chance of receiving regulatory approval – a level of customization made possible by Moderna’s artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm. The combination of these emerging technologies raises important questions about their design and regulation. 
Related: MHRA unleashes guidance on mRNA immunotherapies 
For this two-part story , BioXconomy reached out to a range of experts, from the primary investigators studying intismeran to external scholars researching the role of machine learning and AI in drug design. We found that their general sentiment is excitement at what these Phase III results could mean for addressing other forms of cancer. Not everyone is sold just yet – but even the most careful scientists we spoke to remain cautiously optimistic. 
“Landmark moment” 
INTerpath-001 divided over 1,100 trial participants with Stagead IIB–IV cutaneous melanoma into two groups. The first group received pembrolizumab alone, while the other received the antibody alongside intismeran. The trial was set to run for approximately one year with the proviso that dosing would end if the patients experienced “unacceptable toxicity” following treatment. 
The team found that the combination of intismeran and pembrolizumab offered a dramatic improvement on preventing metastasis, recurrence, and death in patients compared to the antibody on its own. The researchers noted in their press release that they saw no new safety indications – for example, severe adverse reactions – relative to the baseline set by previous intismeran trials. 
Related: First mRNA cancer vaccines a paradigm shift for treatment 
Georgina Long, professor, director, and medical oncologist at the Melanoma Institute Australia, was the lead investigator on INTerpath-001. 
“This is the first Phase III study to show that intismeran, a treatment based on the unique mutational ‘fingerprint’ of a patient’s own tumor, given in combination with pembrolizumab, can reduce the risk of recurrence or death in patients with completely resected stage IIB–IV melanoma compared to pembrolizumab alone,” she shared with us in a statement. “Intismeran, in combination with pembrolizumab, has the potential to establish a new treatment paradigm in the adjuvant melanoma setting, helping patients remain cancer-free for longer.” 
A Melanoma Institute spokesperson called the trial results a “landmark moment” in melanoma care. They added that Long and the team at the Melanoma Institute are looking forward to the full Phase III trials being published. They said this data will be shared “at a congress later this year.” 
The positive results of this Phase III trial build on a Phase IIb trial called KEYNOTE-942 ( NCT03897881 ). That study yielded similarly promising data earlier this year: pembrolizumab plus intismeran led to a 59% reduction in distant melanoma metastasis or death and a 49% reduction in recurrence or death when compared to the antibody by itself. 
Related: Moderna trial suggests mRNA vaccine may halt solid tumor growth 
For lead investigator Adnan Khattak, medical oncologist at One Clinical Research and Edith Cowan University in Australia, those numbers were only part of a much bigger story. 
“For me, the most important aspect of KEYNOTE-942 was not simply the magnitude of the clinical result, but the proof of principle,” Khattak told BioXconomy . “For the first time, we have seen a personalized immune-modulating approach – an individualized neoantigen therapy [INT] combined with checkpoint inhibition – demonstrate meaningful improvement in outcomes in patients with high-risk resected melanoma.” 
“That is conceptually very important,” he continued. “Rather than giving every patient an identical immune therapy, we are effectively providing the immune system with information derived from that patient's own tumor and attempting to direct immunity toward those tumor-specific targets.” 
Dusting for fingerprINTs 
mRNA-based immunotherapies are often referred to as “vaccines” in the press and even by drug developers due to their role promoting an immune response in the patient. Yet some organizations have pushed back against the term. For example, UK regulators stated in 2025 that “individualized mRNA cancer immunotherapies do not meet the definition of vaccines” because they treat disease rather than prevent it. 
Moderna and Merck also avoided using the term in their press release. A Merck spokesperson clarified their choice of terminology to BioXconomy . 
“Intismeran is a therapeutic vaccine, not a prophylactic vaccine,” the spokesperson said. “Unlike preventive vaccines, intismeran is designed to address an existing clinical challenge by activating tumor-specific immune responses after cancer has already been diagnosed.” 
The decision to use the term “individualized neoantigen therapy (INT)” over “therapeutic vaccine” is intended to emphasize the bespoke nature of intismeran. 
“We use the term INT because it better reflects what makes this approach unique. Rather than taking a one-size-fits-all approach, INTs are designed around the unique mutational signature found in an individual patient's tumor.” 
That means each patient needs their cancerous tissue extracted and analyzed so that it can be used to design an mRNA-LNP formulation that fits their needs. 
“Intismeran is designed using a patient’s tumor sample to identify the unique mutational signature, or ‘fingerprint,’ of their cancer,” the spokesperson explained. “This information is then used to create a personalized synthetic mRNA coding for up to 34 neoantigens – abnormal proteins that arise from mutations in cancer cells and are not found in healthy cells.” 
“Since these tumor-specific mutations are unique to each individual, they could create a personalized therapy tailored to generate anti-cancer immunity.” 
This precision medicine approach is what excites Khattak, who believes classical cancer therapeutics are too broad-brush to address the disease effectively. 
“Many of our systemic cancer treatments remain relatively generic,” he told us. “Chemotherapy, and to a considerable extent immunotherapy, are administered according to tumor type and stage rather than being individually designed for a particular patient's cancer.” 
His point echoes sentiments we’ve heard from other industry leaders about the drawbacks of chemotherapy: the nonspecific side effects are potentially life-altering . 
“The direction we need to move toward is the right treatment for the right patient at the right time, rather than a one-size-fits-all approach.” 
Researchers have begun to explore how to generate personalized mRNA-LNP therapies for use in the clinic, for example in the realm of genome editing . 
“We have already made substantial progress with personalized targeted therapies, where treatment is selected according to specific molecular alterations,” Khattak continued. “What has historically been much more difficult is developing a truly personalized immune-modulating therapy.” 
mRNA-based cancer therapeutics are advancing across the world. BioXconomy has covered how these medicines are being tested against late-stage lung cancer , pancreatic cancer , and solid tumors . 
“Individualized neoantigen therapy represents an important step in that direction,” said Khattak. “The treatment is designed around the unique mutational and neoantigen profile of an individual patient's tumor, with the aim of generating a tumor-specific immune response. The encouraging results from KEYNOTE-942, and now the subsequent Phase III program, suggest that this concept can translate into clinically meaningful benefit.” 
Resource cost 
Bespoke cancer drugs like intismeran could shift paradigms around cancer treatment and give hope to patients who have run out of other options. However, what the drug gains in customization could also make it an expensive medicine to produce, with potential consequences for patient access. 
“These therapies are inherently resource intensive,” Khattak confirmed. “They require tumor sequencing, sophisticated computational analysis, selection of patient-specific neoantigens, individualized manufacturing, quality assurance, and rapid delivery back to the treating center. I would therefore expect the initial costs to be substantial.” 
Still, he believes it’s premature to think about pricing. “It is difficult to predict the eventual cost at this stage, as pricing will ultimately be determined by the sponsors and the healthcare systems in which these treatments are introduced.” 
The Merck spokesperson agreed. 
“It’s too early at this stage to comment on pricing or access,” the Merck spokesperson said. “MSD has had a long history of responsibly pricing medicines and vaccines to reflect their value to patients, payers, and society, and we plan to continue to uphold this commitment for any pipeline asset that may come to market in the future.” 
Khattak believes that even a high price may be warranted given the typical costs of cancer treatment for the patient and the wider healthcare system. 
“The key question should ultimately be value rather than acquisition cost alone,” Khattak said. “We will need robust health-economic and cost-benefit analyses incorporating not only the price of manufacturing the therapy but also the potential value of preventing recurrence, metastatic disease, and subsequent lines of treatment.” 
Looking ahead 
There is still more information to come on the Phase III trial once it has undergone peer review. But if the data bears out, Khattak believes mRNA-based INTs could find applications in other cancer types. 
“I think the broader significance extends well beyond melanoma,” he said. “Individualized neoantigen therapies are being investigated across a range of tumor types, and we hope that ongoing studies will reproduce the encouraging results seen in melanoma.” 
Researchers like Khattak envision a world where medicines aren’t designed against common denominator mutations but rather the precise variants found in patient tumors. 
“For decades, personalized oncology has largely meant matching molecularly targeted drugs to particular genomic abnormalities,” he continued. “We may now be entering an era in which we can also personalize the immune response itself.” 
“If these results continue to be confirmed across Phase III studies and other cancers, this could represent an important shift in how we think about cancer treatment – from treating a tumor category to increasingly treating the unique biology of an individual patient's tumor.” 
Not everyone is as optimistic about the future of mRNA tech. Jared Auclair and Rominder Singh, both of whom serve on faculty at Northeastern University in Boston and who study emerging technologies in drug development, are waiting to see more data. Neither were involved in the development or testing of intismeran. 
“Moderna and Merck's melanoma results represent real progress, but we don't read them as proof that mRNA cancer vaccines work broadly,” Auclair and Singh shared with BioXconomy . “A search of ClinicalTrials.gov shows 32 active mRNA cancer vaccine studies, and to date only one has produced a clear positive result.” 
For Auclair and Singh, this stagnation runs up against a broader context of mRNA medicines that have been unable to make headway in the clinic. 
“Just a few days after the Moderna results, BioNTech and Genentech terminated their colorectal cancer vaccine trial, and Moderna's own CMV vaccine failed in Phase III last October,” they said. “The experts believe that the differing outcomes come down to tumor biology and trial design, not the mRNA platform itself where melanoma is immunologically ‘hot’ and responds well to immunotherapy while colorectal cancer is ‘cold’ and has historically resisted it.” 
For now, Auclair and Singh are keeping an open mind as to whether the tide could turn on the tech. 
“We see mRNA as a promising delivery chassis, but with 32 shots on goal and only one scored so far, time will tell whether that one success translates into a broader pattern or stays an outlier.” 
Quotes have been lightly edited for clarity. This article was updated on September 7, 2026, to update Adnan Khattak's affiliation. Click here to read the second part of this story.

London —Dentons has advised the National Wealth Fund on its investment of up to US$70 million (£52.6 million) in Nexeon Ltd, a leading developer of advanced silicon-based battery materials. The investment will support the expansion of the company's domestic operations, strengthening the UK's battery supply chain, creating jobs and boosting growth.
The National Wealth Fund's investment forms part of Nexeon's latest funding round, which is expected to raise a total of US$133 million (£100 million). It will support the development of Nexeon's UK-based pilot manufacturing facility, enabling the company to scale its advanced manufacturing technology unit and research and development capabilities. 
The transaction was led by Projects Partner Torquil Law and Corporate Partner Adam Knowles , with assistance from Corporate and Projects associates Murray Newell , Mel Mahon  and Karina Chopra  and other Dentons UK colleagues from its Projects, Corporate, Environment, Competition, Employment and Pensions, and Technology, Media and Telecoms teams.
Torquil Law commented: "We are delighted to have advised the National Wealth Fund on this investment, which will help decarbonise supply chains, boost place-based investment, and strengthen sovereign capabilities - supporting all three of the National Wealth Fund’s strategic ambitions."

Criteo Names Guillaume Dupont As New ANZ Country Head
Staff Writer September 7, 2026 News 
Surprisingly Useful AI Article Enhancements
Criteo, the global commerce intelligence platform, has appointed Guillaume Dupont as Country Head for Australia and New Zealand, as the company looks to build on local growth across retail media, AI-assisted commerce and cross-channel capabilities.
Dupont currently serves as Head of Monetisation (Retailers & Marketplaces) at Criteo ANZ and brings more than 15 years of experience across eCommerce and advertising technology. During his time at Criteo, he has held senior roles spanning retail media, agency partnerships, mid-market operations and enterprise accounts across Australia and New Zealand.
The appointment comes amid a period of growth for Criteo’s ANZ operations. Total media spend on its platform grew 10 per cent year on year in 2025, while 2026 has delivered 32 per cent growth year to date. Retail media has been a key contributor, with media spend on Criteo’s retail media platform in Australia and New Zealand growing more than fivefold over the past 12 months.
Guillaume Dupont. 
Executive Managing Director of Criteo APAC, Szi-Wei Lo, highlighted the local market’s trajectory as a driver behind the appointment.
“ANZ is an important growth market for Criteo, underpinned by momentum in retail media and an evolving commerce landscape,” Lo remarked. “Guillaume has played an important role in building our business locally, and his appointment positions us well to build on that momentum as we lead Criteo ANZ into its next phase of growth.”
Retail Media Footprint Expanding
In his new role, Dupont will oversee both the retail media and performance media businesses, driving the company’s broader cross-channel and full-funnel strategy. His focus will include helping brands and retailers connect commerce data, media activation and measurement to deliver measurable outcomes across the shopper journey, alongside navigating emerging opportunities in AI-assisted commerce.
Criteo’s retail media platform is now live with six Australian retailers spanning health, beauty, fashion, quick commerce and CPG. The roster includes Uber Eats, Chemist Warehouse, David Jones, JB Hi-Fi, Dan Murphy’s and BWS.
Dupont pointed to the retail media foundation as a launchpad for broader ambitions.
“ANZ is a dynamic commerce market, and I’m excited to lead Criteo into its next phase of growth here,” Dupont commented. “We’ve built momentum in retail media, working with some of Australia’s leading retailers, and there’s a real opportunity to build on that foundation as commerce becomes more AI-assisted and increasingly cross-channel.”
“My focus will be on bringing our capabilities together to help brands and retailers connect with consumers across the journey and turn commerce intelligence into measurable growth.”
AI Reshaping Commerce Discovery
The appointment arrives as commerce is becoming increasingly AI-assisted and cross-channel, creating new pathways for consumers to discover and evaluate products across large language models, retailer environments, social platforms and the open web.
Criteo data indicates that AI-referred visits convert at 1.5 times the rate of other referral channels, while more than 70 per cent of LLM-referred users land directly on product pages. The company argues this demonstrates how AI is beginning to connect high-intent consumers with retailers and create new discovery moments.
While these emerging channels are generating additional entry points for product discovery, Criteo maintains that retailers and brands remain central to transactions, fulfilment and customer relationships. The company is positioning commerce intelligence as a layer that connects discovery signals with real shopping behaviour to help brands and retailers deliver more relevant experiences and measure outcomes.
ChatGPT Ads Partnership
As ChatGPT Ads’ first adtech partner, Criteo is bringing advertiser demand into ChatGPT and helping shape how commerce and advertising experiences evolve within AI-driven environments.
Campaigns are currently live across APAC markets including Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Korea and India, alongside the US, Canada and Europe.

Senior Performance Manager at Petbarn, Ben Zieschang, offered a perspective on the early results of the partnership.
“ChatGPT is a new way to connect with pet parents,” Zieschang explained. “Working with Criteo on this pilot enables us to engage while they’re actively researching what’s best for their pet.”
Cross-Channel Commerce Strategy
Through its cross-channel, full-funnel approach, Criteo is working to help ANZ brands and retailers connect commerce data, media activation and measurement across the customer journey, from discovery through to purchase, while providing greater transparency into the media and experiences driving measurable outcomes.
Criteo operates a global commerce intelligence platform built on proprietary commerce data from more than $1 trillion in annual sales and two decades of AI development. The company works with clients and partners across global retail and digital commerce. Further information is available at www.criteo.com .

U.S. drugmaker Moderna is expanding its cancer drug development following the phase 3 success of its personalized messenger RNA (mRNA) cancer vaccine.
Beyond combination therapy with immunotherapy, the company is evaluating the potential for a vaccine-only regimen and is expected to broaden its research to "in vivo chimeric antigen receptor T cells (CAR-T)," which kill cancer cells directly in the body with a single injection.
A staged photo shows a syringe and needle placed in front of the Moderna logo of a U.S. pharmaceutical company. /Courtesy of Reuters Yonhap 
On the 7th, according to the pharmaceutical and biotech industry, Moderna is developing a range of mRNA-based cancer vaccines and therapies. Its personalized cancer vaccine "intismeran autogene," which recently delivered phase 3 results in combination with Merck's (MSD) immunotherapy Keytruda, is also undergoing additional studies, including a monotherapy approach.
Kim Hee-su, vice president at Moderna Korea, said, "In addition to the combination therapy co-developed with MSD, we are looking at the potential for intismeran autogene as a monotherapy," and added, "Preclinical studies are underway, and we expect to enter full-scale clinical trials around the end of next year."
The intismeran autogene and Keytruda combination therapy, whose clinical results were released in the previous month, met its primary endpoint of suppressing cancer recurrence and metastasis in a phase 3 trial in high-risk melanoma patients. This is the first time an mRNA-based cancer vaccine has met primary endpoints in a phase 3 trial.
Intismeran autogene is made as a patient-specific therapy by analyzing mutations unique to cancer cells from a patient's tumor tissue and selecting neoantigens likely to elicit an immune response.
Currently, MSD is leading the development of combination therapy, including late-stage trials. In Korea, MSD has completed enrollment of melanoma patients for late-stage trials and is conducting the study.
Building on these clinical results, Moderna plans to broaden the use of mRNA in cancer treatment beyond personalized cancer vaccines.
A representative area is "in vivo CAR-T," a next-generation CAR-T technology that kills cancer cells directly in the body with a single injection. By delivering RNA to specific immune cells to generate CAR-T cells inside the patient, it is considered a next-generation technology that could significantly change the manufacturing process of existing cell therapies.
Kim said, "If mRNA is applied to in vivo CAR-T, it could change the complex manufacturing steps of existing cell therapies," adding, "If we can reduce the process of harvesting a patient's cells, manipulating and culturing them externally, and reinfusing them, and instead induce immune cell function directly in the body, this could evolve into a new treatment approach."
The company is also developing mRNA therapies that target antigens commonly found in specific cancer patient groups. Its core candidate, "mRNA-4359," is in phase 2 as both a Keytruda combination and a monotherapy in melanoma and Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients. In phase 1/2 results released in April, it showed a meaningful antitumor response as a first-line treatment for advanced or metastatic melanoma.
While expanding the scope of its mRNA platform in oncology, Moderna is also seeking new growth drivers in infectious disease vaccines. A key next program is the norovirus vaccine.
Norovirus is a major infectious disease that causes vomiting and diarrhea, especially in winter, but vaccine development is considered difficult due to the virus's diversity and frequent mutations. Several corporations have attempted to develop vaccines in the past but fell short in clinical trials. Moderna is currently conducting late-stage clinical trials for its norovirus vaccine.
Moderna emphasizes that for its core business, the COVID-19 vaccine, it must maintain a stable vaccination base focused on older adults and high-risk groups.
As perceptions of COVID-19 as a cold-like illness spread recently, vaccination rates remain lower than for influenza. According to the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency, the budget for procuring next year's COVID-19 vaccines has decreased by about 10% from this year, and the procurement volume has also fallen by about 500,000 doses.
Kim said, "COVID-19 remains a significant respiratory infectious disease that can lead to hospitalization and death among older adults, so regular vaccination is needed for high-risk groups, including older adults and those with weakened immunity," adding, "As the older population grows, we must guarantee sufficient vaccination opportunities for high-risk groups when needed."

Revaluation of Advanced Packaging
半导体行业观察 2026-09-07 14:39 
Who is making money? The logic has changed. 
Open any latest AI accelerator, and you will find a common feature: the world's most expensive chips are all assembled from multiple small components called "chiplets". Several computing chips are arranged side by side, surrounded by a large amount of memory. If you want higher performance, why not just make a larger chip? The answer lies in the way chips are printed.
The chip manufacturing process uses a lithography scanner to project circuit patterns onto the wafer, and the maximum exposure area per shot is fixed at 26 × 33 mm, approximately 858 square millimeters. Chips must fit within a single exposure range, so 858 square millimeters is the physical limit of chip size. For many years, the size of NVIDIA's flagship GPUs has been constrained by this limit.
TSMC has achieved mass production of CoWoS packaging, with an exposure size 5.5 times that of ordinary packaging, capable of accommodating up to 12 HBM stacks, with a reported yield of over 98%. The roadmap released by TSMC at its North America Technology Symposium in April 2026 shows that its packaging size will reach 9.5 times in 2027 and 14-field in 2028. TSMC describes the 14x exposure field packaging as approximately 10 large computing chips plus 20 HBM stacks. Photoresist limits the size of individual chips, and the industry has broken through this limitation by packaging multiple chips in one package, which is exactly the development direction of packaging technology.
Profit Calculation: 
Splitting Alone Only Reaches Break-Even Point 
The second common reason for splitting chips is yield, but there is a widespread misunderstanding here. Manufacturing defects appear almost randomly on the wafer, so a larger chip means a higher probability of defects. Assuming the defect density is 0.1 per square centimeter, the calculation shows that the pass rate of a large 800-square-millimeter chip is about 45%, while the pass rate of a small 200-square-millimeter chip is about 82%. So is it really cost-effective to split a large chip into four pieces? All four chips must be qualified, which means multiplying 0.82 by itself four times, and the result is still 45%. As far as splitting chips alone is concerned, the gain is exactly at the break-even point.
The real advantage lies in the ability to test each component before assembly. The dies on the wafer can be probed one by one, and unqualified chips can be eliminated in advance. Qualified chips are called known good dies, or KGD for short. In the past, one defect would scrap the entire 800-square-millimeter processor, but now it only results in the loss of one 200-square-millimeter component. Reducing the loss unit from the entire product to a single component is the core of chip economics.
In fact, chip designers have been playing this game inside individual chips for a long time. The H100 physically contains 144 computing units, but NVIDIA only enables 132 of them: the reserved capacity ensures that no matter which unit has a defect, it will be shut down, and the rest of the units can still be delivered as a complete product. Cerebras uses the entire wafer as a single chip, taking this principle to the extreme, shrinking each core to 0.05 square millimeters, so that the impact of defects is limited to that exact scope. Chiplet extends the same principle beyond the chip boundary and brings two additional advantages. Components that do not require cutting-edge processes, such as I/O or cache, can be manufactured using cheaper mature nodes, and components verified once can be reused in other products. The mask size limit prompted the emergence of Chiplet; KGD sorting and node mixing made it profitable.
The Problem Has Not Disappeared, 
But Has Shifted Into the Package 
However, splitting chips does not make engineering design easier. The four tasks that were originally completed inside a monolithic chip now fall on the packaging layer. It must realize thousands of short and dense signal connections to ensure that all parts still work like a single chip; it must transmit hundreds of amperes of current without voltage drop; it must dissipate several kilowatts of heat; and it must firmly bond materials with mismatched thermal expansion coefficients (such as silicon, copper, organic substrates and packaging materials) under various temperature changes.
The more chips are stacked, the more severe the heat dissipation problem becomes. A simulation result released by the Belgian semiconductor research institute imec at the end of 2025 confirms this point: when HBM is directly stacked on the GPU (3D stacking) without any heat dissipation measures, the hot spot temperature reaches as high as 141.7°C; while the same silicon chips are placed side by side under the same heat dissipation conditions (2.5D stacking), the temperature remains at 69.1°C. The moment stacking is completed, the heat of the lower chip must be transferred to the upper chip. This is not just a simulation result.
The zHBM concept chip demonstrated by Samsung at the Hot Chips 2026 conference eliminates the interposer and stacks DRAM directly on the processor, which directly exposes it to heat dissipation problems. Samsung is trying to solve this problem by keeping the number of stacked layers at a low level (about four chips), mainly to reduce heat dissipation costs and avoid forming a single hot spot by dispersing I/O interfaces across the entire chip surface. At the same conference, Samsung's Heat Path Block technology and SK Hynix's iHBM technology also tried to solve the centralized heat dissipation problem from another perspective. Both technologies open up a dedicated heat dissipation channel in the interface area where heat accumulates. All of these are just attempts rather than finished products, and Samsung has not given a launch timetable for zHBM.
The bottleneck never disappears. It only shifts, and where it lands becomes the next equipment market.
The first step of the bottleneck stems from mask and yield calculation, that is, the wiring between chips. After that, the bottleneck continues to shift, and each step brings a question: from which vendors must the industry start purchasing equipment and materials?
Consequences Brought by This Transformation 
For fifty years, packaging has been a low-margin and tedious part of the semiconductor value chain. A wafer worth tens of thousands of dollars comes out of the fab, undergoes probe testing, thinning, and dicing, then is sent to a packaging plant in Penang (Malaysia) or Kaohsiung (Taiwan). The packaging plant only needs to solder a few wires, encapsulate the chip in a plastic shell, perform testing, and then ship it, with negligible cost. The entire packaging equipment market is worth approximately... 5 billion U.S. dollars in 2025, within the current range guided by the wafer manufacturing equipment market of 150 billion to 160 billion U.S. dollars in 2026. No one studied it because there was nothing worth writing about.
The above physical principles put an end to this possibility. A single chip cannot economically break through the limit of one exposure field, and the closer it gets to this limit, the more waste it generates. The only solution is to print multiple smaller chips and stitch them together on the same substrate, a process called advanced packaging. Since the speed of this connection now determines the performance of the chip, packaging technology has evolved from a low-cost encapsulation process to one of the most critical technologies in the AI field. And since only one manufacturer (TSMC) can reliably assemble these chips on a large scale, this factory determines who can sell AI chips.
The backend has become the allocation mechanism for global AI computing.
CoWoS allocation is the way computing resources are rationed: it is estimated that NVIDIA will occupy more than half of TSMC's CoWoS quota, about 630,000 wafers in 2026, and will increase to about 1 million wafers in 2027 according to supply chain conditions; Broadcom ranks second, while MediaTek, AMD and hyperscale data center operators share the remaining quota. TSMC said they will not choose between customers and will not give up any business, adding that despite all their efforts, supply remains very tight. According to different definitions, the supply-demand gap in 2026 is expected to be between 10% and 20%. The data in June only includes accelerators, while the data in July incorporates the demand for server CPUs into the same queue. Without access to CoWoS quotas, AI chips cannot be delivered, and the increase in wafer capacity will not change this.
Today, the packaging business has become the top revenue source for one of the world's most important companies, TSMC: TSMC's backend revenue has risen from about 2.5 billion U.S. dollars in 2023 to 7.5 billion U.S. dollars in 2024, and is expected to reach around 12 billion U.S. dollars in 2025-2026. The proportion of advanced packaging products in TSMC's sales will grow from about 9% in 2026 to 16-18% in 2030. TSMC is already the world's largest packaging company, and is consolidating its position with a 50% growth rate.
The flow of funds has changed: ASE has raised its 2026 capital expenditure plan twice to 10.5 billion U.S. dollars, of which 70% of the equipment portion is used for cutting-edge packaging and testing. Amkor is investing heavily, putting 7 billion U.S. dollars into its Arizona plant. Intel requires customers to prepay for EMIB-T substrates, and in Intel's own words, customers responded enthusiastically with prepayments amounting to billions of dollars.
At the semiconductor conference in August, the clearest message from computing vendors was: supply, not demand, is the constraint; NVIDIA is actively locking in substrate and DRAM supply; AMD's growing server market share benefits both from the substrate capacity booked during the pandemic and its Venice architecture on the N2 platform. The supply chain determines revenue, and packaging is the supply chain.
The scale behind this is not dominated by NVIDIA alone:
By 2025, about 518,000 wafers per month use some form of stacking technology, accounting for about 8% of all wafers.
By 2030, this figure is expected to reach about 3.5 million wafers per month, accounting for 38% of the total output of the entire industry, among which HBM, NAND CBA and DRAM CBA will dominate the output, while logic chips carry the value.
The tool and consumable companies serving this market are not in a cyclical fluctuation, but are experiencing a platform reshaping of the way the entire industry assembles products.
What Is Advanced Packaging? 
Why There Are Several Times Differences in Published Data? 
Published estimates for the same market range from less than 200 billion U.S. dollars to more than 500 billion U.S. dollars this year, with annual growth rates ranging from 11% to 59%. Why are the differences so large? Because they are counting different contents, so let's map out the value chain of advanced packaging.
The level you focus on determines which companies look like winners:
Based on revenue, TSMC becomes the focus.
Based on production volume, the scale of OSAT (Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test) looks larger than it actually is.
Based on wafer volume, the rise of Disco seems unstoppable.
Based on equipment, the entire industry looks very small, which is why ordinary investors ignore it.
Conclusion: The truly important number is capital expenditure, not revenue.
For investors at the equipment and materials level, the correct denominator should be the expenditure of packaging vendors, not their revenue, because payments to equipment suppliers come from expenditures, and expenditures come earlier and are stronger than revenue. Only two large OSATs have expenditures of about 13 billion U.S. dollars this year. TSMC allocates 10-20% of its mid-year raised capital expenditure budget to advanced packaging. Intel has allocated a large part of its increased capital expenditure to EMIB-T, and memory manufacturers are expanding HBM TSV capacity, targeting approximately 760kwpm by the end of 2027. Capital expenditure in the advanced packaging field easily exceeds 20 billion U.S. dollars every year, growing faster than wafer manufacturing equipment, and is concentrated in a small number of suppliers.
Disassemble the Advanced Packaging Supply Chain 
It should be noted that due to the rapid development of the packaging industry, its market share data is usually only valid for about one year. To disassemble the advanced packaging supply chain, the easiest way to understand is to divide the process of chips from design to final system into five layers, plus a design layer that runs through all layers. Each layer has its own economic benefits, market share and certification cycle.
Materials: Ajinomoto's ABF thickening film is used in almost all high-performance packaging, with a market share of over 95%, and the company announced a 30% price increase in May. Nittobo's T-glass cloth is used to control the warpage of substrate core materials. ABF substrates themselves are manufactured by companies such as Ibiden (accounting for 70-80% of Blackwell substrates), Unimicron, Shinko, Nan Ya PCB, AT&S and Kinsus. Resonac provides die attach films for dicing, while Kao occupies about 60% of the substrate cleaning agent market share.
On the packaging vendor side: TSMC's 3DFabric platform (CoWoS, SoIC, InFO and WMCM) is the reference architecture and also the bottleneck. Intel Foundry provides EMIB, EMIB-T and Foveros packaging. Samsung provides turnkey HBM packaging services and has its own glass interposer product line.
On the OSAT vendor side: ASE (in partnership with SPIL) is the largest vendor and the only one with wafer-level advanced capital expenditure. Amkor is the local US alternative and Intel's first external EMIB assembler. JCET, TFME and Hua Tian Technology are Chinese vendors. KYEC, Sigurd and Ardentec are testing specialists.
Equipment: Bonders come from Besi, Hanmi, ASMPT, Kulicke & Soffa, SEMES, Hanwha, Shinkawa and Shibaura. Grinders and dicers come from Disco and Tokyo Seimitsu. Wafer bonders come from EV Group, Tokyo Electron and SUSS MicroTec. Packaging lithography equipment comes from Canon, Ushio and Nikon. Wet process equipment comes from GPTC and Scientech. Molding equipment comes from Towa, Yamaha Robotics and Besi. TSV etching and plating equipment comes from Lam Research and Applied Materials, CMP equipment comes from Applied and Ebara, temporary bonding and debonding equipment comes from SUSS, Tazmo and Tokyo Electron. Dispensing and thermal bonding equipment comes from All Ring, Nordson and Musashi.

AboitizPower expands industrial solar push
Maria Bernadette Romero · 5 September 2026 · 10:58 PM PHT · 2 MIN READ 
AUSI and Proterial Philippines will install the first ground-mounted, a solar photovoltaic system targeted for commercial operations in 2027 within Batangas province-located LIMA Estate, the largest privately owned industrial estate in the country. Aboitiz InfraCapital Economic Estates, the infrastructure division of conglomerate Aboitiz Group, fully acquired the site from the Alsons Land Corp. and Japanese firm Marubeni Corporation in 2014.
PHOTOGRAPH courtesy of Property Guru
Text size A− Reset A+ 
Save 
Aboitiz Power Corp. is expanding its industrial solar footprint through a new 20-year power supply deal that will bring a 1,587.20-kilowatt-peak solar facility to LIMA Estate in Batangas.
Advent Upgrade Solar Inc. (AUSI), a joint venture between AboitizPower Distributed Renewables Inc. and Upgrade Energy Philippines Inc., signed a power purchase agreement with Proterial Philippines Inc. for the ground-mounted solar photovoltaic system.
Set for commercial operations Q1 2027 
Targeted to begin commercial operations in the first quarter of 2027, the project will be the first ground-mounted solar installation within LIMA Estate.
“We are incredibly proud to partner with you on what is the very first ground-mounted solar facility in LIMA Estate. By pioneering this installation, Proterial is setting a new benchmark for industrial sustainability in the region,” AUSI chairperson and Upgrade Energy Philippines president and CEO Ruth Yu-Owen said on Friday.
“Together with Proterial and LIMA Estate, we are proving that industrial growth and environmental responsibility can move forward hand-in-hand, and we look forward to building on this partnership over the next 20 years,” she added.
Expected to avoid 1,400 tons of carbon dioxide yearly 
Proterial expects the solar facility to avoid more than 1,400 tons of carbon dioxide equivalent annually, or about 28,000 tons over the 20-year agreement.
“Through this collaboration, we are taking a meaningful step toward reducing our carbon footprint, enhancing energy efficiency, and contributing to the country’s transition to a more sustainable energy landscape,” Proterial Philippines President Yoshiaki Yamashita said.
“As a responsible corporate organization, we recognize the growing importance of renewable energy in addressing environmental challenges while supporting long-term economic growth,” he added.
LIMA Estate locator since 1997 
Proterial Philippines, formerly Hitachi Cable Philippines Inc., is the local manufacturing arm of Japan-based Proterial Ltd. and has been a locator at LIMA Estate since 1997.
AUSI develops, builds, and operates distributed solar solutions for large commercial and industrial customers.

Ambarella reported fiscal Q2 revenue of $108.1 million, up 13.2% year over year, and adjusted earnings of $0.18 per share versus $0.17 expected. Shares remained sharply lower following the results, extending a 5.6% regular-session decline as investors weighed margin and memory-supply uncertainty. The results arrived weeks after a report that NXP was in talks to acquire the company, talks that might not produce a deal. Ambarella, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMBA ) supplies edge-AI vision chips; NXP Semiconductors N.V. (NASDAQ: NXPI ) could add distribution across vehicles and industrial systems. 
TSMC’s 2nm Era Is Accelerating With MediaTek. Nvidia and Alphabet Already Have Money on the Table Ambarella's bull case is efficient inference near the device. Cameras, driver-assistance systems, and robots need low-power processing without sending every frame to the cloud. Management guided fiscal Q3 revenue to $115 million to $124 million, indicating continued growth. Insider Monkey counted 33 hedge funds holding AMBA at June 30, down from 35 at March 31. Millennium Management reported 41,318 shares at June 30 after sharply reducing its position during the quarter. 
The bear case sits in expectations. The acquisition report lifted Ambarella about 19% on July 31, so part of the takeover premium was already embedded before earnings. A buyer could walk away, negotiate a lower price, or face integration challenges. Even without a deal, memory constraints and customer timing can pressure revenue, while other supply-chain costs can weigh on margins. 
NXP's rationale would be strategic breadth. Ambarella could strengthen software-defined vehicle, radar, vision, and edge-inference offerings inside NXP's automotive relationships. Hedge-fund participation rose to 60 funds holding NXP Semiconductors N.V. (NASDAQ:NXPI) in Q2 from 51 in Q1. Lyrical Asset Management held 887,619 shares after trimming 5%. 
NXP shareholders face acquisition discipline. Buying a volatile growth company after a rumor-driven rise could dilute returns, and combining roadmaps does not guarantee design wins. NXP shares fell about 3% when the talks were reported, showing that investors recognized the cost side. 
The August 14 settlement showed 4.07 million AMBA shares sold short, about 9.72% of float, with 3.42 days to cover. It predates earnings but follows the takeover report. Ambarella's edge-AI opportunity remains intact; the stock now asks investors to underwrite both execution and optional deal value. Guidance, gross margin, and a definitive filing matter more than continuing speculation. 
If no agreement emerges, the share price will have to rest on standalone design wins. Automotive production schedules are long and cancellations can be painful, making customer concentration and backlog conversion essential checks. If a deal does emerge, price, financing, regulatory conditions, and retention of engineering talent will determine whether NXP creates value.

Veolia sponsors Professional Pickleball Association tournaments
The investments from Veolia include water refill stations, a paint recycling program, recycled-material benches, pickleball recycling and an upcycled trophy.
Image courtesy of Veolia 
Posted by
Alexandra Golden, Assistant Editor 
Published September 04, 2026
Listen to article 
/ 
Veolia, a waste management company based in France with North American headquarters in Boston, has partnered with the Professional Pickleball Association (PPA) for the past three years to reduce waste and conserve resources. 
Veolia sponsors six tournaments on the professional tour per year, which includes two tournaments in September, the Veolia Pickleball National Championships in Cary, North Carolina, and the Veolia Arizona Open in Mesa, Arizona. 
The company sponsored events in Dallas/McKinney, Texas, in March and Atlanta in May and will sponsor events in Chicago and Los Angeles/Malibu in October and December, respectively. 
Veolia says it helps reduce waste and conserve resources throughout tournament operations by offering water refill stations, recycled-material benches, pickleball recycling initiatives and an upcycled trophy.
“Pickleball’s growth presents a unique opportunity to demonstrate that sustainability can grow with the sport itself,” says Laurent Obadia, deputy CEO in charge of stakeholders and communication at Veolia. “Our strategic partnership with the PPA Tour shows how simple, measurable solutions can reduce waste, conserve resources and create lasting benefits for host communities while enhancing the experience for players and fans as the sport continues to grow.”
At tournament sites across the country, leftover paint used to mark pickleball courts is collected in 55-gallon drums by Veolia teams and transported to the company’s solvent recovery facilities where it is processed and repurposed rather than discarded. 
Veolia estimates it has collected at least 48 drums across 12 PPA Tour tournaments, accounting for more than 2,000 gallons of material diverted from disposal and returned to productive use through recovery and recycling processes.
“Fans increasingly expect organizations to take sustainability seriously,” Carvana PPA Tour founder and CEO Connor Pardoe says. “Our partnership with Veolia demonstrates that sustainability can be visible, practical and measurable. It’s helping us build a stronger future for the sport while creating positive impacts in the communities that host our events.”
Paint recovery is an example of the sustainability initiatives Veolia and the PPA Tour have implemented across the tour to advance the circular economy by finding practical ways to recover materials, reduce waste and keep valuable resources in use for longer, the entities say. 
Veolia also supports recycling programs, circular economy demonstrations and the use of upcycled materials throughout tournament activations across the PPA Tour.

Mercedes-AMG Motorsport Extends Its Official Automotive Partnership With The Nürburgring
The legendary racing venue continues to keep Mercedes-AMG Motorsport as its Official Automotive Partner.
by 
Tyler Rampersaud – September 03, 2026
Mercedes-AMG Mercedes-Benz Mercedes-Benz News Motorsport 
- Advertisement -
It’s where records are broken, dreams come to fruition or are shattered, and where legacies are forged for drivers, manufacturers, and cars alike. The Nürburgring is one of the world’s most daunting racing venues, with its incredibly long Nordschleife layout, dramatic elevation changes, and a forested setting. Nicknamed the “Green Hell” for how challenging it is, the Nürburgring has become a measuring stick for performance at the highest echelon of the automotive industry, and its official automotive partner is Mercedes-AMG Motorsport. 
That partnership has just been extended, with Mercedes-AMG remaining the Official Automotive Partner of the legendary track. Originally minted in 2017, the partnership is a reaffirmation of the shared history between Mercedes-Benz and the Nürburgring that stretches back nearly a century. 
With the partnership’s extension, Mercedes-AMG will continue to have a prominent brand presence at the Nürburgring, including at the iconic Carousel corner, and, in addition, naming rights to the AMG Arena and the AMG Grandstand on the Grand Prix circuit will also remain. The AMG VIP Lounge will also continue as a part of the partnership. 
The very first race held at the Nürburgring, which took place in 1927, was won by a Mercedes-Benz , specifically by Rudolf Caracciola. More recently, Mercedes-AMG Motorsport celebrated an overall victory at this past May’s ADAC RAVENOL 24h Nürburgring, with the Mercedes-AMG Team RAVENOL and drivers Maro Engel, Maxime Martin, Fabian Schiller, and Luca Stolz. 
Outside of competition, the Nürburgring has been an important venue for testing Mercedes-AMG road cars, providing a respectable gauntlet for all standards of automotive performance. Recently, the Mercedes-AMG CLA 45 4MATIC+ set a new record in its category with its Nürburgring Nordschleife lap time of 7:32.070. 
About the continued partnership, Simon Wilbers, Head of Mercedes-AMG Motorsport, commented, “Whether in motorsport or as a benchmark for our road cars, the Nürburgring has always held a special significance for the brand. It has been the setting for numerous milestones, from historic racing victories to pioneering record-breaking runs. In addition, we have now shared an official partnership for ten years, underlining our emotional connection with this unique race circuit. We are delighted to continue this successful collaboration in the years ahead.” 
With a cherished shared history and icon status among both brands, the Nürburgring and Mercedes-AMG Motorsport are celebrating a fruitful partnership for nearly a decade by continuing it for years to come.

Asahi Kasei opens wet-process separator coating line at Celgard’s Charlotte plant
Posted September 3, 2026 by Chris Ruoff & filed under Newswire , The Tech . 
Asahi Kasei has opened a Hipore wet-process lithium-ion battery separator coating line at its Celgard manufacturing facility in Charlotte, North Carolina, establishing North America-based coating and supply capability for its wet-process separators. 
The coating line adds wet-process separators to a plant that has produced dry-process separators in the US since 1986. Asahi Kasei made the investment decision in 2023, and commercial production is scheduled to begin in the second half of fiscal 2026.
Toyota Tsusho has entered a capacity rights agreement tied to the facility.
A separator is the porous membrane that keeps a lithium-ion cell’s anode and cathode apart while letting ions pass between them. Wet-process and dry-process separators are made by different manufacturing routes.
The Charlotte line is paired with a wet-process separator plant under construction in Canada, which Asahi Kasei says is progressing according to plan. The company describes the coating line as the first step toward a regional supply structure for wet-process separators, and says North American battery demand will expand beyond electric vehicles into energy storage systems.
“By leveraging Celgard’s experienced workforce and established operations, we are expanding our North American product portfolio to include both dry-process and Hipore wet-process technologies,” said Ryu Taniguchi, President of Asahi Kasei Battery Separator Corporation. “Together with our planned separator facility in Canada, this investment will bring production capabilities closer to the region’s battery market and position Asahi Kasei to swiftly respond as demand grows across electric vehicles and energy storage systems.”
Source: Asahi Kasei

Syensqo to double capacity with new aromatic compounding line in India
New line at Panoli site will support growing automotive demand with flexible, local sourcing 
By ICN Bureau | September 03, 2026 
Syensqo's Panoli site, India. Photo: Syensqo.
Syensqo, a premier global producer of advanced materials, has announced a strategic investment in a new high-performance aromatic polymer compounding line at its facility in Panoli, India. This expansion strengthens the company's supply chain and engineering support for the country's booming automotive industry.
Scheduled for Q1 2028, Syensqo's new production line will double its compounding capacity at the Panoli site. Serving as the foundation for a flexible, modular compounding hub, the asset will process various high-performance materials like Ryton PPS, KetaSpire PEEK, Amodel PPA, and Ixef PARA. This addition allows Syensqo to scale and modify its aromatic polymers production efficiently as market needs shift.
The investment strengthens Syensqo’s supply capabilities in India, serving local and global automotive manufacturers and suppliers while also addressing opportunities in other industries. It also aligns with the broader localization of manufacturing and supply chains encouraged by the Government of India’s Make in India initiative.
Syensqo’s aromatic polymers are used in demanding automotive applications where high-temperature and chemical resistance, mechanical performance and lightweighting are critical.
“India is an important growth market for high-performance polymers, particularly as the automotive industry continues to localize and adopt more advanced material solutions. By bringing compounding capacity closer to our customers, we can respond more quickly and efficiently to their evolving needs while offering greater flexibility across our aromatics portfolio,” Tom Wood, VP Product and Asset Manager at Syensqo.
The investment builds on Syensqo’s established manufacturing and Research & Innovation presence in India and reinforces the company’s commitment to supporting market and customer growth across Asia Pacific.

BASF modernises acid chloride and chloroformate plant in Ludwigshafen, boosting capacity and cutting carbon footprint 
BASF has officially inaugurated a fully modernised production plant for acid chlorides and chloroformates at its Ludwigshafen site. The investment increases production capacity by around 30 % and reduces the product carbon footprint by an average of 19 %, with applications spanning coatings, pharmaceuticals, and crop protection. 
3 September 2026 
BASF 
Expansion 
Investment 
Save in bookmarks 
he modernized plant for acid chlorides and chloroformates (ACCF) at BASF’s Ludwigshafen site. The investment, amounting to a low three-digit million-euro sum, increases production capacity by around 30 %. 
Source: BASF 
Advertisement:
BASF has officially inaugurated its fully modernised plant for the production of acid chlorides and chloroformates at its Ludwigshafen Verbund site in Germany. The investment, amounting to a low three-digit million-euro sum, represents a significant upgrade of the production infrastructure and increases capacity at the site by approximately 30 %. BASF states it is one of the world’s leading manufacturers of these products, with production facilities in Ludwigshafen and Yeosu, South Korea. 
The modernised plant is designed to combine increased production capacity with improved sustainability performance and long-term supply reliability for customers worldwide. Since 2025, BASF has produced its entire Ludwigshafen portfolio of around 25 acid chlorides and chloroformates using renewable electricity credits, covering all upstream raw material processes. This transition has reduced the portfolio’s product carbon footprint by an average of 19 %, without changes to product specifications, certifications, or ordering processes. 
Coatings among key application areas for expanded production 
Acid chlorides and chloroformates serve as essential chemical building blocks across a wide range of value chains. Customers use them in applications including pharmaceuticals, crop protection products, organic peroxides, coatings, plastics, and rubber mixtures. The expanded capacity is intended to help BASF meet growing global demand whilst ensuring reliable supply of these intermediates. 
Mary Kurian, Member of the Board of Executive Directors of BASF SE, commented on the inauguration: “The opening of this modernized plant demonstrates BASF’s commitment to investing in competitive and sustainable production assets at our Ludwigshafen Verbund site and in Europe. By combining increased capacity, supply reliability and a significantly reduced product carbon footprint, we are creating value for our customers and supporting their green transformation.” 
Sustainability strategy and Scope 3 emission reductions 
The use of renewable electricity credits supports customers in advancing their Scope 3 emission-reduction efforts, a factor of increasing relevance across the coatings and chemicals supply chain. BASF emphasises that the transition requires no adjustments to product specifications, certifications, or ordering processes on the part of customers. 
Ketan Joshi, President of BASF’s Intermediates division, added: “This investment strengthens our position as one of the world’s leading suppliers of acid chlorides and chloroformates and supports our vision of being the preferred partner for sustainable intermediates. The modernized plant further supports our ability to provide reliable supply and consistent quality to customers around the world who depend on these essential intermediates.”

content_text:
EVG's NILPhotonics Competence Center. (Photo: EVG) 
EV Group (EVG) said on Sept. 2 it is accelerating customers' mass production of co-packaged optics (CPO) through its technology and infrastructure.
"CPO requires comprehensive process expertise because it integrates photonic and electronic components using advanced packaging technologies," said Bernd Dielacher, director of business development at EVG. "With decades of accumulated expertise and close collaboration, EVG is helping customers develop and optimize the entire manufacturing process from early CPO development through high-volume manufacturing (HVM)." CPO has recently drawn attention for large-scale data centers, AI infrastructure and high-performance computing (HPC).
EVG has several bonding technologies for CPO as well as nanoimprint lithography (NIL). Its fusion bonding technology bonds surfaces using dielectric materials alone and is used for heterogeneous integration of next-generation optical modulation materials such as thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) and barium titanate (BTO). It can also heterogeneously integrate light-emitting III-V compound semiconductors to create laser sources.
Hybrid bonding is an advanced packaging technology that directly connects copper (Cu) surfaces when stacking and interconnecting two semiconductor chips, or dies. It can minimize parasitic effects between photonic integrated circuits (PICs) and electronic integrated circuits (EICs) while enabling high-density integration. Parasitic effects interfere with signal flow at bonding interfaces and cause transmission losses. The technology is suited for high-bandwidth products.
EVG also has oxide-free room-temperature bonding technology. It enables low-loss, optically transparent interfaces and integrates heat-spreader materials such as diamond and silicon carbide (SiC) to efficiently transfer heat through interfaces.
NIL is a manufacturing technology capable of precisely producing nanoscale optical devices or circuit patterns in high volumes. It directly transfers circuit patterns by pressing a mold, or stamp, containing a specific semiconductor circuit pattern onto a substrate. The process is simpler and less expensive than deep ultraviolet (DUV) and extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography. Lithography equipment typically uses a light source and photomask to create fine circuit patterns.
NIL is useful for manufacturing CPO grating couplers, vertical light and beam-shaping components, and lenses and components for micro light-emitting diode (LED) packaging. Grating couplers are fine-patterned structures that help light efficiently enter and exit between chips or between a chip and an optical fiber.
EVG's NILPhotonics Competence Center is a process development platform that works with customers to enable faster and easier adoption of NIL technology for CPO development. It provides consulting across CPO processes as well as technology and equipment solutions. In particular, it provides contract manufacturing of large-area step-and-repeat (S&R) master stamps required for NIL processes and replicated stamps used for actual printing. Their availability in high volumes at low cost makes it easier to scale up production.
EVG also operates a Heterogeneous Integration Competence Center. Customers can test EVG equipment and receive services to optimize next-generation processes. The center supports areas requiring more advanced system integration, including HPC, data centers and CPO.
EVG expects the industry to shift from CPO toward optical input/output (I/O) chiplet architectures and advanced 3D photonic-electronic integration (EI). CPO horizontally places PICs, light sources, micro-optical structures and computing chips on a single package substrate. Optical I/O chiplet architectures combine optical interconnect functions as modules. Advanced 3D photonic-EI vertically stacks PICs and EICs.
"With our semiconductor 3D and heterogeneous integration technologies and capabilities, we can support not only CPO implementation but also optical I/O architectures," EVG said. "We will expand semiconductor packaging technology into next-generation photonic-EI systems."

GeoCue Elevates Survey-Grade Drone Mapping with Ouster's BABA-Compliant Native Color Rev8 Digital Lidar
Provided by Business Wire Sep 2, 2026, 4:00:00 PM 
GeoCue Elevates Survey-Grade Drone Mapping with Ouster's BABA-Compliant Native Color Rev8 Digital Lidar 
Pairing survey-grade precision with Ouster’s 256-channel Rev8 OS1 Max lidar, GeoCue’s latest TrueView lineup sets a new benchmark for U.S. drone surveying 
Ouster, Inc. (Nasdaq: OUST) (“Ouster” or the “Company”), a leader in sensing and perception for Physical AI, announced a strategic partnership with GeoCue, a premier provider of drone mapping payloads and software, to integrate Ouster’s native color Rev8 OS1 Max digital lidar into GeoCue’s TrueView product line. The collaboration pairs GeoCue's TrueView 1 payloads and LP360 software with Ouster's digital lidar to deliver survey-grade data to the utility and infrastructure industries.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260902576177/en/ 
Ouster Rev8 OS1 Max on GeoCue's TrueView drone payload, mapping a construction site (product rendering).
GeoCue is expanding its TrueView lineup to include options featuring the Ouster Rev8 OS1 Max, which is Build America, Buy America Act (BABA)-compliant. These new options give customers who have domestic production requirements a high-performance solution without technical compromises.
Ouster and GeoCue selected the Rev8 OS1 Max after joint flight testing and firmware tuning in Huntsville, Alabama. "We are moving America's drone surveying onto American sensing by pairing our TrueView payloads with Ouster's Rev8 OS1 Max," said Frank Darmayan, CEO of GeoCue. "This transition allows us to offer our customers a compliant, high-performance solution that delivers the survey-grade data they depend on for critical infrastructure monitoring and large-scale mapping projects."
The Rev8 OS1 Max brings four key advantages to GeoCue's utility and infrastructure customers:
Superior Precision: A smaller spot size and tighter beam allow TrueView payloads to resolve thin objects such as power lines and structural edges.
Expanded Operational Range: Longer range (200m at 10% reflectivity) clears altitude restrictions around utility corridors, letting operators fly higher while maintaining data quality.
Native Color Integration: The Rev8 OS1 Max captures native color in addition to 3D lidar data, so every point arrives inherently aligned to its color. Alongside the dual cameras in every TrueView payload, that gives LP360 an additional RGB reference for registering camera imagery to the point cloud, enabling tighter sensor fusion.
Density at Speed: 256 channels in 2K and 4K modes keep point density high even at fast flight speeds, supporting long-corridor surveys by propeller and fixed-wing aircraft.
"Our partnership with GeoCue is a testament to how native color digital lidar can serve as the bedrock for physical AI applications that have a profound impact on infrastructure and public safety," said Ouster CEO Angus Pacala. "By integrating our Rev8 OS1 Max sensor, we are providing the survey-grade precision and reliability required to empower the next generation of drone mapping professionals."
Experience the Rev8 OS1 Max for Drone Surveying at Commercial UAV Expo 
Ouster will be showcasing its Rev8 OS1 Max native color digital lidar at Booth #1653 during the Commercial UAV Expo in Las Vegas (September 1-3, 2026). Attendees can stop by the booth for live hardware demonstrations or schedule a meeting with our technical team.
About Ouster 
Ouster (Nasdaq: OUST) is a leader in sensing and perception for Physical AI across industrial, robotics, automotive, and smart infrastructure. With a unified platform of high-performance digital lidar, cameras, AI compute, sensor fusion and perception software, and AI models, Ouster delivers solutions that improve quality of life in the physical world. Headquartered in San Francisco, CA, Ouster has a global presence serving thousands of customers with offices in the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. For more information about our products, visit www.ouster.com , contact our sales team , or connect with us on X or LinkedIn .
About GeoCue 
GeoCue brings geospatial professionals advanced drone, mobile and terrestrial surveying equipment, point-cloud processing software, workflows, training and support for high-accuracy LiDAR and imagery mapping. With TrueView LiDAR and imaging sensors and LP360 point-cloud processing software, GeoCue provides complete solutions for successful data collection, processing, quality control and deliverable creation. GeoCue meets customers where they are in terms of technology, adoption, budget and resources while supporting their continued growth. To learn more about GeoCue, visit www.geocue.com .

The current state of Hybrid Bonding in 2026 — TSMC sits at 6 microns and the HBM delay that nobody expected
MEMBER EXCLUSIVE
Features
By
Luke James 
Published
2 September 2026
Copper-to-copper stacking is in volume on logic, but the memory payday has slipped to the end of the decade.
(Image credit: Getty Images / Bloomberg)

Hybrid bonding, the copper-to-copper joining technique that replaces solder microbumps in 3D chip stacks, is in high-volume production on logic chips and has just been postponed for use with memory. TSMC has scaled its SoIC bond pitch from 9 microns to 6 and laid out a path to 4.5 by 2029; Intel began shipping Foveros Direct hybrid bonding in its Clearwater Forest server CPU in the first half of 2026, and AMD has used the technology in volume since the first 3D V-Cache parts. However, a JEDEC decision earlier this year to raise the HBM stack-height limit lets HBM4 stay on the less sophisticated and expense microbump technology, deferring hybrid bonding's arrival in high-bandwidth memory, and is now set to debut in HBM4E and HBM5 at the end of the decade.
The technique works by polishing two dies flat, then bonding their copper pads and surrounding dielectric directly under heat and pressure, with no solder bump in between. Because there’s no bump to collapse, the connections can be packed far tighter. AMD has cited roughly 15 times the interconnect density of conventional 2.5D microbump stacking, and figures presented at TSMC's 2026 technology symposium put face-to-face hybrid bonding at around 14,000 signals per square millimeter against roughly 1,500 for face-to-back through-silicon-via stacking.
Wafer-to-wafer, die-to-wafer, and throughput
Microbumps have historically run at pitches around 40 microns, tightening toward 10 for the latest memory. Hybrid bonding, however, starts where microbumps end and keeps scaling: the leading edge is at 6 microns now, with 4.5- and 3-micron generations in development and sub-micron pitches demonstrated in research. Each step down multiplies the number of vertical connections between stacked dies, allowing a cache die or a compute tile to behave as if it were part of the chip rather than a separate component wired across a package.
Latest Videos From Tom's Hardware 
Watch full video here: 
The method is split into two different approaches: wafer-to-wafer and die-to-wafer. Wafer-to-wafer bonding joins two full patterned wafers face-to-face and dices them afterward, which allows the tightest pitch and fastest production because alignment happens once at the wafer scale. Imec and EV Group demonstrated a 200-nanometer wafer-to-wafer pitch with post-bond overlay below 40 nanometers at ECTC in May. The constraint here is that both wafers must carry identically sized dies, and every die gets bonded, including defective ones, so a single bad die on either wafer ruins the pair.
In contrast, die-to-wafer bonding places individual, pre-tested dies onto a wafer — which is what chiplet and HBM stacks require — because it allows known-good-die selection and the mixing of different die sizes and process nodes. There’s a penalty in terms of throughput with die-to-wafer as each die is picked, aligned, and placed in sequence rather than in one wafer-scale step.
The best die-to-wafer pitch shown at ECTC 2026, from CEA-Leti, was 1 micron, roughly five times looser than the wafer-to-wafer record. Because the dies are placed one at a time, the speed the bonder runs at sets the limit on how many chips it can produce. Applied Materials and Besi cite around 1,600 die placements per hour on the Kinex platform, and Besi's Chameo bonders are rated near 2,000 chips per hour, with the next generation aiming for 50-nanometer placement accuracy to reach finer pitches.
Hybrid bonding is difficult to achieve, as two surfaces have to be almost perfectly flat and clean. The dielectric holds on contact through van der Waals forces, so the polished surface can vary by no more than around 0.2 nanometers, and the copper pads have to sit a few nanometers below it, close enough that they swell into contact when the stack is heated to 200 to 300℃. A single particle smaller than a micron holds the surfaces apart and leaves a gap spanning many pads at once. So keeping the wafer clean and flat through the polishing step (known as chemical-mechanical planarization) is critical for good yields.
TSMC SoIC and Intel Foveros Direct
(Image credit: TSMC) In terms of who’s leading hybrid bonding, TSMC’s System on Integrated Chips (SoIC) platform leads in terms of volume. At its 2026 North American Technology Symposium, the company laid out a pitch roadmap moving from 9 microns in 2023 to 6 microns in 2025 and 4.5 microns by 2029, with second-gen SoIC adding face-to-face bonding on top of the face-to-back stacking that the first generation supported. The node-stacking roadmap runs in parallel, from N3P-on-N4 today toward N2P-on-N2P by 2028 and A14-on-A14 by 2029.
With SoIC, the hybrid-bonded stack is built first as a vertical block, then placed into a CoWoS module alongside HBM on a silicon interposer, a combination the industry calls 3.5D. AMD's MI300 is the reference case, stacking compute and I/O dies by hybrid bonding before the assembly is mounted in CoWoS with its memory. SoIC handles the front-end vertical density; CoWoS handles the back-end lateral integration with memory.
Capacity is slowly growing, with TSMC building out its Chiayi AP7 site as its largest advanced-packaging campus. Output is targeted for 2026, and analysts at TrendForce have estimated SoIC capacity roughly doubling year on year from a few thousand wafers a month in 2024. Customers include AMD, whose 3D V-Cache and MI300 accelerators were the first volume SoIC products, and the Broadcom-built Fujitsu Monaka CPU.
Meanwhile, Intel's hybrid-bonding implementation, Foveros Direct, reached high volume with Clearwater Forest, the Xeon 6+ server processor built on the 18A node and demo’d at MWC back in March. The design uses a 9-micron copper-to-copper pitch to bond compute and I/O tiles onto base tiles that act as an active interposer, and Intel has described a second generation targeting a 3-micron pitch. Enabling that on a leading-edge logic node required a dedicated process variant, 18A-PT , which adds the through-silicon vias (TSVs) and bonding support that standard 18A doesn’t carry. The shift from Intel's earlier Foveros, which used solder microbumps across the Ponte Vecchio GPU's chiplets, to direct copper bonding is a generational change now playing out across its server offerings.
The unexpected HBM delay
(Image credit: Getty Images / Bloomberg) The widely held assumption was that HBM, the stacked DRAM that sits beside every AI accelerator, would be hybrid bonding's largest market by volume. That changed back in January when JEDEC raised the HBM package height limit from 720 to 775 microns, and the extra room means 16-high HBM4 stacks can be assembled with microbumps after all. With HBM4 pad pitch at 10 microns, reporting from SemiEngineering noted that moving to hybrid bonding at that pitch wouldn’t yet make economic sense.
SK hynix has reflected that logic in its own planning, reportedly sticking with advanced mass-reflow molded underfill for 16-high HBM4 while keeping hybrid bonding as a backup and continuing to validate 12-high hybrid-bonded samples for later generations. The company demonstrated a 16-layer HBM4 sample at CES 2026, built without the all-hybrid bonding many expected the generation to require. The result pushes hybrid bonding's HBM debut toward HBM4E and HBM5, expected around 2027 to the end of the decade, where taller stacks and tighter pitches finally make the older bonding methods run out of room.
Meanwhile, the memory makers are building the packaging capacity regardless. SK hynix is investing $3.87 billion in an advanced-packaging plant in Indiana, with production targeted for 2028, and Micron broke ground on a $7 billion HBM advanced-packaging facility in Singapore early last year, with output expected around 2027. Those plants are sized for the volumes hybrid bonding will eventually carry, even as the first HBM4 generation ships on the older interconnect, meaning the equipment commitments are running ahead of the technology's confirmed deployment date in memory.
Samsung is doing the same thing from the memory side. Its SAINT packaging family includes SAINT-D, which stacks DRAM directly on a logic die, and the company has discussed a bufferless HBM4 design that removes the separate base die, with custom HBM logic dies reportedly moving to its 2nm foundry process for 2027 samples. At GTC in March, Samsung claimed hybrid bonding cuts thermal resistance by more than 20% against thermocompression bonding.
Another drag on the timeline is intellectual property. Adeia, which holds a large portfolio of bonding patents, sued AMD last year, alleging that the hybrid bonding behind 3D V-Cache infringes 10 of its patents.
China is pursuing the technique as a way around its lack of access to cutting-edge lithography. With SMIC limited to 14nm-class production and cut off from next-gen EUV, domestic researchers have identified 3D hybrid bonding as a route to competitive performance by stacking older logic and DRAM, with public claims of 14nm parts paired with domestic DRAM aimed at rivaling far newer GPUs. Given that it’s China we’re talking about here, those claims remain claims, and no foundry has demonstrated mass production of hybrid-bonded logic memory in China.
A scramble for tools
In terms of tooling, Applied Materials and Besi, partners on hybrid-bonding equipment since 2020, launched their Kinex die-to-wafer bonding system late last year, billed as the first fully integrated die-to-wafer hybrid bonder combining surface preparation, bonding, and metrology. Applied Materials has taken an equity stake in Besi, and reports from March placed Besi at the center of takeover interest from both Lam Research and Applied Materials, an indication of how important the bonding-tool market has become as logic adoption ramps and memory adoption is staged behind it.
Analyst tracking put Besi’s hybrid-bonding revenue on a path toward roughly €476 million by 2026, up from about €36 million in 2023, with second-half 2025 orders rising more than 60% against the first half on early HBM4 production-line bookings. Competing tool vendors are moving in alongside it: ASMPT has partnered with EV Group on hybrid bonding, and SK hynix is working with Hanwha Semitech on bonders targeting a commercial HBM launch in 2027. The sheer scale of this equipment build-out is a clear demonstration that the industry is treating hybrid bonding as an inevitability, even where the products that’ll use it are still years out.
Hybrid bonding is already in volume production, but its capability is outpacing its adoption. TSMC offers 6-micron pitch while its newest disclosed customer ships at 9; Intel ships at 9 with 3 on the roadmap; and the memory market that was meant to consume it in quantity has bought itself one more generation on microbumps. Two things will show where it goes next — whether any leading logic product drops below 9 microns in volume, and whether HBM4E marks hybrid bonding's first real use in memory before the end of the decade.
